confirmed.title: README cheat sheet shows `pm undo --last [N]` but --last requires a value
confirmed.summary: undoP defines --last as `option auto (long "last" <> value 1)`, so the flag only exists with an argument; the bracketed `[N]` in README (and DESIGN.md §5 `pm undo --last [n]`) advertises an optional argument that optparse-applicative rejects.
confirmed.failure_scenario: User types `pm undo --last` as the cheat sheet suggests → optparse error "The option `--last` expects an argument" exit 1. The DocDriftTests sentinel only checks that the substring `pm undo --last` is present, so it does not catch this. || A user follows the README literally and runs `pm undo --last` expecting the default of 1. pm prints a parser error and exits 1; no reverse plan is generated. The correct invocations are `pm undo` or `pm undo --last 1`, which the docs do not show.
confirmed.evidence: Main.hs:415-419 undoP: `option auto (long "last" <> metavar "N" <> value 1 ...)`; README.md:227 `pm undo --last [N]`; README.zh.md:173; docs/DESIGN.md:256 `pm undo --last [n]`; test/DocDriftTests.hs:333 only asserts `"pm undo --last" `isInfixOf` s`.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: app/Main.hs:415-419 `undoP = CmdUndo <$> option auto (long "last" <> metavar "N" <> value 1 <> help ...)`. In optparse-applicative `option` builds an OptReader that always consumes exactly one argument; `value 1` is only the default used when the option is entirely absent from argv. There is no `optional`/flag-with-optional-argument form, so `--last` followed by nothing (or by `--backup`) is a parse error. The parser is the only consumer of the flag (grep of src/, gui/, scripts/ shows no other `--last` producer). REPRO: root initialised, one Done op in .pm/journal.ndjson; user copies the README.md:227 cheat-sheet line `pm undo --last [N]` and, reading `[N]` as optional (the same bracket convention the README uses on lines 211 `[--json]`, 220 `[list]`, 223 `[--unskip]`), runs `pm undo --last`. optparse-applicative reports `The option `--last` expects an argument` + usage and exits 1 before `run (CmdUndo …)` (Main.hs:119) is reached; no reverse plan is generated. `pm undo` or `pm undo --last 1` work. DESIGN: docs/DESIGN.md:256 repeats the same wrong shape `pm undo --last [n]`; README.zh.md:173 likewise. docs/REVIEW-LOG-4.md:421-424 (round 41 #7) explicitly ruled that the README undo summary must be the 'real CLI form', and DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:522 says the README summary was changed to be '与 --help 同形' — but optparse's own --help would render `[--last N]`, not `--last [N]`, so the docs contradict their own stated contract rather than documenting this as intended. The sentinel test/DocDriftTests.hs:333 only asserts `"pm undo --last" `isInfixOf` s`, which the wrong form satisfies, so the test does not pin the current text as correct. Nothing in README 465-553 lists it as a known limitation. Severity low: the only consequence is a clear parser error and a retry; no data risk.
verdict.corrected_summary: README.md:227, README.zh.md:173 and docs/DESIGN.md:256 write the undo invocation as `pm undo --last [N]`, using the docs' own bracket-means-optional convention, which implies `--last` may be given without a value. The parser (app/Main.hs:417, `option auto … value 1`) only defaults N when `--last` is absent altogether; `pm undo --last` alone is rejected by optparse-applicative with `The option `--last` expects an argument` (exit 1). The correct shape, and what `pm undo --help` prints, is `pm undo [--last N]`. The DocDriftTests sentinel (test/DocDriftTests.hs:333) checks only for the substring `pm undo --last`, so it does not catch the misplaced bracket even though REVIEW-LOG-4 round 41 #7 required the README summary to be the real CLI form.
verdict.suggested_fix: Change the three doc lines to `pm undo [--last N]` (DESIGN.md: `pm undo [--last n]`), and update the sentinel in test/DocDriftTests.hs:333 to assert the corrected substring (e.g. `"pm undo [--last N]" `isInfixOf` s`, keeping the existing `pm undo <planId>` negative check) so the drift cannot regress. No code change needed.

confirmed.title: pm init --workers accepts any Int (0, negative, >64) while pm config set enforces 1..64; checkConfig does not cover workers
confirmed.summary: checkPatch (config set / POST /api/config) rejects workers outside 1..64, but initP takes `option auto` with no bounds and runInit writes cfgWorkers straight into config after checkConfig, which never inspects workers. The two write paths that the docs describe as sharing one validation sink therefore accept different value domains; a hand-edited or init-written `workers = 0`/`-5`/`1000` is loaded without complaint.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `pm init --main D:\Photography --workers 0` → exit 0, config.toml has `workers = 0`; `pm config` prints "并发数 0"; `pm scan` silently runs with max 1 0 = 1 worker; later `pm config set --workers 0` is refused with "并发数 0 越界（1..64）" although init just accepted it. With `--workers 100000` scanRoot spawns 100000 hashing threads (replicateConcurrently_ has no cap).
confirmed.evidence: Main.hs:265-270 initP: `optional (option auto (long "workers" ...))` with no reader validation; Commands.hs:167-175 runInit: `cfgWorkers = ioWorkers o` then `errs <- checkConfig newCfg`; ConfigEdit.hs:57-80 checkConfig checks only absolute paths, nesting, backup pairing; ConfigEdit.hs:159-161 checkPatch: `Just (Just w) | w < 1 || w > 64 -> [...]`; Scan.hs:340 `replicateConcurrently_ (max 1 (soWorkers opts)) worker`.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: app/Main.hs:269 `initP` parses `--workers` with `optional (option auto ...)` and help text "hash 并行度（默认=物理核数）" — no range in the reader or the help. By contrast app/Main.hs:239 (`config set --workers`) advertises "扫描并发数（1..64）" and src/Pm/ConfigEdit.hs:159-160 `checkPatch` enforces it: `Just (Just w) | w < 1 || w > 64 -> ["并发数 " <> show w <> " 越界（1..64）"]`. src/Pm/Commands.hs:177 `runInit` builds `newCfg` with `cfgWorkers = ioWorkers o` and at :200 runs only `errs <- checkConfig newCfg`; ConfigEdit.hs:57-80 `checkConfig` computes `absErr` (checkAbsolute), vault/main nesting, backup id/subpath pairing and backup nesting — `cfgWorkers` is never inspected. src/Pm/Config.hs:126 decodes `[main] workers` via `TOML.getFieldsOpt` with no bound either, so a hand-edited value is loaded verbatim. Consumers: Commands.hs:250 `workers = fromMaybe (fromMaybe defWorkers (cfgWorkers cfg)) (scWorkers sc)`; Scan.hs:340 `replicateConcurrently_ (max 1 (soWorkers opts)) worker` — 0/negative are clamped to 1 (no crash, no div-by-zero), oversized values spawn that many green threads draining one shared IORef queue (bounded in practice by the number of files to hash; no crash). Backup ignores cfgWorkers entirely (BackupCmd.hs:225 `fromMaybe 1 mworkers`). REPRO: `pm init --main D:\Photography --workers 0` → initP yields `ioWorkers = Just 0`; runInit: config absent, no orphan .tmp, vaultOk = Nothing, `checkConfig newCfg` returns [] (main path absolute, no vault, no backup pair) → `writeConfig` renders `workers = 0` (Config.hs:255) → exit 0. `pm config` prints "并发数    0" (ConfigEdit.hs:243). `pm scan` runs with `max 1 0 = 1` worker and prints "workers=0" in the progress banner (Scan.hs:283-290 prints raw `soWorkers`). Later `pm config set --workers 0` → checkPatch → "并发数 0 越界（1..64）" exit 2. So the same value is accepted by one write path and refused by another, exactly as the finder claims. DESIGN: docs/REVIEW-LOG-4.md:242-250 (cluster G6, C101/F011) established that init / config set / POST config / backup init must share the `checkConfig` sink — but scopes it to cross-field invariants (paths absolute, nesting, backup pairing); the 1..64 range was left as a per-field check inside `checkPatch`, which init never calls. docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:497 says `pm init --force` runs "整份新配置过 checkConfig 汇点". No doc, README, or review round states that init is meant to accept arbitrary worker counts, and nothing rules the drift as intended; test/ServeWriteTests.hs:277-279 pins only the API side (0 and 999 rejected). The GUI/README (README.md:229) direct users to `config set` which advertises 1..64. Impact is benign (clamp to 1, or many green threads), so this is a real but low-severity validation/help-text drift, not a crash or data-safety issue; `pm scan --workers` (Main.hs:274) and `pm backup --workers` (Main.hs:341) are likewise unbounded per-run flags, which suggests the 1..64 gate was only ever intended for the persisted setting — which makes init (the other persisting path) the inconsistent one.
verdict.corrected_summary: `pm init --workers N` persists any Int (0, negative, >64) into config.toml because initP has no reader bound and runInit validates only via checkConfig, which never inspects cfgWorkers; the same value is refused by `pm config set --workers` / POST /api/config via checkPatch's 1..64 gate. Consequence is a confusing inconsistency (init accepts, config set later refuses; `pm config` shows 0; scan banner prints workers=0 while actually running 1 thread via `max 1`), not a crash or data-safety violation. Hand-edited config is also loaded without a range check (Config.hs:126).
verdict.suggested_fix: Move the range check into the shared sink: in ConfigEdit.checkConfig add `["并发数 " <> show w <> " 越界（1..64）" | Just w <- [cfgWorkers c], w < 1 || w > 64]` (and drop or keep the duplicate in checkPatch since checkPatch already calls checkConfig (applyPatch c p)); update initP's `--workers` help to "hash 并行度（1..64；默认=物理核数）". Optionally pin with a test that `runInit` with workers 0 / 65 exits 2.

confirmed.title: Packaged pm-ui.exe exits silently (no window, no message) when `pm serve` fails to announce
confirmed.summary: spawn_serve() errors (config missing/unreadable → serve prints an error line instead of the announce JSON; pm.exe not found; bind failure) are reported only via eprintln! followed by process::exit(2). main.rs sets `windows_subsystem = "windows"` for release, so the process has no console: stderr is discarded, no Tauri window is ever built, and the app just vanishes. The `pm ui` path is no better: Pm/Ui.hs maps the child's exit code 2 straight through without printing anything.
confirmed.failure_scenario: 用户从 Start 菜单启动 pm-ui 但还没跑过 pm init（无 config.toml）：pm-ui 启动 `pm.exe serve --exit-on-stdin-eof --writable --allow-apply` → withCfg 走 `Left e -> putStrLn e >> pure 2`，首行是中文错误文本 → lib.rs:89 serde_json::from_str 失败 → eprintln!（无 stderr，丢弃）→ exit(2)。用户看到的只是「双击没反应」。 || Fresh NSIS install, user clicks the Start-menu entry before running `pm init`. lib.rs read_line() gets the Chinese error text, serde_json::from_str fails → Err → run() hits `Err(e) => { eprintln!("pm-ui: {e}"); std::process::exit(2); }`. With windows_subsystem="windows" there is no console; nothing is shown. Same silent outcome for `PM_EXE` pointing at a stale path; via `pm ui` the terminal just returns exit 2 with no line.
confirmed.evidence: lib.rs:105-111 `let (info, child) = match spawn_serve() { Ok(x) => x, Err(e) => { eprintln!("pm-ui: {e}"); std::process::exit(2); } };`；main.rs:2 `#![cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), windows_subsystem = "windows")]`；lib.rs:74 `.stderr(Stdio::inherit())`；lib.rs:84-90 只读一行 stdout 并要求是 JSON。src/Pm/Commands.hs:87-91 withCfg：`Left e -> putStrLn e >> pure 2`。src/Pm/Ui.hs:44-48 no message for a non-zero child exit. README.md:137-139 'Start the GUI from the Start Menu or with `pm ui`'.

verdict.reasoning:
CODE. gui/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:105-111 is exactly as quoted: `Err(e) => { eprintln!("pm-ui: {e}"); std::process::exit(2); }` before any Tauri window is built; main.rs:2 sets `windows_subsystem = "windows"` for release. spawn_serve (lib.rs:72-74) pipes stdout, inherits stderr, reads one line (86-88) and requires JSON (89-90). On the Haskell side app/Main.hs:165 `run (CmdServe o) = withCfg (\cfg -> runServe cfg o)` and src/Pm/Commands.hs:87-90 `Left e -> putStrLn e >> pure 2`: a missing config prints `配置不存在: <fp> —— 先运行 pm init --main <主库路径>` (Config.hs:188) to STDOUT (the piped side), never the announce JSON. Likewise a bind failure in runServe (Serve.hs:167) is `putStrLn ("pm serve: " <> show e)` on stdout. Both therefore reach lib.rs:89 as a non-JSON first line → Err → eprintln → exit(2).

However the finder's `pm ui` half is wrong on two counts: (a) app/Main.hs:166-167 `-- 先过 withCfg：配置缺失时在这里报清楚，而不是让 GUI 里的 serve 静默失败 / run CmdUi = withCfg (const runUi)` — `pm ui` loads the config itself first and prints the error on the terminal, so pm-ui is never spawned in the missing-config case (docs/reviews/2026-08-24-p3b-codex-review-2.md:324 checked this: `withCfg 先行合理`); (b) src/Pm/Ui.hs:42-44 launches pm-ui with `createProcess (proc exe [])` (std handles = Inherit), and the GHC process library always passes the parent's handles via STARTF_USESTDHANDLES, so pm-ui's `eprintln!` (and serve's inherited stderr) DO land on the terminal even though pm-ui is a GUI-subsystem binary; and PM_EXE is always set to pm's own `getExecutablePath` (Ui.hs:41-43), so a stale PM_EXE cannot arise via `pm ui`. "The terminal just returns exit 2 with no line" is refuted.

REPRO (the surviving path). Fresh NSIS install (README.md:131), user has not run `pm init`, clicks the Start-menu entry (README.md:138 documents this as a first-class launch). Explorer starts pm-ui.exe: GUI subsystem, no console, GetStdHandle(STD_ERROR_HANDLE) is NULL. pm_exe() (lib.rs:36-51): no PM_EXE, sibling `pm.exe` sidecar exists (tauri.conf.json:37 externalBin, DESIGN-GUI.md:214-217) → spawn `pm.exe serve --exit-on-stdin-eof --writable --allow-apply` with stdout piped (lib.rs:68-74). Main.hs:165 → withCfg → loadConfigState (Config.hs:173-188) → `CfgAbsent "配置不存在: …"` → Commands.hs:90 `putStrLn e >> pure 2`. lib.rs:87 read_line gets that Chinese line; lib.rs:89 `serde_json::from_str` fails → `Err("serve announce 不是 JSON：…")` → lib.rs:108 `eprintln!` — Rust's Windows stdio treats a NULL std handle as EBADF and silently drops the write — → lib.rs:109 `exit(2)`. No window, no dialog, no log; the user experiences "double-click does nothing". Same trace for a loopback bind failure (Serve.hs:167 prints to stdout → non-JSON) or a corrupt/unreadable config.toml (Config.hs:190-193 → Left).

DESIGN. README.md:138 ("Start the GUI from the Start Menu or with `pm ui`") and DESIGN-GUI.md:214-217 (the sibling-lookup exists precisely so a Start-menu launch works) make direct launch a supported path. README 465-553 known-limitations and REVIEW-LOG do not list a silent GUI exit; on the contrary the comment at Main.hs:166 explicitly names "让 GUI 里的 serve 静默失败" as the thing to avoid — but the mitigation only covers the `pm ui` route, not the Start-menu route that DESIGN-GUI itself says is the normal packaged-build entry. No test pins the behaviour. So the docs agree with the finder for the direct-launch case; not refuted. Severity is low: no data risk, it only bites when the documented order (pm init first, README quick start) is not followed or serve cannot bind, and the message is merely lost rather than wrong.
verdict.corrected_summary: When packaged pm-ui.exe is launched directly (Start menu / double-click) and `pm serve` fails to announce — most realistically because `pm init` has not been run yet (config missing/unreadable → withCfg prints the Chinese error on stdout instead of the JSON announce), or the loopback bind fails — lib.rs:105-111 only `eprintln!`s and `exit(2)`s before any window exists; with `windows_subsystem = "windows"` and no inherited console there is no stderr, so the app vanishes with no message. The `pm ui` half of the finding is wrong: Main.hs:166-167 gates `pm ui` behind withCfg (config errors are printed by pm itself before pm-ui starts), PM_EXE is always pm's own path, and pm-ui's stderr is inherited from the terminal via GHC createProcess, so `pm ui` does show the error line.
verdict.suggested_fix: In lib.rs run(), on the Err arm show the message before exiting, e.g. under `#[cfg(windows)]` call user32 `MessageBoxW(null, msg, "pm-ui", MB_OK | MB_ICONERROR)` via a small `extern "system"` declaration (or `rfd`/tauri-plugin-dialog), keeping the eprintln for the console case; optionally also forward the first stdout line verbatim so the user sees pm's own `先运行 pm init --main <主库路径>` hint. No Haskell-side change needed.

confirmed.title: GUI collapses 'catalog refused / unreadable' into '主库尚未索引 → pm scan' and drops the server's warnings (three-state → two-state)
confirmed.summary: `GET /api/status` encodes CatRefused as `index: null` plus a non-empty `warnings` list, and the CLI renderer distinguishes the two. The GUI status page and archive page test only `!s.index` / `!i`, print '主库尚未索引 … → pm scan', and `return` before the `s.warnings` loop, so the actual refusal reason is never shown and the user is told the library was simply never scanned.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `.pm/catalog.json` exists but loadCatalog returns CatRefused (e.g. 'catalog 身份不符', or requirePmTrusted rejects `.pm`). statusReport → `StatusReport root warns Nothing 2`. GUI loadStatus: `s.index` is null → banner '主库尚未索引：D:\Photography → 在终端运行 pm scan（首次全量约 10–25 分钟）' and returns at line 90; `for (const w of s.warnings)` at line 196 is never reached. archive.js:29 does the same. The user is steered to a 10–25 min rebuild without ever seeing why the index was refused.
confirmed.evidence: src/Pm/Status.hs:121-125 `(mcat, warns) <- catalogMaybe <$> loadCatalog root; case mcat of Nothing -> pure (StatusReport root warns Nothing 2)`; Status.hs:200-205 CLI distinguishes; Catalog.hs:104-108 comment '「尚未索引 → 先 pm scan」与「索引读不出（原因）」不能是同一句话'. gui/ui/app.js:88-91 `if (!s.index) { … return; }` (warnings loop at app.js:196 unreachable); gui/ui/archive.js:29.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Catalog.hs:63-92 — loadCatalog returns CatRefused [m] when requirePmTrusted fails, CatRefused ws for unreadable/hand-edited/three-generations-bad snapshots (classify (Nothing, ws)), and CatRefused [...] for missing root-id.json or identity mismatch; every CatRefused carries a non-empty reason list. src/Pm/Status.hs:124-126 `(mcat, warns) <- catalogMaybe <$> loadCatalog root; Nothing -> pure (StatusReport root warns Nothing 2)`; Status.hs:95-101 encodes it as {root, warnings, exit:2, index:null}. src/Pm/Serve.hs:219-221 returns that JSON verbatim. CLI renderer Status.hs:192-197 branches on `null (srWarnings r)` and prints '主库索引读不出（见上）… 排除原因后重试，或 pm scan 重建' otherwise. gui/ui/app.js:88-91 `if (!s.index) { banner '主库尚未索引：…→ 在终端运行 pm scan（首次全量约 10–25 分钟）'; $('#layer-cards').innerHTML=''; return; }` — the `for (const w of s.warnings)` loop at app.js:196 is only reachable after that return; s.exit is never read. gui/ui/archive.js:28-29 `if (!i) st.textContent = '主库尚未索引——先在终端 pm scan。'` likewise. REPRO: D:\Photography\.pm\catalog.json is a snapshot copied from another library (catRootId ≠ .pm/root-id.json id). GET /api/status → loadCatalog → CatLoaded → readRootInfo → riId ≠ catRootId → CatRefused ['catalog 身份不符：快照属于 root …——像是整目录拷贝/恢复错位，拒绝使用；确认后 pm scan 重建'] → statusReport → {index:null, warnings:[that], exit:2}. loadStatus: `!s.index` true → banner says 尚未索引 → pm scan, return. The refusal reason is never displayed; same on the 归档 page. `pm status` in a terminal would print the ⚠ line and '索引读不出（见上）'. DESIGN: DESIGN-GUI.md:33 says /api/status is the same StatusReport as pm status '含退出码' and :134 that the status page translates the exit-code semantics into actions; Catalog.hs:104-108 states '「尚未索引 → 先 pm scan」与「索引读不出（原因）」不能是同一句话'; the loadStatus vault catch at app.js:170-175 already applies the 三态 rule elsewhere in the same function. No REVIEW-LOG/README ruling says the GUI may collapse this. Severity low: it is a misleading message (pm scan is also one of the CLI's suggested remedies, and the trusted-path refusal would resurface in the terminal on scan), but the identity-mismatch signal is hidden and the user is steered to a full rebuild without seeing why.
verdict.corrected_summary: GUI status page (app.js:88-91) and archive page (archive.js:28-29) test only `!s.index` and print '主库尚未索引 → pm scan', returning before the `s.warnings` loop. For CatRefused (index:null + non-empty warnings + exit 2 — untrusted .pm, unreadable/hand-edited snapshot, missing root-id.json, catalog identity mismatch) the real reason is dropped and the user is told the library was never scanned; the CLI renderer distinguishes the two cases.
verdict.suggested_fix:
In loadStatus, when `!s.index`: if `s.warnings.length` show '主库索引读不出：<root>
' + warnings.join('
') + '
→ 排除原因后重试，或在终端 pm scan 重建' (banner class bad) instead of the 尚未索引 text; same branch in archive.js:29. Optionally still emit the warnings list before returning.

confirmed.title: Plans page: apply result with code 2 and no items is described as 'has unfinished/needs-decision items' and told to consider `pm undo`
confirmed.summary: applyPlan() renders any non-zero `code` as '执行结束（退出码 N）：<id>——有未完成/待裁决项，见逐项结果' and always appends '回滚：终端 pm undo。'. The server returns HTTP 200 with code 2 and items [] when nothing was executed at all (execPlanRetry Left → `sink e >> pure (2, [])`, e.g. root lock held), so the headline is false and the undo hint suggests there is something to roll back.
confirmed.failure_scenario: User runs `pm scan` in a terminal (holds .pm/lock) and clicks 「执行这个计划」 twice in the GUI. POST /api/apply → execPlanRetry returns Left '另一个 pm 正在写主库…' → response {code: 2, items: [], log: [...]}. Banner: '执行结束（退出码 2）：…——有未完成/待裁决项，见逐项结果\n…\n回滚：终端 pm undo。' The user may run `pm undo` (which would undo the previous, unrelated plan).
confirmed.evidence: app.js:378-386 `out.textContent = (j.code === 0 ? … : `执行结束（退出码 ${j.code}）：${j.planId}——有未完成/待裁决项，见逐项结果`) + … + "\n回滚：终端 pm undo。";`. Server: Cli.hs:150-152 `Left e -> sink e >> pure (2, [])` and Serve.hs apply handler returns status200 regardless of code.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Exec.hs:176 execPlan returns `Left "另一个 pm 实例正持有该 root 的锁（I10），稍后重试"` when hTryLock fails (also Left at 95/99/100/145/156/165 for identity/barrier/re-check refusals). src/Pm/Removable.hs:246-249 execPlanRetry passes `Right (Left e)` through as `Left e`. src/Pm/Cli.hs:150 `Left e -> sink e >> pure (2, [])`. src/Pm/Serve.hs:331-359: prepareApply does not take the root lock; executePlanNowWith result is returned with status200 and `code`, `items` (empty), `log` (contains the sink'd message). gui/ui/app.js:374-386: r.ok → counts empty → summary '' → `out.textContent = '执行结束（退出码 2）：<id>——有未完成/待裁决项，见逐项结果' + logTail + '\n回滚：终端 pm undo。'`. REPRO: terminal runs `pm scan` (holds .pm/lock); user arms and clicks 执行 in the GUI → POST /api/apply → execPlan Left at Exec.hs:176 → (2, []) → 200 {code:2, items:[], log:['另一个 pm 实例正持有该 root 的锁（I10），稍后重试']} → banner headline claims 未完成/待裁决项 and 见逐项结果 although nothing was executed and no per-item line is rendered; the lock message does appear in the log tail directly beneath. DESIGN: DESIGN-GUI.md:83 explicitly requires that the apply result '逐项结果与 log 从 JSON 响应体渲染，并指明 pm undo' — so the always-present undo hint is documented and must stay. `pm undo` only generates a reverse plan (DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:490, exit 1, not executed) which still needs a confirmed `pm apply` (I3), so the finder's rollback-of-a-previous-plan harm is heavily mitigated. What remains is a factually wrong headline for code 2 / items [] (executePlanNow' only yields code 2 with an empty item list, code 1 with items). Not refuted, but low: a wrong sentence with the real reason printed right below it.
