confirmed.title: Copy pending classification uses a boolean dst probe, so an unreadable/ACL-denied dst becomes 'C1 Info: no trace' with exit 0
confirmed.summary: classifyPending' for OpCopy probes the destination with doesFileExist, which returns False for ACL denial or media errors. The Intent-without-terminal is then classified as C1 Info and `pm doctor` exits 0. The three-state discipline (probeName/userSideExists) is applied to Rename but not to Copy.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A backup batch dies between the landing rename and the Done. The landed dst has an ACL that denies attribute reads. `pm doctor --backup` → doesFileExist → False → tmp probe Right False → 'C1 Info … 重跑原计划即可', exit 0. Rerunning cannot repair the missing Done (Exec sees a foreign file and reports conflict), and `--repair` never gets a C2 row.
confirmed.evidence: Doctor.hs:395-426: `OpCopy _ dstRel sha _ _ -> do … dstEx <- doesFileExist dstAbs; if dstEx then … else … Right False -> pure [Finding "C1" Info …]`. Contrast the Rename arm (Doctor.hs:455-459) `userSideExists` with comment at 445-451. runDoctor' 260-261 exit code. Quarantine arm (474) same collapse but conservative direction.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Doctor.hs:395-397: OpCopy _ dstRel sha _ _ -> do { let dstAbs = root </> dstRel; dstEx <- doesFileExist dstAbs; if dstEx then ... else ... }. The False branch goes to the tmp probe (probePmExists, three-state) and, with no tmp, to line 426 Finding 'C1' Info '...Intent 后无痕迹（写 tmp 前中断），重跑原计划即可'. The Rename arm (452-459) uses userSideExists = probeName three-state and emits PM-LINK Bad on ProbeUnknown; the comments at 445-451 (F033) explain exactly why a boolean probe is wrong there. The Quarantine arm's victimEx (474) has the same collapse but in the conservative direction. Library behaviour: System.Directory.doesFileExist wraps getFileMetadata in catchIOError (\_ -> return False); on Windows getFileMetadata opens the path with CreateFile(0 access, FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS) and any failure (ACCESS_DENIED, media error) becomes False. The project's own mutation record confirms this collapse empirically: REVIEW-LOG-4.md:312 (F041) 'root-id.json 被 ACL 全拒 -> 布尔探针塌 False', and test/TestUtil.hs:83-107 (withDenyAll via icacls /deny (F)) is the injection used. REPRO: journal ends with JIntent P#7 (OpCopy src 相册/a.jpg sha s) and no terminal (crash between the landing rename at Exec.hs ~535 and the Done at 568); dst root/相册/a.jpg exists with sha s but its DACL (or its directory's) now denies the user. pm doctor: doesFileExist -> CreateFile ACCESS_DENIED -> False; pendingTmp -> probePmExists PmEntryFile -> Right False (tmp was renamed away) -> Finding 'C1' Info; worst=Info -> exit 0 and the text tells the user nothing is on disk. Rerunning the plan under the same ACL: Exec.hs:458 doesFileExist also False -> writes tmp -> moveBoundNoReplace fails on the existing dst -> JFailed '落位失败' (line 540): the Intent is retired as FAILED and the actually-landed copy is never journaled Done (should have been C2 Warn + --repair Done, or PM-LINK Bad pending human check). No wrong write happens (C1 Info is outside the repair whitelist), so the harm is a false all-clear (exit 0) and wrong guidance. DESIGN: DESIGN.md:361 PM-LINK row states the three-state rule for Rename only; the CONTEXT fail-closed philosophy and REVIEW-LOG-4 R1 cluster ('布尔存在探针 False->安心继续') treat exactly this pattern as a defect class, and no doc or review round rules the Copy dst probe as an accepted boolean. Drive dropout specifically is covered by requireDrive at runDoctorWith (so not that case), but ACL denial is deterministic and passes through. Scenario is edge (ACL on a pm-landed file), severity low.
verdict.corrected_summary: classifyPending' probes a pending Copy's dst with boolean doesFileExist (Doctor.hs:397), which returns False on ACL denial (project-verified via F041/withDenyAll), so an Intent whose dst actually landed but is unreadable-by-attributes is classified 'C1 Info: Intent 后无痕迹' with exit 0 instead of a PM-LINK Bad (as the Rename arm does after F033). No repair is wrongly applied, but doctor gives a false all-clear and a rerun then retires the Intent as FAILED while the landed copy stays un-journaled.
verdict.suggested_fix: Replace `dstEx <- doesFileExist dstAbs` with `eDst <- userSideExists dstAbs` and add a `Left m -> pure [Finding "PM-LINK" Bad (oid <> ": " <> m <> "，不推导、不修复（需人工核查）") ""]` arm before the existing True/False branches (the True branch already falls back to 'C?' Bad when sha256File throws). Optionally do the same for victimEx in the Quarantine arm (line 474) for consistency.

confirmed.title: A pending Copy Intent can never retire once its dst is legitimately re-filled with different content by another plan: doctor then reports C5 Bad forever and --repair emits a quarantine plan for the legitimate file
confirmed.summary: pending = every oid whose last journal event is an Intent. Exec writes no journal record when a re-run hits an I5 conflict or a source-stat failure, so a Copy Intent left by a crash can only be retired by re-running the same item to Done or by --repair when dst matches. If the user re-exports the source and archives it through a new plan, classifyPending' classifies the stale oid as C5, exits 1 on every doctor run, and `--repair` generates a `doctor-c5-quarantine` plan whose victim is the correctly landed newer file.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Power loss during `pm import` right after Intent P1#7 → doctor: C1 Info. User re-edits a.jpg in Lightroom, runs `pm import` (P2) → 成片\E\a.jpg landed with sha2. Now every `pm doctor` prints `✗ [C5] P1#7: dst 存在但内容不符` (exit 1), and `pm doctor --repair` writes plan `doctor-c5-quarantine` targeting 成片\E\a.jpg; `pm apply P1` returns CONFLICT and journals nothing, so the row never goes away.
confirmed.evidence: src/Pm/Doctor.hs:126-141 opState/pending; :401-410 `Right dsha | dsha == sha -> C2 … | otherwise -> … Finding "C5" Bad …`; :715-738 applyRepairs c5 → savePlan of OpQuarantine. src/Pm/Exec.hs:457-469 `OConflict "目标已存在且内容不同（I5：不覆盖）"` before any jAppend; :450-452 `OFailed ("源 stat 失败…")`. docs/DESIGN.md:378 defines C5 as a step-7 tear only.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Doctor.hs:126-141 opState marks an oid pending iff its last journal event is a JIntent; 401-410 classify a pending OpCopy whose dst exists with a different sha as 'C5' Bad with repair text '--repair 将生成 dst 隔离计划'; 704-738 applyRepairs then savePlan's an OpQuarantine of dstRel with the file's current sha. Exec.hs:449-469: on rerun, `preE <- try (statSnap src)` failure -> OFailed with no jAppend; size/mtime mismatch -> OConflict, no jAppend; dst exists with different sha -> OConflict '目标已存在且内容不同（I5：不覆盖）' with no jAppend. The only JFailed/JDone writers for a Copy are after the Intent at 483 (lines 509-568), all inside the tmp-write path that is never reached once dst exists. grep confirms no other module writes JFailed (Doctor only writes JDone for C2/R2/Q-DONE-LOST; pm plan prune / resolve touch plan files only). REPRO: P1#7 = OpCopy staging/a.jpg -> 成片/E/a.jpg sha1; power loss right after JIntent P1#7 (before tmp) -> doctor: C1 Info. User re-exports a.jpg (sha2), runs pm import -> P2#0 OpCopy -> 成片/E/a.jpg landed, JIntent P2#0 + JDone P2#0. Now opState: P1#7 -> (op, True) still pending. classifyPending': dst exists, sha256 = sha2 ≠ sha1 -> Finding 'C5' Bad -> exit 1 on every run; --repair (also invoked automatically as the heal step in Pm.Cli.executePlanNowWith / execPlanRetry) writes a fresh doctor-c5-quarantine plan for 成片/E/a.jpg each time. pm apply P1: source stat now differs (size/mtime) -> OConflict at 455, or if it matched, dst-mismatch OConflict at 469 — no journal record either way, so the Intent never retires. DESIGN: DESIGN.md:359 defines C5 solely as the step-7 tear ('进程死在步 7 与步 8 之间'); the finder's state is reachable by a different, legitimate path that the doc does not consider, and no REVIEW-LOG entry or README limitation rules a permanently stuck Intent as accepted. Nothing is lost (the quarantine plan needs pm apply confirmation and is undoable), so severity low, but the report is persistently wrong and the suggested remedy targets the correct newer file.
verdict.corrected_summary: A Copy Intent left pending by a crash before any tmp write can never be retired if its dst is later legitimately landed with different content by another plan: Exec journals nothing on the I5 conflict / source-changed / source-stat-failed outcomes of a rerun, so opState keeps the oid pending, doctor reports it as C5 Bad (exit 1) on every run, and --repair (including the automatic heal pass in execPlanRetry) generates a doctor-c5-quarantine plan whose victim is the correctly landed newer file. Requires the user to abandon the crashed plan and re-plan the same dst; no data is lost without a further confirmed apply.
verdict.suggested_fix: Doctor-side, read-only: in classifyPending' for OpCopy, before emitting C5 check whether a later JDone exists for a different oid whose Intent is an OpCopy with the same foldPath dstRel and opSha == the current dst sha; if so emit an Info row (e.g. 'C5-SUPERSEDED: dst 已由 <oid2> 落位，旧 Intent 作废') that is outside the repair whitelist, and optionally let --repair append a JFailed for the stale oid so it retires. Alternatively, have Exec append JFailed when a rerun of an item whose last journal event is an Intent ends in OConflict at Exec.hs:455/469.

confirmed.title: DESIGN §6.4 row C3 (journal tail lost, dst intact → 补记 Done) is not implemented; the code's "C3" tag means 'Done without Intent (skip)', and the test named "C3 语义" pins zero findings
confirmed.summary: DESIGN.md defines C3 as 'dst 存在 sha==expected + journal 无任何记录（掉电丢 journal 尾）→ 按内容归属为已完成拷贝并补记 Done', and says the power-loss model is 'caught by C3/R2'. Doctor has no code path for that state: with no Intent there is nothing pending, so the run reports nothing and never appends a Done. The finding tag "C3" in Doctor.hs is instead used for "Done 无对应 Intent（journal 头部轮转或跨批），跳过". KernelTests.hs:416-428 asserts zero Warn rows, pinning the non-implementation, and DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:293 still tells users the "C3/C4 行专门接这个残余". A user reading doctor output against the matrix is told the wrong meaning for C3.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Power loss after a batch landed N copies but before the journal tail reached media. `pm doctor` (and `--repair`) report nothing and append no Done; `pm undo` cannot see those N copies, `pm plan list` shows the plan as 未执行, and a reader following DESIGN §6.4 expects a C3 row/補記 that never appears. || Journal ends up with a Done for X#3 but its Intent line was lost. `pm doctor` prints `· [C3] X#3: Done 无对应 Intent（journal 头部轮转或跨批），跳过`; the user looks up C3 in DESIGN §6.4 and reads 'dst ok, no journal record, doctor 补记 Done' — the opposite of what happened.
confirmed.evidence: DESIGN.md:355/375 C3 row; DESIGN.md:388 '掉电模型（journal 尾部丢失）由 C3/R2 接住'; Doctor.hs:530/542 `Nothing -> pure [Finding "C3" Info (T.unpack oid <> ": Done 无对应 Intent（journal 头部轮转或跨批），跳过") ""]`; Doctor.hs:132-142 pending/verify derivation has no branch for 'no record at all'; KernelTests.hs:416-428 expectation `[r | r@(tag, sev) <- rows, sev >= Warn, tag /= "TORN"] @?= []`; DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:293.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Doctor.hs:126-141 derive pending (last event Intent) and donesAfterClean (Done entries after the last CleanShutdown); there is no code path that considers a dst present on disk with no journal record at all — such a file is invisible to doctor (only pm scan / --deep look at catalog vs disk, and neither appends a Done). The tag 'C3' is used only at Doctor.hs:542: verifyDone with no Intent for a Done -> Finding 'C3' Info '<oid>: Done 无对应 Intent（journal 头部轮转或跨批），跳过'. applyRepairs (676-698) appends Done only for C2/R2/Q-DONE-LOST. REPRO: execute P (Intent + Done landed 相册/a.jpg), then truncate the journal to empty (test/KernelTests.hs:416-427 does exactly this): opState empty, pending [], donesAfterClean [] -> no C-row at all, no Done appended even with --repair; `pm undo` cannot see the copy. Second half: a journal with JDone X#3 but no JIntent X#3 -> line 542 prints '· [C3] X#3: Done 无对应 Intent…'; DESIGN §6.4 C3 describes the opposite state ('dst 存在 sha==expected + journal 无任何记录 -> 补记 Done'). DESIGN: DESIGN.md:355 (C3 row), :365 ('掉电模型（journal 尾部丢失）由 C3/R2 接住'), :599 (risk table cites 'C3/C4') and DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:293 ('doctor（--backup）的 C3/C4 行专门接这个残余') all promise a C3 补记-Done behaviour that does not exist; the docs agree with the finder. The only test, KernelTests.hs:416-427, is named '(C3 语义)' but asserts merely that no Warn rows appear and the file is intact — it does not assert a Done is appended and does not run --repair, so it pins 'nothing happens', contradicting the doc rather than confirming it. Mitigating: under I4 the Intent is barrier-flushed before the copy starts, so 'dst landed + no record at all' needs lying hardware (the C4 row's model), which is why the gap is low-impact; still, the printed 'C3' tag has a meaning different from the matrix a user is told to consult. Doc/code drift, low.
verdict.corrected_summary: DESIGN §6.4 row C3 (dst intact, sha==expected, no journal record -> attribute as completed copy and append Done; DESIGN.md:355/365/599, DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:293) has no implementation: doctor derives everything from Intent/Done records and never sees a landed file with no record, and --repair never appends such a Done. The 'C3' finding tag actually printed by Doctor.hs:542 means 'Done without a matching Intent, skipped', so a user cross-checking doctor output against the matrix reads the wrong row. KernelTests.hs:416 '(C3 语义)' only asserts no Warn rows and does not test the documented 补记. Practical impact is small because I4's Intent barrier makes the documented C3 state reachable only through hardware that lies about flush.
verdict.suggested_fix: Documentation/label fix: rename the Doctor.hs:542 tag from 'C3' to a distinct tag (e.g. 'DONE-ORPHAN'), and rewrite the DESIGN.md C3 row (and the references at DESIGN.md:365/599, DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:293, the KernelTests.hs:416 test name) to state the actual contract: a copy with no journal record is not reconcilable by doctor (the Intent barrier makes that state a lying-flush case caught by C4 / --deep / pm scan), or, if the promised behaviour is wanted, implement it by reading stored plan files for OpCopy items with no journal record whose dst sha matches and reporting them (Info, and 补记 Done only under --repair).

confirmed.title: Legitimately purged trash payloads are reported as C4 'Done target missing' when no CleanShutdown follows the Done
confirmed.summary: The C4 verification window is 'every Done after the last JCleanShutdown'. Only Pm.Exec writes JCleanShutdown; doctor --repair appends Done entries without one, and `pm trash empty` writes nothing to the journal. So Quarantine Dones in the open window stay under verification indefinitely, and after the user purges the trash doctor reports them as C4 Bad with advice to regenerate the plan.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A batch crashes after item #3's Quarantine Done but before JCleanShutdown (or the user runs `pm doctor --repair`, which appends Q-DONE-LOST Done #3). The user runs `pm trash empty --yes`. Next `pm doctor`: afterClean still contains Done #3 → checkTrashTarget → PmStateMissing → 'C4 Bad: Done 记录的目标不存在 … 重新生成计划', exit 1, on every subsequent run until some other plan execution writes a CleanShutdown.
confirmed.evidence: Doctor.hs:144 `afterClean = lastSegment entries` (348-353 cuts at last JCleanShutdown). Sole writer Exec.hs:169. applyRepairs (Doctor.hs:690-698) appends JDone only. Commands.hs trashEmptyLocked' purgeLoop (421-427) never touches the journal. checkTrashTarget (583-597) has no exemption other than restoredAfter (156-166).

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Doctor.hs:144 `afterClean = lastSegment entries`; lastSegment (Doctor.hs:318-323) cuts at the last JCleanShutdown, whole list if none. donesAfterClean (145) feeds verifyDone (Doctor.hs:543-568), which for an OpQuarantine Done with a trash path calls checkTrashTarget (583-597) unless restoredAfter holds; PmStateMissing from probePmSha (isDoesNotExistError, Doctor.hs:~380) yields `Finding "C4" Bad (oid <> ": Done 记录的目标不存在 (" <> trashRel <> ")") "不删任何东西；该项标回未确认，重新生成计划"`. Writers: grep shows JCleanShutdown is appended only at Exec.hs:169 (end of execPlan, inside withJournal, unconditionally even for an empty item list since validatePlan Plan.hs:145-153 does not reject []). applyRepairs Doctor.hs:690-698 appends only `JDone oid sha trash` with Barrier and no CleanShutdown. Commands.hs trashEmptyLocked' (338-427) and purgeLoop (421-427) touch only deleteBoundAt; there is no jAppend anywhere in Commands.hs, and the summary line says `manifest 记录保留为历史`. The resume branch of execQuarantine' (Exec.hs:660-672) deliberately does not rewrite the journal (`journal 不重写：缺失的 Done 由 doctor 补记`). REPRO: backup root, journal tail = [..., JCleanShutdown(prev batch), Intent P#3 (OpQuarantine victim v.jpg sha S reason supersede:P), <drop before Done>]. User runs `pm doctor --backup --repair` (CLI, as in REVIEW-LOG.md:593 `修复: 补记 Done #569`) → classifyPending reports Q-DONE-LOST Warn → applyRepairs appends JDone P#3 (Just S) (Just "P\v.jpg"). No plan is re-executed (`pm backup` is a scan). User later runs `pm trash --backup empty --yes` → reason supersede: → barrierOf = Nothing → plainRecs → purgeable → deleteBoundAt unlinks .pm/trash/P/v.jpg, manifest unchanged, journal unchanged. Next `pm doctor --backup`: afterClean = [Intent P#3, Done P#3]; verifyDone: intents has P#3, opPathsOk, msha=Just S, mtrash=Just "P\v.jpg", restoredAfter False (no ~r Done) → checkTrashTarget → probePmSha → open fails DoesNotExist → PmStateMissing → C4 Bad `Done 记录的目标不存在 (P\v.jpg)` with advice to regenerate the plan; runDoctor' exit code 1 (worst >= Warn). Repeats on every run until some plan execution on that root writes a CleanShutdown. Same result if the batch simply crashed after item #3's Done and the user never re-ran the plan (e.g. `pm plan rm`), then purged the trash. The built-in 1.1.2 execPlanRetry path is NOT affected: heal → then `go` calls execPlan (even with todo'=[]) which writes CleanShutdown, so the window closes there. DESIGN: DESIGN.md §6.4 (line 366) and §6.6 say the default window is 「上次 CleanShutdown 之后的全部 Done」(有界：只有被中断那场会话) — the intent is a bounded window for the interrupted session, but nothing closes it after a CLI `--repair`. The C4 row of the matrix (DESIGN.md:356) is defined as `Intent+Done 齐全但 dst sha ≠ expected`; no matrix row covers `Done + trash payload absent`, and `pm trash empty` is the sanctioned unlink (DESIGN.md:255, §5). No REVIEW-LOG entry rules this intended; REVIEW-LOG.md:593 only notes the window semantics as a discovery. The pinned test PlannerTests.hs:606-613 covers *external* removeFile of a trash file inside the window (must be C4), not a pm-sanctioned purge; README known limitations do not list it. Severity is low: misleading Bad row + exit 1, no disk effect, no repair inference (C4 is not in the --repair whitelist).
verdict.corrected_summary: The C4 re-verification window is 'every Done since the last JCleanShutdown', but JCleanShutdown is written only at the end of Pm.Exec.execPlan. A Quarantine Done appended by a standalone `pm doctor --repair` (Q-DONE-LOST), or left by a crashed batch that is never re-run, stays in the window indefinitely. `pm trash empty` unlinks those trash payloads without touching the journal, so the next `pm doctor` reports each purged item as `C4 Bad: Done 记录的目标不存在 … 重新生成计划` and exits 1 until some unrelated plan execution on that root writes a CleanShutdown. The 1.1.2 execPlanRetry heal path is unaffected (it re-enters execPlan, which writes CleanShutdown even for an empty todo). Misleading message on an edge path; nothing on disk is affected.
verdict.suggested_fix: Minimal: in checkTrashTarget (Doctor.hs:585-587) change the PmStateMissing wording for trash targets to say the payload is absent and may have been purged by `pm trash empty` (drop the '重新生成计划' advice), and/or downgrade it to Warn when the manifest still holds a record for that trashRel. Cleaner: have `pm trash empty` (inside its root lock, after a fully successful purgeLoop) or `doctor --repair` (after a pass whose window verified with zero Bad rows) append a JCleanShutdown so verified/purged Dones leave the window — but that widens the set of CleanShutdown writers and should be reflected in DESIGN §6.4.

confirmed.title: applyRepairs reports repairs via bare putStrLn, so the automatic heal inside pm serve's apply endpoint loses them
confirmed.summary: Pm.Cli.executePlanNow' calls `runDoctorWith dw root (DoctorOpts False True)` as the `heal` step and only forwards a count of Warn rows to the sink. Everything applyRepairs actually did — '跳过: … 人工核查', '✗ pm 自建文件未清除', '修复: C5 隔离计划已生成 …' — is written with putStrLn to stdout, which under `pm ui` is a null device, so these lines never reach the GUI user.
confirmed.failure_scenario: GUI user executes a backup plan; the USB drive drops mid-copy; heal → doctor --repair detects a C5 and generates `doctor-c5-quarantine` plan P; the only text in the GUI log is '· 自愈：pm doctor --repair 补记 Done 0 条'. The user later sees an unexplained doctor-c5-quarantine plan with no message saying why it exists.
confirmed.evidence: src/Pm/Doctor.hs:698 `putStrLn ("  修复: 补记 Done " <> T.unpack oid)`, :707, :712-714, :722, :738; src/Pm/Cli.hs:149-151 heal; src/Pm/Cli.hs:106-113 sink rationale.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: applyRepairs (Doctor.hs:679-740) reports every action with bare putStrLn: 698 `putStrLn ("  修复: 补记 Done " <> T.unpack oid)`, 707 `跳过: … 不再是可信路径 … 人工核查`, 712-714 `修复: 清除 pm 自建文件…` / `✗ pm 自建文件未清除…`, 722 `跳过: C5 隔离计划未生成…`, 738 `修复: C5 隔离计划已生成 <fp> → 审阅后 pm apply <pid>`. Its signature is `FilePath -> [Finding] -> [(Text,Op)] -> [FilePath] -> IO ()`, it returns nothing, and runDoctor' (Doctor.hs:~255) does `[] <$ applyRepairs …`, so the actions never appear as Findings either. Cli.hs:146-151: `heal = do (fs,_) <- runDoctorWith dw root (DoctorOpts False True); sink (printf "· 自愈：pm doctor --repair 补记 Done %d 条" (length [() | f <- fs, fRow f `elem` ["C2","R2","Q-DONE-LOST"], fSeverity f == Warn]))` — only a count derived from the diagnosis rows is forwarded (note: it is computed from findings, not from what applyRepairs did, so on an I11/I10 refusal (Doctor.hs:99-108 diagnoseOnly) it would still print '补记 Done N 条' with N>0 while nothing was appended). Serve.hs:151 `when (soExitOnStdinEof o) muteStdout` and ServeGuard.hs:101-114 confirm that under `pm ui` stdout is hDuplicateTo'd onto \\.\NUL after the announce line, so the finder's 'null device' claim is accurate. confirmed.title: Copy: second tmp confinement check failing after JIntent was journaled returns OConflict without a terminal JFailed (dangling Intent; doctor then reports a bogus C1 'interrupted')
confirmed.summary: In execCopy' the Intent is appended with a barrier, then createDirectoryIfMissing runs and confinedTmp is re-resolved. If that second resolution yields Nothing (surrogate layer, or ProbeUnknown from an ACL/transient error), the item returns escapeOutcome (OConflict) without appending any terminal for the oid, unlike every other post-Intent failure arm which writes JFailed. The batch then writes JCleanShutdown, leaving a dangling Intent that doctor classifies as C1 and that planExecs counts neither as done nor failed. PathGuardTests.caseExecTmpSecondCheck never asserts the journal.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Plan item Copy ix=3: first confinedTmp succeeds and Intent 'p#3' is written. Between line 483 and 491 the probe of .pm/tmp/<pid>/3-x.jpg answers ProbeUnknown, so mTmp2 == Nothing and the item returns OConflict '路径逐级解析后不在 root/.pm\trash 之内'. No JFailed; execPlan' appends JCleanShutdown. Afterwards `pm doctor` reports C1 for p#3 claiming an interruption 'before writing tmp' although the session ended cleanly; `pm plan list` shows the item as neither done nor failed. || Backup drive hiccup or AV momentarily denies GetFileAttributes on .pm\tmp\<pid> → same outcome; the plan page keeps the oid unresolved.

confirmed.title: updateCatalog never re-adds the entry restored by `pm undo` of a Quarantine (rename from .pm/trash), leaving the catalog silently missing a file that is back in the library
confirmed.summary: When a Quarantine item lands, updateCatalog deletes the victim's catalog entry. The reverse op generated by Undo.reverseOp' is `OpRename (trashSrcRel trashRel) victim`, and updateCatalog's OpRename branch only re-keys entries under `old` (`.pm\trash\…`); no such keys exist, so the catalog is unchanged. The in-session rollback path avoids this by rewriting the quarantine outcome to OFailed, but the cross-session undo path has no equivalent.
confirmed.failure_scenario: 1) `pm clean staging --apply` quarantines `To-Be-Sync'd\X\a.jpg`; updateCatalog deletes the entry. 2) `pm undo --last 1` then `pm apply <undo-id>`: execRename moves the file back, prints `DONE`. 3) updateCatalog (OpRename old=`.pm\trash\...`) matches nothing → catalog saved without `a.jpg`. `pm import`/`pm backup` are blocked by the freshness sweep ('暂存区与索引不一致（新增 1…）→ 先 pm scan') with no hint that the undo caused it.
confirmed.evidence: ExecTypes.hs:119-126 `(OpRename old new _, ODone {}) -> let (moved, kept) = partition (underPrefix old . fst) …`; ExecTypes.hs:127-128 `(OpQuarantine victim _ _, ODone {}) -> c {catEntries = Map.delete victim …}`. Undo.hs:129-136. Exec.hs:633-637 restore rename returns `ODone Nothing Nothing Nothing`. Contrast Exec.hs:179-181 `restoredMark = OFailed …`. Cli.hs:273-286 writeBackCatalog.
confirmed.category: wrong-result / stale index on edge path

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Undo.hs:129-136 reverses a Quarantine Done into `OpRename (trashSrcRel trashRel) victim (FpFileSha sha)`; Op.hs:226-227 makes `old` = `.pm\trash\<trashRel>`. `pm undo` (Apply.hs:95-109) only saves the plan; `pm apply` runs Cli.hs executePlanNow' which, after execPlanRetry, calls writeBackCatalog (Cli.hs:158, 273-286) → updateCatalog. execRename (Exec.hs:633-637) returns `ODone Nothing Nothing Nothing` (no stat, no sha). updateCatalog (ExecTypes.hs:119-126) handles OpRename purely by re-keying entries whose key is `underPrefix old`; the catalog never contains `.pm\…` keys because scan skips dot dirs (Scan.hs:79 SkipDotDirs), so `moved = []` and the fold is the identity. The victim's entry was removed at quarantine time by ExecTypes.hs:127-128. Nothing else re-adds it: no rescan in runUndoCmd, afterApply, or writeBackCatalog. REPRO: catalog has entry `To-Be-Sync'd\X\a.jpg`. (1) `pm clean staging --apply` → OpQuarantine lands ODone(sha, Nothing, Just "<pid>\To-Be-Sync'd\X\a.jpg") → line 128 deletes the entry, catalog saved. (2) `pm undo --last 1` → plan with OpRename `.pm\trash\<pid>\To-Be-Sync'd\X\a.jpg` → `To-Be-Sync'd\X\a.jpg`; `pm apply <id>` → execRename fingerprint check passes, moveBoundNoReplace succeeds, DONE, ODone Nothing Nothing Nothing. (3) updateCatalog line 125: `partition (underPrefix ".pm\trash\<pid>\…")` over keys like `Raw\…`, `相册\…` → no match → catalog saved unchanged, i.e. without a.jpg although the file is back on disk. (4) Next `pm import`/`pm clean staging`/`pm sort` hit stagingFresh (Cli.hs:472-489) → `暂存区与索引不一致（新增 1 …）→ 先 pm scan`; `pm status` (Status.hs:163) reports pending 1 and exits 1. Contrast: the in-session rollback path deliberately rewrites the outcome to OFailed precisely so the catalog does not lose a restored entry (Exec.hs:178-181: "不能报 ODone，否则 catalog 回写会删掉一个实际已回到原位的条目"), showing the intended contract is catalog ≙ disk after a restore; the cross-session undo path has no equivalent. DESIGN: DESIGN.md:138 documents the snapshot as a rebuildable cache and Cli.hs:270-272 accepts lag only for the lock-busy case ("滞后可以接受，静默丢更新不可以"); no doc/REVIEW-LOG entry says undo of a quarantine requires `pm scan`; DESIGN.md:256 / README:227 describe undo→apply with no scan step. The only test (KernelTests.hs:703-715 "undo quarantine = 从 trash 原位复位") checks file contents only and does not pin catalog state, so nothing pins the current behaviour. Impact is bounded: the freshness gates in import/backup/status catch the drift before any decision is made from the stale index and the message names the remedy, and no data-safety invariant is touched — hence low severity, but the defect is real.
verdict.corrected_summary: After `pm undo` of a Quarantine is applied, the reverse op is `OpRename .pm\trash\<pid>\<victim> -> <victim>`; execRename returns `ODone Nothing Nothing Nothing` and updateCatalog's OpRename branch only re-keys entries under `old`, which never exist for a `.pm\trash` prefix. The victim's catalog entry (deleted when the quarantine landed) is therefore never restored, so the saved catalog silently omits a file that is back in the library. confirmed.title: I11 guard (pmIgnoreGuard) does not skip a UTF-8 BOM in .gitignore, so a BOM'd file whose first line is `.pm/` is rejected as '缺 `.pm/` 行' although git honours it
confirmed.summary: The guard splits `TE.decodeUtf8Lenient raw` with T.lines and requires a line exactly equal to ".pm/"; `norm` strips only a trailing CR and spaces. A .gitignore saved with a UTF-8 BOM (Notepad, PowerShell 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`) yields a first line "\xFEFF.pm/", so hasRule is False and init/backup init/vault push/execPlan are refused with a message saying the `.pm/` line is missing. git itself strips the BOM (skip_utf8_bom since v2.6).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repo root .gitignore created in Notepad containing exactly `.pm/` (with BOM). `pm init --main <repo>` → Left "I11: 主库 root 是 git 工作树且 .gitignore 未有效覆盖 `.pm/`（缺 `.pm/` 行）". `git check-ignore .pm/x` answers ignored. || vault root's `.gitignore` BOM-prefixed: `pm vault push` / `pm apply` refused; the user re-adds `.pm/` (now duplicated) to make pm accept it. || PowerShell 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 .gitignore ".pm/"`: the user checks the file, sees the line, and cannot tell what to fix.
confirmed.evidence: src/Pm/GitGuard.hs:99-102: `let norm l = T.dropWhileEnd (== ' ') (fromMaybe l (T.stripSuffix "\r" l)); ls = map norm (T.lines (TE.decodeUtf8Lenient raw)); hasRule = ".pm/" `elem` ls`; :108/:111 `(False, _) -> pure (Left (i11Msg igFp "缺 `.pm/` 行"))`. No BOM handling in the module. DESIGN.md §2 I11 row claims alignment with git 2.52. Callers: Config.requireWritable, Exec.execPlan', initPreflight/backupInitPreflight, Vault.ensureVaultRoot. GuardTests only write BOM-less files.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/GitGuard.hs:91 reads the raw bytes with BS.readFile; :100-102 `norm l = T.dropWhileEnd (== ' ') (fromMaybe l (T.stripSuffix "\r" l))`, `ls = map norm (T.lines (TE.decodeUtf8Lenient raw))`, `hasRule = ".pm/" `elem` ls`. Data.Text.Encoding.decodeUtf8Lenient decodes EF BB BF as U+FEFF and keeps it (no BOM stripping in the text library); T.lines only splits on '\n'; norm only removes a trailing CR and trailing spaces. grep -rn -i 'BOM|FEFF' over src/ test/ docs/ README.md finds nothing, so nothing upstream strips it either. Every caller passes the file untouched: Commands.initPreflight (:103, main root — on Left it just prints and exits 2, no append offer), BackupCmd.hs:70, Vault.ensureVaultRoot (:472), Exec.hs:101/:151 (pre-lock and in-lock recheck), Config.requireWritable (:563), Serve.hs:232. git's dir.c add_patterns_from_buffer calls skip_utf8_bom() before parsing (since git 2.5/2.6), so git ignores `.pm/` in a BOM'd file. REPRO: on-disk .gitignore = EF BB BF 2E 70 6D 2F 0D 0A (Notepad 'UTF-8 with BOM' / PowerShell 5.1 Set-Content -Encoding UTF8), `.git` dir present. probeName -> NamePlain -> Right True (:82); doesFileExist True; raw decoded = "\xFEFF.pm/\r\n"; T.lines -> ["\xFEFF.pm/\r"]; norm -> "\xFEFF.pm/"; `".pm/" elem ["\xFEFF.pm/"]` = False; negations = []; case (False, _) at :108 -> Left (i11Msg igFp "缺 `.pm/` 行") -> message '主库 root 是 git 工作树且 .gitignore 未有效覆盖 `.pm/`（缺 `.pm/` 行）'. `pm init --main <repo>` exits 2 with that text while `git check-ignore .pm/x` says ignored; same Left for vault push / apply / execPlan. Wrong outcome reached: the diagnostic asserts a line is missing that is visibly present. DESIGN: docs/DESIGN.md:103 (I11 row) says '行的归一与 git 2.52 逐字符对齐' and the :95-99 comment says the guard is a '精确限制' of gitignore(5) — the docs claim git alignment, and git does honour the BOM, so the docs side with the finder rather than pinning the rejection as intended. REVIEW-LOG-4 F066 (:207, :316) only ruled on leading/trailing whitespace and CRLF; no review round, README known-limitations (465-553), or test (GuardTests/VaultTests write only BOM-less files) addresses a BOM. Mitigating: the miss is on the fail-closed side (refuse, never grant), so no I11 safety violation and no data risk; a user who appends a second `.pm/` line gets past it. Hence severity low (misleading message / minor contract drift), not medium.
verdict.corrected_summary: pmIgnoreGuard (src/Pm/GitGuard.hs:100-108) does not strip a leading UTF-8 BOM from .gitignore, so a file whose first (or only) line is `.pm/` written with a BOM (Notepad 'UTF-8 with BOM', PowerShell 5.1 Set-Content/Out-File -Encoding UTF8) is rejected with '缺 `.pm/` 行' although git (skip_utf8_bom in dir.c) ignores `.pm/` for that file. The refusal is on the safe (fail-closed) side, so I11 is not violated; the defect is the false diagnostic ('the line is missing') that contradicts what the user sees and the DESIGN §2 I11 claim of character-level alignment with git 2.52. Workaround is trivial (append a second `.pm/` line or re-save without BOM), so impact is low.
verdict.suggested_fix:
In pmIgnoreGuard, drop one leading U+FEFF before splitting: `let txt = TE.decodeUtf8Lenient raw; body = fromMaybe txt (T.stripPrefix "\xFEFF" txt); ls = map norm (T.lines body)` (mirrors git's skip_utf8_bom, which only skips the BOM at the very start of the file, and stays a strict subset of git's accept set). Add a GuardTests case that writes BS.pack [0xEF,0xBB,0xBF] <> ".pm/
" next to a `.git` dir and asserts Right (), plus a case that a BOM in the middle of the file (`_site/
\xFEFF.pm/
`) is still rejected. Alternatively, if the maintainers prefer to keep rejecting, change the message to say a BOM/non-ASCII prefix was found rather than '缺 `.pm/` 行'.

confirmed.title: runTwoPlans reports 'unfinished items' when the main plan was refused outright (lock busy / root mismatch)
confirmed.summary: executePlanNowWith returns `(2, [])` when execPlan is refused. runTwoPlans treats every `PrRun c1 rs1` that is not `c1 == 0 && fullyExecuted rs1` identically and prints `主库（相册）那份有未完成项（失败/冲突/待裁决…）：vault 那份不执行…pm resolve 处理后重跑本命令`, directing the user to pm resolve although no item was executed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `pm vault ingest --apply --yes a.jpg --category landscape` while another pm holds the main root lock: the sink prints `另一个 pm 实例正持有该 root 的锁（I10），稍后重试`, then the ingest layer adds the contradictory `主库（相册）那份有未完成项…pm resolve 处理后重跑本命令` and exits 2.
confirmed.evidence: Cli.hs:183-184 `Left e -> sink e >> pure (2, [])`; Cli.hs:280-281 fullyExecuted; Ingest.hs:153-170 `PrRun c1 rs1 | c1 == 0 && fullyExecuted rs1 -> … | otherwise -> do putStrLn "主库（相册）那份有未完成项…"; pure (max c1 1)`.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Cli.hs:182-184 (executePlanNow') — `r <- execPlanRetry dw heal env plan; case r of Left e -> sink e >> pure (2, [])`. So every kernel-level refusal of execution (Exec.hs:176 lock busy `另一个 pm 实例正持有该 root 的锁（I10），稍后重试`; Exec.hs:128-146 root-id mismatch; Exec.hs:93-100 requirePmTrusted / validatePlan / noIdentityMsg; Exec.hs:159 `（执行期重检，整批拒绝）`; Removable.hs:245-247 drive-retry abort) surfaces to savePlanAndMaybeRunTo (Cli.hs:262) as `PrRun 2 []` — the PlanRun type (Cli.hs:190-197) has no constructor for 'saved but execution refused'; PrRefused is documented only for 'root 不可写，计划未保存'. In src/Pm/Ingest.hs:153-170 runTwoPlans matches `PrRun c1 rs1 | c1 == 0 && fullyExecuted rs1 -> … | otherwise -> putStrLn "主库（相册）那份有未完成项（失败/冲突/待裁决——待裁决不进退出码，也算未完成）：vault 那份不执行（I7…）；pm resolve 处理后重跑本命令" >> pure (max c1 1)`. `fullyExecuted [] = False` (Cli.hs:281, deliberately) so the refusal lands in the `otherwise` branch. REPRO: main root D:\main with .pm/root-id.json, vault configured, another pm process holds D:\main\.pm\lock. Run `pm vault ingest --apply --yes D:\_inbox\a.jpg --category landscape`. runVaultIngest builds mainPlan/vaultPlan (Ingest.hs:126-128) → runTwoPlans → runPlan mainPlan = savePlanAndMaybeRun' → Cli.hs:255 requireWritable Right → savePlan writes the plan file → confirm with --yes = True → executePlanNowWith (plRootId is Just) → execPlanRetry → execPlan → requirePmTrusted OK → execPlan' → withRootLock returns Nothing → Exec.hs:176 Left lock message → Cli.hs:184 prints it and returns (2, []) → Ingest.hs:153 `PrRun 2 []`: guard fails (c1=2), `otherwise` prints the 'has unfinished items (failed/conflict/pending) … run pm resolve then rerun' line and exits 2. No item was executed and there is nothing for pm resolve to act on; stdout shows the two contradictory lines back to back. REVIEW-LOG-2.md:298 (round 33) verified 'ingest 各分支退出码与次序正确' and 'fullyExecuted [] = False 无协议洞' — exit codes and ordering, not this message. No test in test/IngestTests.hs pins the message for a PrRun 2 [] input (caseIngestVaultGate/caseIngestStepsGate exercise real per-item outcomes). README 465-553 lists nothing about it. Hence not ruled intended; finding stands at low severity.
verdict.corrected_summary: In runTwoPlans (src/Pm/Ingest.hs:168-170) a main plan whose execution was refused outright by the kernel (lock busy I10, root-id mismatch, .pm untrusted, plan validation, drive-retry abort) arrives as `PrRun 2 []` (Cli.hs:184) and is reported with the same text as a plan that ran and left CONFLICT/FAILED/NEEDS-DECISION items — '主库（相册）那份有未完成项…pm resolve 处理后重跑本命令' — right after the kernel already printed the real reason. The exit code (2) and the I7 gate (vault plan not executed) are correct; only the guidance is misleading (pm resolve has nothing to resolve; the plan is on disk and just needs pm apply/rerun once the lock is free).
verdict.suggested_fix: Add a dedicated guard before `otherwise` in Ingest.hs:153-170, e.g. `PrRun c1 [] -> do putStrLn "主库（相册）那份未执行（执行被拒，原因见上一行）：vault 那份不执行（I7：相册在前）；处理后重跑本命令或 pm apply <主库计划 id>"; pure (max c1 1)`. Alternatively give PlanRun a distinct constructor (e.g. PrExecRefused String) returned from savePlanAndMaybeRunTo when executePlanNowWith yields (2, []), with planRunCode = 2 and planIdOf = Just pid, and handle it in runTwoPlans and Vault.hs:615 (`_ -> pure ()` already covers it).

confirmed.title: isTrashSrcRel admits `.pm/trash` itself and `.pm/trash/manifest.ndjson` as rename sources, so a hand-edited plan can move pm's own trash state into user data
confirmed.summary: isTrashSrcRel only compares the first two path components against ['.pm','trash'], so `.pm/trash` (exactly two components) and `.pm/trash/manifest.ndjson` pass. opPathsOk therefore accepts OpRename with these as the old path, and validatePlan/loadPlan/execItem all defer to opPathsOk. Exec's execRename resolves the old side with plain resolveUnder, so the manifest (or the entire trash directory) can be moved into user space by a hand-edited plan. PathGuardTests never probe the trash root or the manifest.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A plan file is hand-edited to contain `{"t":"rename","old":".pm/trash/manifest.ndjson","new":"m.txt","fp":{"file":"<sha256>"}}`. loadPlan -> validatePlan passes. `pm apply <id>` -> execRename: moveBoundNoReplace moves the write-ahead manifest to <root>/m.txt, Done. Afterwards every quarantined file is UNREGISTERED, `pm trash empty` reports nothing purgeable, doctor emits Q1 for every trash file, and `pm undo` refuses the reversal with '撤销一次复位需要独立的 redo 协议，拒绝'. || `old = ".pm\\trash"` + FpDir moves the whole quarantine area into the library where the next `pm scan` indexes the quarantined bytes as library photos.
confirmed.evidence: Op.hs:219-220 `isTrashSrcRel p = relPathOk p && map normComp (take 2 (splitDirectories p)) == map normComp [".pm", pmSubTrash]`; :232-235 opPathsOk; :229-231 doc comment '其余任何 .pm 前缀…拒绝'. Plan.hs:151; Exec.hs:360; Exec.hs:580-583 `mOld <- if isTrashSrcRel (opOldRel op) then resolveUnder root (opOldRel op) else confinedUserPath …`; Exec.hs:589-637. Trash.hs:75-76 manifestPath. Undo.hs:103-111. Exec.hs:282-286, Undo.hs:136 generated sources always ≥2 components below trash. Trash.hs:220-233; Commands.hs:383-384.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Op.hs:219-220 `isTrashSrcRel p = relPathOk p && map normComp (take 2 (splitDirectories p)) == map normComp [".pm", pmSubTrash]` has no depth requirement, so `.pm/trash` (2 comps) and `.pm/trash/manifest.ndjson` (3 comps) satisfy it. opPathsOk (Op.hs:232-235) is the sole lexical gate for validatePlan (Plan.hs:151), execItem (Exec.hs:360) and reverseOp (Undo.hs:105,121). execRename (Exec.hs:580-583) routes any isTrashSrcRel old-path through plain `resolveUnder root`, which for all-NamePlain components returns `Just <root>/.pm/trash/manifest.ndjson` (Win.hs:478-504). moveBoundNoReplace (Win.hs:695-715) opens via pm_open_for_dispose with FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS (cbits/pm_win.c:55), so both the file and the directory (`.pm/trash` + FpDir via dirFingerprint, Exec.hs:613) forms rename successfully. All generated trash sources are `trashSrcRel (quarDirFor pid sfx </> victim)` (Exec.hs:282-286, Undo.hs:136, Trash.hs:96-97), i.e. depth >= 4, so no producer needs the shallow forms. REPRO: plan 20260925-120000-abcdef.json with item {t:rename, old:".pm/trash/manifest.ndjson", new:"m.txt", fp:{file:<sha256 of manifest>}}. `pm apply`: loadPlan -> validatePlan passes (userRelOk old False, isTrashSrcRel old True, userRelOk new True); runApply (Apply.hs:154-171) prints renderPlan and calls executePlanNowWith with no further prompt; execRename' sees oldIsFile, new absent, sha matches -> JIntent -> moveBoundNoReplace -> JDone. Then readManifest' returns Right Nothing (Trash.hs:150): all quarantined files become unregistered; `pm undo` of that Done generates OpRename "m.txt" ".pm/trash/manifest.ndjson" which reverseOp rejects (Undo.hs:104-111) with the redo-protocol message. Wrong outcome reached. DESIGN: the comment at the site (Op.hs:215-218, 229-231) states the contract: the only .pm exception is the undo/reset rename *source* that moves a quarantined file back; any other .pm-prefixed path is manipulation of pm's own state and must be rejected. Plan.hs:143-146 and REVIEW-LOG-1 (P3b-8 six-round major, P3b-16) treat hand-edited plan paths as fail-closed input. No REVIEW-LOG ruling, DESIGN §14 window, or README limitation accepts the trash root or manifest as a rename source; PathGuardTests.hs:116,206-210 only pin depth-4 sources. Docs agree with the finder, so not refuted. Severity low: no bytes are destroyed (manifest/dir is renamed, hand-recoverable), the user must author the plan and run apply themselves, and the printed plan shows the odd rename.
verdict.corrected_summary: isTrashSrcRel (Op.hs:220) only checks the first two components, so opPathsOk admits OpRename sources `.pm/trash` (with FpDir) and `.pm/trash/manifest.ndjson` (with FpFileSha) even though the documented contract (Op.hs:215-231) allows only quarantined payloads (`.pm/trash/<pid>[~displaced-N]/<victim>`, depth >= 4) as rename sources. validatePlan/loadPlan/execItem all defer to opPathsOk and execRename resolves such an old-path with plain resolveUnder, so a hand-edited plan run through `pm apply` moves pm's write-ahead manifest (or the whole quarantine directory) into user data; afterwards every trash payload is unregistered (doctor Q1, `pm trash empty` finds nothing purgeable) and `pm undo` refuses the reversal because `.pm/trash/...` is not allowed as a rename target. No bytes are lost and recovery is manual, so impact is low, but it is a validation gap relative to the documented .pm exception.
verdict.suggested_fix: Tighten the predicate to the shape every producer actually generates: `isTrashSrcRel p = relPathOk p && length comps >= 4 && map normComp (take 2 comps) == map normComp [".pm", pmSubTrash] where comps = splitDirectories p` (optionally also require the third component to parse via opIdParts / isValidPlanId-with-suffix). Add PathGuardTests cases asserting `opPathsOk (OpRename ".pm/trash" "x" (FpDir "aa")) == False` and `opPathsOk (OpRename (".pm" </> "trash" </> "manifest.ndjson") "m.txt" (FpFileSha "aa")) == False`, while keeping the existing depth-4 positives.

confirmed.title: deletePlanAnyRoot reports the vault root's 'plan does not exist' instead of the main root's real failure
confirmed.summary: deletePlanAnyRoot walks planRoots (main, then vault) and on any Left from the main root discards that message and continues; when the vault also answers Left the message returned is the vault's, so a genuine failure on the main root (untrusted .pm, sharing violation, ACL collapse) is reported as '计划不存在: <vault>/.pm/plans/<id>.json'. Same via POST /api/plan/delete (404).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Vault configured. Plan <id> exists in <main>/.pm/plans and is open in an editor (DELETE refused). `pm plan rm <id>`: deletePlan main → Left "删除失败: …"; go continues to vault → Left "计划不存在: <vault>/…"; runPlanRm prints that with exit 2.
confirmed.evidence: Plan.hs:429-433 `go ((label, root) : rest) = do r <- deletePlan root pid; case r of Right () -> pure (Right label); Left m -> if null rest then pure (Left m) else go rest`. deletePlan (Plan.hs:399-417) four indistinguishable Left reasons; line 412 boolean doesFileExist. Callers: runPlanRm (Plan.hs:487-489); Serve.hs:420-423.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Plan.hs:425-433 `deletePlanAnyRoot cfg pid = go (planRoots cfg)`; `go ((label, root) : rest) = do r <- deletePlan root pid; case r of Right () -> pure (Right label); Left m -> if null rest then pure (Left m) else go rest`. `planRoots` (Plan.hs:422) = [("主库", main)] ++ [("vault", v)] when configured. `deletePlan` (Plan.hs:399-417) returns four Left shapes: bad id, `requirePmTrusted` failure, `untrustedMsg` from resolveUnder, "计划不存在: <fp>" (line 412-413 after boolean doesFileExist), and "删除失败: <IOException>" (line 416) from `deleteBoundAt` (Win.hs:720-730, which throws userError on handle-open/bind/delete failure, e.g. sharing violation or bind mismatch). The main root's Left is discarded whenever a vault exists. The sibling `loadPlanAnyRoot` (src/Pm/Apply.hs:112-126) deliberately keeps and returns `mainErr` when later roots also fail, so the delete path is inconsistent with the load path. REPRO: config main=D:\Photography, vault=E:\vault. D:\Photography\.pm\plans\20260920-101010-abc123.json exists and is held open by a process without FILE_SHARE_DELETE (or the main .pm fails `requirePmTrusted`). `pm plan rm 20260920-101010-abc123` → runPlanRm (Plan.hs:484-491) → deletePlanAnyRoot → go [(主库,D:…),(vault,E:…)] → deletePlan main → deleteBoundAt throws → Left "删除失败: user error (D:\\…\\20260920-101010-abc123.json: 句柄删除失败, Win32 错误码 32)"; rest non-empty → go [(vault,…)] → deletePlan vault → doesFileExist False → Left "计划不存在: E:\\vault\\.pm\\plans\\20260920-101010-abc123.json"; rest null → returned; runPlanRm prints "✗ 20260920-101010-abc123: 计划不存在: E:\\vault\\…" exit 2, and POST /api/plan/delete (Serve.hs:420-423) answers 404 with that text although the plan exists in main and the real failure was a sharing/ACL error. The user is told the plan does not exist rather than that deletion failed. DESIGN: the comment at Plan.hs:424 only specifies the both-absent case ("都没有 → Left（最后一个根的原因）"); DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:570 says "主库 → vault 按序查找" with no ruling on error aggregation; REVIEW-LOG.md:564 registers a different minor (400-vs-404 for bad ids) and does not rule on this; no test pins deletePlanAnyRoot with a vault (test/PlanExecTests.hs only calls deletePlan directly). Not documented as intended → not refuted. Severity low: misleading message only; no write occurs and fail-closed is preserved.
verdict.corrected_summary: deletePlanAnyRoot (Plan.hs:429-433) drops the main root's Left and keeps only the last root's message, so when a vault is configured a real deletion failure on the main library (handle delete refused, untrusted .pm, resolveUnder failure) is reported to `pm plan rm` (exit 2) and to POST /api/plan/delete (404) as "计划不存在: <vault>/.pm/plans/<id>.json", hiding the true cause; loadPlanAnyRoot in Apply.hs already preserves the main-root error, so the two helpers are inconsistent.
verdict.suggested_fix: In deletePlanAnyRoot, distinguish absent from failed: only continue to the next root when the Left is the not-found case (e.g. have deletePlan return a small sum type or check the message prefix "计划不存在"), otherwise return that root's error immediately; when every root reports not-found, return the existing aggregate message. Alternatively collect all Lefts and join them with "；" in the final message.

confirmed.title: MAX_PATH pre-check (240) is applied to source paths only; derived .pm/trash and .pm/tmp paths are up to 33+ chars longer and can exceed 260 for sources that passed the gate
confirmed.summary: The only long-path guard is `length abs' >= maxPathLen` on scanned source paths. Quarantine lands at `.pm\trash\<22-char planId>\<victimRel>` and copy tmp at `.pm\tmp\<planId>\<ix>-<name>`; neither is length-checked. `length` counts Chars, not UTF-16 units. pm.exe carries no longPathAware manifest.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A staging file whose absolute path is 230 chars passes the gate and is planned by `pm clean staging`. At apply, moveBoundNoReplace victim → `.pm\trash\<pid>\...` (263 chars) → FileRenameInfo fails → JFailed + OFailed '隔离移动失败' on every retry. For a copy whose tmp path exceeds 260, copyFileHashed's openFreshBinary throws outside any try, the batch aborts, and Removable.judgeIO classifies the deterministic error as a Hiccup and retries 5× with 30 s cooldowns.
confirmed.evidence: Scan.hs:44-45 `maxPathLen = 240`; Scan.hs:130-132. Exec.hs:365-366 quarantine target; Trash.hs:89-91 quarDirFor; Exec.hs:66-73 tmpDirFor/tmpNameFor; Exec.hs:487-489 `wsha <- copyFileHashed (opSrcAbs op) tmp` not wrapped; Exec.hs:700-705. DESIGN.md:214. Removable.hs:197-203 judgeIO.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: The only length guard in the repo is Scan.hs:131 `if length abs' >= maxPathLen` (maxPathLen = 240, Scan.hs:45); `grep -rn maxPathLen src` finds no other user, and Op.hs/Plan.hs have no length check of any kind. Derived paths are built without a check: quarantine target = `quarDirFor pid SfxPlain </> opVictimRel op` (Exec.hs:366, Trash.hs:90-91 = the bare 22-char planId) under `.pm\trash\` via `confinedTrash` (Exec.hs:419-420), i.e. exactly `length abs' + 34` chars; copy tmp = `.pm\tmp\<pid>\<ix>-<name>` (Exec.hs:66-73, 430-432). Library behaviour: `directory` calls (createDirectoryIfMissing, doesFileExist, listDirectory) furnish absolute paths with `\\?\` so they succeed beyond MAX_PATH, but pm's own Win32 calls do not: `pm_rename_by_handle` passes the raw DOS string to SetFileInformationByHandle(FileRenameInfo) (pm_win.c:63-72) which goes through the DOS→NT conversion that is MAX_PATH-limited in a process without a longPathAware manifest; `openExclusiveBinary` uses Win32 `createFile` with `withTString` (Win.hs raw path) and base's openBinaryFile uses `_wopen`. package.yaml has no manifest/optl flags and GHC's generated manifest carries only requestedExecutionLevel, so pm.exe is not long-path aware. REPRO: root `D:\Photography` (14 chars); a file whose absolute path is 238 chars (passes the gate at 131). `pm dedupe`/`pm clean staging` plans a Quarantine of it. At apply: confinedUserPath OK; confinedTrash → resolveUnder probes each component with GetFileAttributesW; the >260-char tail probes fail with ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND(3) → NameMissing → Just path (Win.hs probeName). execQuarantine' (Exec.hs:659-700): doesFileExist True, sha256File on the 238-char victim OK, appendManifest, JIntent barrier, createDirectoryIfMissing (furnished, succeeds creating a 272-char dir), then moveBoundNoReplace: open victim OK, rawRename to the 272-char DOS path fails → `ioError (userError "… rename 失败（Win32 错误码 N，183=目标已存在）")` → caught at Exec.hs:700 → JFailed + OFailed '隔离移动失败' (Exec.hs:702-705). Every rerun fails identically; the group's other items are withheld by group semantics. No overwrite, no data loss, journal is consistent. The tmp branch: copyFileHashed at Exec.hs:500 is indeed not wrapped, but the failure is a CreateFileW ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND → errno ENOENT → NoSuchThing, which Removable.judgeIO (Removable.hs:110-116) classifies Deterministic, not Hiccup, so the finder's '5× retry with 30 s cooldown' detail is wrong; the escape is the documented write-port process-death semantics (DESIGN §14 row 'Lightroom / 用户并发改文件': 执行期写口逃逸 = §6.4 进程死亡语义). DESIGN: DESIGN.md:214 and §14:600 state the long-path mitigation is '完整路径 ≥240 字符即计划期报错 预检兜底', and Scan.hs:42-43 says 'refuse early and loudly instead of corrupting behaviour near MAX_PATH'. The 20-char margin does not cover pm's own 34-char trash prefix (or the ~36-char tmp prefix), so a file the gate admits still hits MAX_PATH at apply time, failing late with a message that hints at '183=目标已存在'. Not documented as a known limitation (README 465-553 has nothing on path length). Severity low: loud failure on an edge path with a misleading message; no invariant violated.
verdict.corrected_summary: The ≥240 pre-check (Scan.hs:131) only covers scanned source paths; quarantine targets (`.pm\trash\<22-char pid>\<victimRel>`, +34 chars) and copy tmp names (`.pm\tmp\<pid>\<ix>-<name>`) are never length-checked and pm's Win32 rename/create calls are not long-path aware, so a 226–239-char source file that passes the gate cannot be quarantined: `createDirectoryIfMissing` (directory furnishes `\\?\`) succeeds but `pm_rename_by_handle` fails and the item is JFailed/OFailed '隔離移動失敗 … rename 失败（Win32 错误码 …，183=目标已存在）' on every rerun. The tmp-copy escape is a NoSuchThing IOException (judged Deterministic by Removable, not a Hiccup retry) and falls under the documented write-port process-death semantics. Loud, no data loss, but contradicts the 'refuse early at plan time' intent of DESIGN.md:214/§14.
verdict.suggested_fix: Either lower `maxPathLen` so that abs' + 37 < 260 (i.e. 223), or add a plan-time validation in Pm.Plan/validatePlan that computes `length (root </> ".pm" </> "trash" </> T.unpack pid </> victimRel)` and the tmp name for Copy items and rejects the plan with a clear '路径过长' message; optionally special-case the Win32 error in moveBoundNoReplace's message (drop the '183=目标已存在' hint when the code is 3/206).

confirmed.title: scanRoot drops the previous catalog entry of any enumerated file whose stat or hash fails, collapsing "cannot determine" into "absent" for per-file failures
confirmed.summary: The F040 carry-over only preserves old entries under unenumerated subtrees. Files whose `statSnap` or `sha256File` threw are neither in `reused`/`newEntries` nor in `unknown`, so their old entries vanish from `srCatalog`. Commands.hs then saves unconditionally and the 3-generation rotation pushes the last complete snapshot down.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Lightroom holds `Raw\2025\…\DSC0100.ARW` open so open fails during the scan. `pm scan` prints `! …` and exits 1, but saves a catalog in which that entry no longer exists. `pm status` reports it as 新增, `pm backup` refuses with 主库与索引不一致, and `pm doctor --deep` no longer covers the file; two more scans rotate the last snapshot that contained it out.
confirmed.evidence: Scan.hs:265-269 statErrs; Scan.hs:308-312 hash Left → errs only; Scan.hs:347-348 `unknown = Map.filterWithKey (\k _ -> coversKey uncovered k) oldEntries; entries = entryMap (reused <> newEntries) `Map.union` unknown`. Commands.hs:253-258. Contrast Scan.hs:249-250 sweepCounts. DESIGN-COMMANDS:237; Scan.hs:233-238.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Scan.hs:265-269 `statted <- forM files (try . statSnap)`; `stats` keeps only Right, `statErrs` only reports. `split` (:275-280) sees only stats, so a stat-failed file is in neither `reused` nor `toHash`. Hash pass: hashOne exceptions go to `(rel, show ex) : errs` (:312), volatile to `vs` (:311) — neither produces an Entry. Final assembly :347-348: `unknown = Map.filterWithKey (\k _ -> coversKey uncovered k) oldEntries`, where `uncovered` comes solely from the walk (listTreeCov's third component: listDirectory failure :126, link-probe failure :145, root-id probe :171). An enumerated file that fails stat/hash is not covered, so its old entry is absent from `entries = entryMap (reused <> newEntries) \`Map.union\` unknown`; srCarried does not count it. Commands.hs:253 `saveCatalog root (srCatalog result)` writes unconditionally, then :268-269 prints issues and exits 1. Contrast the project's own per-file discipline in sweepCounts (Scan.hs:239-258, comments :230-238): 'stat 失败 … 是「查不出」，fail-closed 的去向是错误数而不是消失', pinned by caseFreshnessSweepDenied (ScanGuardTests.hs:201-214), and the F040 comment at Scan.hs:343-346: '「查不出」不是「不存在」：原样保留上次快照值，而不是让它们从快照消失、随即无条件落盘、三代轮转把完整快照顶掉——与 freshnessSweep 对同一情形的处置同一纪律'. scanRoot applies that discipline to unenumerated subtrees only. REPRO: old catalog has `Raw\2025\X\DSC0100.ARW`; a process holds it open without FILE_SHARE_READ (or an ACL deny(F), the fixture the suite itself uses). `pm scan`: walk lists it (pathIsSymbolicLink on deny(F) throws → :145 branch marks it uncovered, so the ACL case is actually carried; but for a sharing-violation lock GetFileAttributes/pathIsSymbolicLink succeed and only sha256File in hashOne throws) → hash Left → errs; entry dropped; catalog saved; exit 1. Next `pm status` after the lock is released: freshnessSweep finds the file on disk and absent from catalog → '新增 1' (Status.hs:262) although it is a known, unchanged file; `pm backup`'s mainFresh gate refuses with 'pm scan' (fail-closed, fine); `pm doctor --deep` and dedupe/versions silently omit the file; three scans while it stays locked rotate out the last snapshot that held it. DESIGN: DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:237 documents carry-over only for '进不去的子树'; §6.7:437 documents dropping only for volatile files ('本轮不入索引'), so volatile is intended and excluded from this finding. No doc or test pins dropping on stat/hash IO failure (caseScanDeniedProbe starts from `Nothing` old catalog, ScanGuardTests.hs:283-293). The ACL-denied case is in fact carried via the link-probe branch, so the reachable shape is a sharing-violation/media read error at sha256File or a getFileSize/getModificationTime failure. Severity low: loud at scan (exit 1 with the path), no invariant breach, but the fail-closed philosophy ('can't determine' ≠ 'absent') and the project's own F040 reasoning are contradicted for per-file failures, yielding a misleading '新增' in pm status and silent loss of --deep coverage.
verdict.corrected_summary: scanRoot keeps old entries only for unenumerated subtrees (`unknown` from walk-level `uncovered`); an enumerated file whose statSnap or sha256File throws (sharing violation, media read error — an ACL deny(F) is actually carried because the link probe fails first) contributes nothing to `entries`, so its previous catalog entry disappears from the unconditionally saved snapshot and from srCarried. This collapses 'could not read' into 'not present' for per-file failures, inconsistent with sweepCounts' per-file '错误口不算消失' rule and the F040 subtree rule; effects are a misleading '新增' in pm status once readable again, silent exclusion from doctor --deep/dedupe/versions, and rotation-out after three failing scans. Volatile files are documented as intentionally not indexed and are not part of this defect.
verdict.suggested_fix: In scanRoot, treat `statErrs` and `hashErrs` paths as '查不出': `unknown = Map.filterWithKey (\k _ -> coversKey uncovered k || k `Set.member` failedKeys) oldEntries` (with failedKeys = stat-failed ∪ hash-exception rels, excluding volatiles), count them in srCarried, and add a test seeded with an old catalog where sha256File fails for one file (e.g. a handle opened with FILE_SHARE_NONE) asserting the entry survives.

confirmed.title: GET /api/plans and POST /api/plans/prune hit GHC's in-process single-writer file lock while POST /api/apply is running: journal.ndjson reported as untrusted ('人工核查') and every plan as 未执行
confirmed.summary: During `POST /api/apply` the executing thread holds `.pm/journal.ndjson` open in ReadWriteMode for the whole batch. GHC's base enforces a per-process multiple-reader/single-writer lock, so any concurrent `GET /api/plans` or `POST /api/plans/prune` in the same process calling readJournal → openStateRead → openBinaryFile ReadMode fails with `ResourceBusy "file is locked"`. readPmState does not treat ResourceBusy specially, so it returns `Left "… 无法可信读取（…）——人工核查"`, which the plans endpoint returns as a journal error and folds into an empty execution map.
confirmed.failure_scenario: User clicks 执行 (POST /api/apply inside withJournal for minutes), then switches pages and comes back (GET /api/plans). readJournal → 'file is locked' → response errors contain a 'manual check' warning and every plan, including ones executed earlier, is labelled 未执行 until the apply finishes. || User presses 5 / 重新载入 during the apply: table gets the row "⚠ 装不出来的计划：journal：…无法可信读取（... file is locked）——人工核查"; 清理已执行/失效 deletes nothing. Same for the vault root journal during a vault-push apply.
confirmed.evidence: Win.hs:367-369/355 `openStateAppendTail fp = do h <- openBoundTo ReadWriteMode fp` → Win.hs:399 `openBinaryFile fp mode` (Journal.hs:274-284 `bracket (openStateAppendTail fp) …`, held across execItems in Exec.hs:114-166). Win.hs:432-434 `openStateRead`; Config.hs:434-445 `Left e | isDoesNotExistError e -> Right Nothing | otherwise -> Left (… " 无法可信读取（" <> show e <> "）——人工核查")`. Serve.hs:328-340 apply holds only seApplyLock; Serve.hs:388-398 `(mes, mwarns) <- readJournal (cfgMainPath cfg)`; :403 `runs = planExecs (mes <> ves)`; :406 staleOf; Plan.hs prunePlans `victims <- if null warns then …`. Config.hs:639 comment; test/SortGuardTests.hs:526. gui/ui/app.js:275.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Exec.hs:166-167 `withJournal root $ \j -> do (outs, restoredIxs) <- execItems …` keeps the journal handle open for the whole batch; withJournal (Journal.hs:85-95) → withPmStateAppend' (Config.hs:465-470) → openStateAppendTail (Win.hs:367-369) → `openBoundTo ReadWriteMode fp` → Win.hs:407 `openBinaryFile fp mode` (System.IO, Win.hs:68). GHC's base `mkFD` calls the RTS `lockFile` for every regular file opened through openFile/openBinaryFile and enforces a per-process multiple-reader/single-writer lock keyed on (volume serial, file index) on Windows; a ReadMode open while a ReadWriteMode handle is live in the same process fails with `IOError ResourceBusy "openFile" "file is locked"`. The project itself relies on and documents exactly this behaviour on Windows: test/SortGuardTests.hs:389-393 and :526 ('GHC 句柄锁不许「已开写」的文件再被开读，抛 ResourceBusy'), and withRootLock maps the same ResourceBusy via isAlreadyInUseError (Config.hs:651-653). readJournal (Journal.hs:110-125) → readPmState (Config.hs:433-445) → `openStateRead` → `openBoundTo ReadMode` → `openBinaryFile`; readPmState only special-cases isDoesNotExistError, everything else becomes `Left (… " 无法可信读取（" <> show e <> "）——人工核查")`. Serve.hs:323 the apply handler holds only `seApplyLock`; GET /api/plans (Serve.hs:388-410) and POST /api/plans/prune (Serve.hs:427-437 → Plan.hs:438-445) do not take it, and warp serves requests concurrently. The GUI can issue them mid-apply: app.js:640-660 `busy()` only covers vault/archive, so pressing 5, clicking a tab, or #btn-plans-reload (app.js:666) calls loadPlans while applyPlan is awaiting. REPRO: user clicks 执行 on a 200-item import plan → apply thread is inside withJournal for minutes → user presses 5 → GET /api/plans → readJournal (cfgMainPath) → openBinaryFile ReadMode → lockFile returns -1 → ResourceBusy → readPmState Left "<main>/.pm/journal.ndjson 无法可信读取（…: openFile: resource busy (file is locked)）——人工核查" → Serve.hs:394-410: `mes = []`, `runs` empty, `staleOf` returns False, `errors` gets ("journal", that message) → app.js:275 renders the row「⚠ 装不出来的计划：journal：…file is locked…——人工核查」and every plan, including ones executed days ago, shows 未执行. Prune at the same moment: Plan.hs:445 `victims <- if null warns then … else pure []` → deletes nothing and reports the same 人工核查 warning. After the apply finishes the next reload is normal. DESIGN: Serve.hs:390-393 comment says a journal read failure is folded as fail-closed with the reason in errors — but that reasoning is about untrusted files, not a benign in-process transient; nothing in DESIGN*/REVIEW-LOG*/README rules on serving /api/plans during /api/apply. Fail-closed direction, no data impact, transient — low severity, but the「人工核查」wording for a self-inflicted lock is misleading.
verdict.corrected_summary: While POST /api/apply is executing, the same serve process holds `.pm/journal.ndjson` open in ReadWriteMode (withJournal across execItems). GHC's in-process single-writer file lock makes any concurrent GET /api/plans or POST /api/plans/prune fail in readPmState with ResourceBusy 'file is locked', which is reported as「无法可信读取（…）——人工核查」and folds the execution map to empty, so all plans (including previously executed ones) are labelled 未执行 and prune deletes nothing until the apply completes. Benign and self-healing, but the wording tells the user to investigate a non-problem.
verdict.suggested_fix: Two trivial layers: (1) in Config.hs readPmState add a branch `| isAlreadyInUseError e -> Left (path <> " 正被本进程的另一操作打开（计划执行中？），稍后重试")` so the ResourceBusy case is worded as a transient rather than 人工核查 (still Left, still fail-closed); (2) in the /api/plans and /api/plans/prune handlers, `tryReadMVar (seApplyLock env)`; when it is Nothing, skip readJournal and return errors [("journal","计划正在执行中（POST /api/apply），执行态待完成后刷新")] so the GUI shows an explicit reason instead of a manual-check warning.

confirmed.title: GET /api/plans gates stale detection on BOTH roots' journal warnings while prune/CLI gate per root
confirmed.summary: `staleOf p mr = if null mwarns && null vwarns then planStale p mr else pure False` disables the stale-draft judgement for every plan when either journal has a warning, but `prunePlans` and `runPlanList` gate per root. The GUI list and its `state` wording therefore disagree with the CLI and with what the GUI's own 'clear executed/stale' button deletes.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Vault journal has a torn tail; main journal is clean. A never-executed main-root import draft whose sources are gone: `pm plan list` says 已失效（源已不在）, but GET /api/plans returns stale=false / 未执行 with the 执行 button. The user clicks 清理已执行/失效 → prunePlans judges main per-root → deletes that plan although the page had just labelled it 未执行.
confirmed.evidence: Serve.hs:399-405; Pm/Plan.hs:438-450 prunePlans per root; runPlanList `st <- if null warns then planStale p mr else pure False`; gui/ui/app.js:239-243, 415-425; DESIGN-GUI.md §11.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Serve.hs:398-405 `runs = planExecs (mes <> ves)` and `staleOf p mr = if null mwarns && null vwarns then planStale p mr else pure False` — one combined gate over both roots' warnings, applied to plans from both `ps` and `vps`. Plan.hs:438-445 prunePlans loops `forM (planRoots cfg)` and gates `victims <- if null warns then filterM cleanable ps else pure []` per root; Plan.hs:453-463 runPlanList likewise `st <- if null warns then planStale p mr else pure False -- journal 有告警不判失效（同 prune）` per root. The Serve.hs comment claims '与 prune 同一 fail-closed' but prune is per-root. REPRO: main journal clean, vault journal has a torn tail (JTornGap-less unparsable last line → readJournal warning). A never-executed main-root import draft whose 220 card sources are gone while the volume is present: `pm plan list` → main root warns=[] → planStale True → 「已失效（源已不在）」; GET /api/plans → vwarns non-empty → staleOf False → stale=false, state=「未执行」, GUI renders the 执行 button (app.js:302 `!isStale`) and no yellow banner; user clicks 清理已执行/失效 → prunePlans main root warns=[] → planStale True → deleted, although the page had just labelled it 未执行 and offered 执行. Same divergence the other way for vault plans when only the main journal warns. DESIGN: docs consistently say per root — DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:581 'journal 有告警的根不判', :582 'journal 有告警的根一份不删', DESIGN-GUI.md:69 'journal 有告警的根整根不删', README.md:518 'a root whose journal read warns is neither judged nor pruned', REVIEW-LOG.md:603 'journal 有告警的根不判、prune 整根不删' and 'CLI / prune / serve / GUI 四处同源'. The docs agree with the finder, and test/PlanExecTests caseStale only pins planStale/prunePlans, not the serve gate. Consequence is cosmetic and on the conservative side (GUI under-reports stale; executing a stale plan only yields per-item CONFLICT), so low.
verdict.corrected_summary: GET /api/plans disables the stale-draft judgement for plans of BOTH roots whenever EITHER journal has a warning (`null mwarns && null vwarns`), whereas `pm plan list` and `prunePlans` gate per root as the docs (DESIGN-COMMANDS §1.1.3, DESIGN-GUI §11, README) specify. With a warning in only one journal, the GUI shows a stale draft of the other root as 未执行 with an 执行 button while the CLI says 已失效 and the GUI's own 清理已执行/失效 deletes it.
verdict.suggested_fix: In the /api/plans handler compute per root like runPlanList: build `(ps, mwarns, planExecs mes)` and `(vps, vwarns, planExecs ves)` separately and use each root's own warnings/runs for its plans, e.g. `staleOf warns p mr = if null warns then planStale p mr else pure False` applied with `mwarns` to `ps` and `vwarns` to `vps` (the per-root `runs` map also matches the CLI's fold).

confirmed.title: classify resolves album names by bare file name over the whole 相册 subtree, so a same-named file in an album sub-directory shadows the flat album photo sent to the model
confirmed.summary: `byName = Map.fromList [(takeFileName (enPath e), e) | e <- …, inAlbum e]` keys on `takeFileName`, and `Map.fromList` keeps the last entry; `相册\sub\a.jpg` sorts after `相册\a.jpg` and wins. The names the GUI sends come from `listFlatPhotos` (flat only), so the suggestion is computed on a different image than the card the user sees.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Album contains `相册\IMG_0001.jpg` (NEW) and a stray `相册\old\IMG_0001.jpg`. User clicks AI 建议 → classify passes `相册\old\IMG_0001.jpg` to `claude -p`; the returned category/location are pre-filled on the card of the flat photo and later written to vault-notes.json for the wrong photo.
confirmed.evidence: ServeAi.hs:106-110; Pm/Vault.hs:128-136 listFlatPhotos; vault.js:189.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/ServeAi.hs:106-107 builds `byName = Map.fromList [(takeFileName (enPath e), e) | e <- Map.elems (catEntries cat), inAlbum e]` with `inAlbum e = take 1 (splitDirectories (enPath e)) == [albumTop] && enKind e == KindPhoto`. `inAlbum` only checks the FIRST path component, so any KindPhoto entry anywhere under `相册\` qualifies. The catalog is produced by `pm scan`, whose `listTreeCov` (src/Pm/Scan.hs:106-135) walks the whole root recursively (only dot-dirs skipped) and stores root-relative paths with native separators (Types.hs:126 'enPath is relative to its root, native separators'), so `相册\old\IMG_0001.jpg` is indexed as KindPhoto (kind is by extension, Types.hs:119-120). `Map.elems` yields entries in key order and `Map.fromList` keeps the LAST duplicate key. Nothing else filters: `isFlatName` (VaultHold.hs:89-90) is only applied to the REQUEST names, and the lookup is `Map.lookup n byName` (line 108). The vault side by contrast is explicitly flat: `listFlatPhotos` (Vault.hs:116-135) is non-recursive and Vault.hs:331 merely warns '相册下有子目录（平铺语义，不递归）', and the sha used when the note is saved is `freshSrcSha r n = freshShaAt (vrSrcDir r)` (Vault.hs:217-218), i.e. the FLAT file. REPRO: main root indexed with `相册\IMG_0001.jpg` (NEW) and `相册\old\IMG_0001.jpg`. Both pass `inAlbum`. Key order: common prefix `相册\`, then 'I' (0x49) < 'o' (0x6F), so the flat entry is emitted first and the `old\` entry last → `byName ! "IMG_0001.jpg"` = the sub-directory entry. GUI sends names from the flat card list (vault.js:189 `[...notes.keys()]`, which come from the flat vault report). Line 110: `resolveUnder root (enPath e)` → absolute path of `相册\old\IMG_0001.jpg`; no error is produced (name is flat, member of byName, jpg, resolvable, unique). Line 127: that path goes into `classifyPrompt`; `claude -p` reads the stray image. The reply is keyed by `name`=`IMG_0001.jpg`, which is in `wanted`, so it is kept (line 135) and vault.js:205-209 prefills it onto the flat photo's card; on save (vault.js:245-248 → POST /api/vault/notes) the record is stored under the flat name with the flat file's sha — data derived from a different image. The outcome is name-order dependent (a sub-dir named `Archive` would let the flat entry win), which confirms the lookup is not intentionally choosing anything. DESIGN: DESIGN-P8 §22.3 says classify `names` are '相册里的名字（NEW 或 HELD 都可）' and the whole vault/album contract is flat (DESIGN-P8 §21.1 `name` 平铺 basename; Vault.hs:116-118). No REVIEW-LOG entry or README limitation rules on this; test/ServeP8Tests.hs caseSuggestClassify only exercises a flat `a.jpg`. Severity low: it is an advisory suggestion the user still reviews (thumbnail and basis are shown), and it needs a stray same-named jpg in an album sub-directory, but the model is fed the wrong image and the user is not told.
verdict.corrected_summary: classify (ServeAi.hs:106-110) resolves the requested flat album names by `takeFileName` over every KindPhoto catalog entry whose first path component is `相册`, including files in album sub-directories that the vault/GUI flat semantics ignore; `Map.fromList` keeps the last entry in key order, so e.g. `相册\old\IMG_0001.jpg` ('o' > 'I') shadows `相册\IMG_0001.jpg` and its path is what is handed to `claude -p`, while the returned suggestion is prefilled on (and, if saved, recorded for) the flat photo. Which file wins depends only on code-point order of the sub-directory name versus the file name.
verdict.suggested_fix: Look the name up by its exact flat catalog key instead of by basename: replace the `byName` construction with `byName = Map.fromList [(n, e) | n <- names, Just e <- [Map.lookup (albumTop </> n) (catEntries cat)], enKind e == KindPhoto]` (import `(</>)` from System.FilePath; `catEntries` is keyed by `enPath` with native separators, see Types.hs:187 `entryMap`). All downstream checks (`Map.member n byName`, `resolveUnder root (enPath e)`) stay unchanged and the existing test (`a.jpg` in flat 相册) still passes.

confirmed.title: AI coordinate suggestions re-rendered with Haskell `show` emit scientific notation (e.g. "-1.5e-3") for |value| < 0.1, which is then prefilled and stored as the note's coordinates text
confirmed.summary: `normItem` re-serialises parsed coordinates as `T.pack (show la <> ", " <> show ln)`. GHC's `show :: Double` uses exponent form below 0.1. The GUI prefills that text, and on save it is written verbatim into `.pm/vault-notes.json` and exported by `pm vault notes --json`, whose documented format is plain decimal.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Model answers `"coordinates":"0.0523, -0.0917"`. `normItem` renders `"5.23e-2, -9.17e-2"`; vault.js prefills it; `noteFieldErrors` accepts it (Data.Text.Read.double parses exponents); the record lands in vault-notes.json and in `pm vault notes --json`.
confirmed.evidence: ServeAi.hs:184; VaultNote.hs:292-302 `parseCoordinates` uses `TR.signed TR.double`; vault.js:171, :222, :63; ServeVault.hs:154-157; DESIGN-P8.md:212/217.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/ServeAi.hs:184 `"coordinates" .= (aiCoordinates it >>= \c -> (\(la, ln) -> T.pack (show la <> ", " <> show ln)) <$> parseCoordinates c)`. `parseCoordinates` (VaultNote.hs:105-115) splits on ',', parses each half with `TR.signed TR.double` (Data.Text.Read.double accepts an optional exponent, e.g. `double "5.23e-2"` = Right (0.0523, "")), and range-checks −90..90 / −180..180. `show :: Double -> String` in GHC (Numeric.showFloat / floatToDigits) uses positional notation only for 0.1 <= |x| < 10^7 and exponent form otherwise: `show 0.0523 = "5.23e-2"`, `show (-0.0917) = "-9.17e-2"`, `show 0.0 = "0.0"`. There is no other formatting site; `Numeric.showFFloat` is not used anywhere in src/Pm (grep). REPRO: the model answers `{"name":"a.jpg","coordinates":"0.0523, -0.0917",...}` (a real location near the equator/prime meridian, e.g. Greenwich lng −0.0015 or Pontianak lat −0.02). parseCoordinates → Just (0.0523, -0.0917) → line 184 renders `"5.23e-2, -9.17e-2"`. vault.js:206 `if (it[k] && !n.inputs[k].value.trim()) n.inputs[k].value = it[k]` puts that text in the coordinates box. On '保存决定', vault.js:245 POSTs it verbatim to /api/vault/notes (ServeVault.hs:154-157 → shared `noteRequest`/`noteFieldErrors`, VaultNote.hs:144), which accepts it because parseCoordinates accepts exponents, and `normalizeFields` only strips whitespace, so `.pm/vault-notes.json` and `pm vault notes --json` / GET /api/vault/notes carry `"coordinates":"5.23e-2, -9.17e-2"`. DESIGN: DESIGN-P8 §21.1 documents the field as `"coordinates":"47.556533, 13.648033"` / `形如 <lat>, <lng>`; the classify prompt itself (ServeAi.hs:152) demands '十进制 "lat, lng"'; README.md:209 shows the same plain-decimal form. Nothing in DESIGN-P8 §22, REVIEW-LOG or README limitations says serve re-serialises coordinates or that exponent form is acceptable; the only pinned test value (`ServeP8Tests.hs:308`, `"47.5, 13.6"`) is in the positional range and so does not cover this. The defect is real but small: the values are numerically correct, the user sees the odd text before saving, and the downstream `/photo-publish` consumer (outside this repo) most likely parses it with a JS/Python float parser that accepts exponents. It is a contract/cosmetic mismatch, so low.
verdict.corrected_summary: normItem (ServeAi.hs:184) canonicalises the model's coordinates with Haskell `show`, which for any component with 0 < |v| < 0.1 produces exponent notation (`0.0523` → `5.23e-2`). That text is prefilled in the GUI, passes `noteFieldErrors` (TR.double accepts exponents) and is stored verbatim in `.pm/vault-notes.json` and exported by `pm vault notes --json`, contradicting the documented plain-decimal `<lat>, <lng>` form (DESIGN-P8 §21.1, README:209, and the prompt's own '十进制'). Numerically correct, cosmetically/contractually wrong; only affects coordinates within 0.1° of the equator or prime meridian.
verdict.suggested_fix: Render with fixed-point formatting instead of `show`: `import Numeric (showFFloat)` and use `T.pack (showFFloat Nothing la "" <> ", " <> showFFloat Nothing ln "")` at ServeAi.hs:184 (`showFFloat Nothing 47.5 ""` = "47.5", so the existing test value is unchanged; `showFFloat Nothing 0.0523 ""` = "0.0523").

confirmed.title: POST /api/album/ignore reports a busy main-root lock as 400 '忽略清单未写入' instead of 409, unlike every other .pm record endpoint
confirmed.summary: `runAlbumIgnoreTo` returns exit code 2 both for validation failures and for `withRootLock` returning Nothing; the handler maps every non-zero code to `status400`. The sibling record endpoints (recordPost → 409) and /api/config (409) treat lock-busy as a conflict.
confirmed.failure_scenario: While POST /api/apply is executing (root lock held by the same serve) the user clicks 忽略: HTTP 400 「忽略清单没写入：忽略清单未写入 / 另一个 pm 正在写主库…」 — a client-error status for a transient conflict, and the message blames 'another pm' although it is this serve's own apply.
