confirmed.evidence: ServeAlbum.hs:69-74 `Right _ -> jsonR status400 [] (object ["error" .= "忽略清单未写入", "details" .= logs])`. Pm/Album.hs:404-409 `Nothing -> sink "另一个 pm 正在写主库…" >> pure 2`. ServeVault.hs:193-197 `Left (msg, 4) -> err status409 msg`.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/ServeAlbum.hs:67-74 runs `runAlbumIgnoreTo` under `seVaultLock` and maps `Right 0 -> 200`, any other `Right _ -> status400 {error:"忽略清单未写入", details:logs}`. src/Pm/Album.hs:398-409: `runAlbumIgnoreTo` returns 2 for parse errors, for `requireMain` failure, and for `withRootLock root txn` returning Nothing (`sink "另一个 pm 正在写主库（.pm/lock 被占用）——稍后重试" >> pure 2`); inside txn it also returns 2 for missing catalog, unreadable ignore list, validation errors and `writeIgnores` failure. So every failure class collapses to one code and the handler cannot distinguish lock-busy. The sibling shell src/Pm/ServeVault.hs:163-197 (`recordPost`, documented in its comment as the mapping for 主库侧记录文件写端点: 400 校验 / 403 不可写 / 404 身份 / 409 锁忙) uses `withVaultTxn` (src/Pm/VaultCmd.hs:75) which tags lock-busy as code 4 and maps it to `status409`. `POST /api/config` likewise returns 409 on lock busy (src/Pm/Serve.hs:285). src/Pm/Config.hs:643-661 `withRootLock` opens `.pm/lock` via `openStateLock` (write mode) — a second write-open of the same file in the same GHC process raises an `isAlreadyInUseError` (RTS single-writer file lock), so an in-process holder also yields `Nothing`, not an exception. REPRO: serve started with --allow-apply; user clicks 执行 on an import plan (plRootPath = main root). src/Pm/Serve.hs:325-341 takes `seApplyLock` (not `seVaultLock`) and calls `executePlanNowWith`; src/Pm/Exec.hs:114 holds `withRootLock root` for the whole execution. While that runs, the user clicks 忽略 on the archive page → `POST /api/album/ignore {"ignore":["E1/a.jpg"]}` → `seVaultLock` is free → `runAlbumIgnoreTo`: parse ok, `requireMain` ok, `withRootLock` → `openStateLock` throws in-use → `pure Nothing` → sink lock message, return 2 → handler line 74 → HTTP 400 `{"error":"忽略清单未写入","details":["另一个 pm 正在写主库（.pm/lock 被占用）——稍后重试"]}`. gui/ui/archive.js:128 shows「忽略清单没写入：忽略清单未写入\n另一个 pm 正在写主库…稍后重试」. The same transient condition on /api/vault/hold, /api/vault/notes and /api/config yields 409. Wrong outcome (status class) reached. DESIGN: docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:393 states the project convention for this record-file transaction shape: 「锁被占用时不排队，直接告知（CLI exit 2 / API 409）」; docs/DESIGN-GUI.md:199 「拿不到锁一律拒（API 409）」 for the config lock. docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:572 for `pm album ignore` only fixes the CLI side (exit 2) and says nothing about the API code; DESIGN-P8 §23.1 and DESIGN-GUI:61 do not document a status mapping for /api/album/ignore, and no REVIEW-LOG entry rules on it. test/ServeP8Tests.hs:167-193 pins only 403 / 400-for-bad-object / 200, not the lock-busy code. So the docs side with the finder's convention rather than with the code. User-visible impact is limited: the GUI ignores the status and prints the message, which does say 稍后重试, so the user is not steered wrong — hence low severity. The secondary complaint (message says 另一个 pm although it is this serve's own apply) is not specific to this endpoint: the identical text is emitted by `withVaultTxn` for the 409 endpoints the finder holds up as the model, so I do not count it as part of the defect.
verdict.corrected_summary: POST /api/album/ignore collapses every non-success outcome of runAlbumIgnoreTo (parse errors, requireMain failure, missing catalog, unreadable/unwritable ignore list, and main-root .pm/lock busy) into exit 2 → HTTP 400 "忽略清单未写入". Concretely, while POST /api/apply is executing (Exec.hs:114 holds the main-root lock under seApplyLock, which does not interlock with seVaultLock), a 忽略 click returns 400 with the lock-busy line in details, whereas the sibling record endpoints (/api/vault/hold, /api/vault/notes via recordPost, /api/config) return 409 for the same transient condition as DESIGN-COMMANDS:393 / DESIGN-GUI:199 describe. The GUI only displays the message (which already says 稍后重试), so impact is an API status-class inconsistency, not a wrong user action.
verdict.suggested_fix: Make lock-busy distinguishable: in Pm.Album have runAlbumIgnoreTo return a distinct code for `withRootLock` Nothing (e.g. 4, matching withVaultTxn's convention), keep `runAlbumIgnore` (CLI wrapper) mapping 4 → 2 so the documented CLI exit 2 is preserved, and in ServeAlbum.hs map `Right 4 -> err status409 <lock message>` before the `Right _ -> status400` catch-all. Optionally also map requireMain/catalog-missing → 404 and writeIgnores failure → 403 to match recordPost, and add a ServeP8Tests case that pre-holds .pm/lock and asserts 409.

confirmed.title: DRIFT-only push-plan response tells the GUI user to manually git add/commit/push although nothing will land
confirmed.summary: `POST /api/vault/push-plan` returns `gitSteps = gitStepsLines cfg vault pid (planCategories plan)`. For a pure adjudication plan (only DRIFT items) `planCategories` is `[]`, so `vaultCommands` returns `Left "没有要 add 的类目"` and `gitStepsLines` renders the fallback 「请在 <vault> 里手动：git add <类目…> → git commit → git push」. The CLI and afterApply print git steps only when something landed (F029/F068). `caseServePushPlanDrift` never inspects `gitSteps`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: vault has `landscape/a.jpg` differing from 相册/a.jpg and no NEW. User clicks 「保存决定并生成推送计划」 → 200 with one NEEDS-DECISION item and `gitSteps` = [header, "（无法安全生成命令：没有要 add 的类目）", "请在 V:\\vault 里手动：git add … → git commit → git push"]. A user following it runs git add/commit/push on a vault where `pm apply` executed nothing.
confirmed.evidence: ServeVault.hs:100-103, :131; Vault.hs:517-521 planCategories; Vault.hs:501-510 gitStepsLines fallback; Publish.hs:141-144; gui/ui/vault.js:258; ServeWriteTests.hs:154-183.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/ServeVault.hs:131 computes `"gitSteps" .= gitStepsLines cfg (plRootPath plan) (plId plan) (planCategories plan)` unconditionally on the 200 path. src/Pm/Vault.hs:523-527 `planCategories` filters out every item whose status is `StNeedsDecision`, so a plan whose only items are DRIFT yields `[]`. src/Pm/Vault.hs:510-518 `gitStepsLines` always emits the header line and then calls `Publish.vaultCommands`; src/Pm/Publish.hs:141-142 has `_ | null cats -> Left "没有要 add 的类目"`, so the Left branch renders `"    （无法安全生成命令：没有要 add 的类目）"` and `"    请在 " <> vaultDir <> " 里手动：git add <类目…> → git commit → git push"`. By contrast the two execution-side consumers guard on landed items: src/Pm/Apply.hs:197-198 `unless (null (landedItems results)) $ mapM_ sink (gitStepsLines … (resultCategories results))` and src/Pm/Vault.hs:614-618 `PrRun _ rs | not (null (landedItems rs)) -> …`. No such guard exists in ServeVault.hs; nothing in the types prevents an empty category list reaching gitStepsLines. gui/ui/vault.js:258 appends the block whenever `j.gitSteps.length` is truthy — which is always, because the header line is unconditional. REPRO: vault has landscape/a.jpg with bytes differing from 相册/a.jpg, no NEW (exactly the fixture of test/ServeWriteTests.hs:154-183). GUI at vault.js:107-110 shows the DRIFT-only hint and enables the button; user clicks → `POST /api/vault/push-plan {"assignments":[]}`. ServeVault.hs:97: `null as && null (vdDrift …)` is False → otherwise; `checkAssignments r []` = [] (Vault.hs:626, no pairs, no dup); `vaultPushItems r []` = one `(OpCopy … ("landscape" </> "a.jpg") …, StNeedsDecision …)` (Vault.hs:657-663); mkVaultPushPlan/requireWritable/savePlan succeed (the test asserts 200 and one NEEDS-DECISION item). `planCategories plan` = [] → `vaultCommands cfg "V:\\vault" [] "photos: pm vault push <pid>"` = Left "没有要 add 的类目" → gitSteps = [header, "    （无法安全生成命令：没有要 add 的类目）", "    请在 V:\\vault 里手动：git add <类目…> → git commit → git push"]. vault.js:258 renders the banner: "已生成推送计划 …（1 项）… 执行：pm apply <id> … 执行后的 git 步骤：" followed by those three lines. Yet `pm apply <id>` on this plan executes nothing (ONotExecuted for NEEDS-DECISION; test/VaultTests.hs:425-446 pins that CLI/afterApply print NO git steps in this case). The wrong outcome is reached: the GUI banner instructs a manual git add/commit/push for a vault in which nothing has changed. DESIGN: docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:363-367 says the add list comes from landed items, "一项都没落位则整段 git 步骤不打", and that the GUI preview takes categories from the plan face via planCategories; docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:491 rules "全部待裁决 → 无 git 步骤"; Vault.hs:520-522 (F029) says NEEDS-DECISION items are excluded from the preview precisely because they cannot land before adjudication. The `Left` fallback text in gitStepsLines is documented (DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:371-372, Vault.hs:508-509) for the "路径嵌不进命令行" case, not for "nothing to add". No doc or REVIEW-LOG entry rules the manual-git fallback as intended for an empty preview; caseServePushPlanDrift (ServeWriteTests.hs:154-183) never inspects gitSteps, so no test pins it. Refuting would require a guard or ruling that does not exist. Severity low: cosmetic/misleading message, no data at risk from pm itself; a user who follows it would at worst run a no-op add/commit or push unrelated pending changes in their own vault repo.
verdict.corrected_summary: `POST /api/vault/push-plan` always renders `gitSteps` from `planCategories plan`, and for a DRIFT-only (pure adjudication) plan that list is `[]`, so `gitStepsLines` falls through to `vaultCommands`' `Left "没有要 add 的类目"` and emits the manual-fallback lines ("（无法安全生成命令：没有要 add 的类目）" / "请在 <vault> 里手动：git add <类目…> → git commit → git push"). The GUI (vault.js:258) shows this under "执行后的 git 步骤" because the unconditional header makes `gitSteps` never empty. This contradicts the documented contract that git steps are only given when something lands (DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:364-367, :491; F029) and the CLI/afterApply guards (Apply.hs:197, Vault.hs:616). Misleading message only; no invariant is violated.
verdict.suggested_fix: In src/Pm/ServeVault.hs:131 emit an empty list when the preview has no categories, e.g. `"gitSteps" .= (let cs = planCategories plan in if null cs then [] else gitStepsLines cfg (plRootPath plan) (plId plan) cs)`; vault.js:258 already handles an empty array. Optionally add an assertion to caseServePushPlanDrift that `gitSteps` is `[]`.

confirmed.title: hardErrors treats the designed 'pm 状态目录…不进入' skip as an enumeration failure → exit code 0→1 and '未能枚举' warning for a fully enumerated source
confirmed.summary: listTreeCov records the deliberate skip of a directory containing root-id.json as an error row `(relPath, "pm 状态目录（内含 root-id.json），源遍历不进入")` and does not add it to the uncovered list. hardErrors only filters `reparseSkipNote`, so foldHardErrors promotes a clean exit 0 to 1 and prints `⚠ 源里有 1 处未能枚举…退出码 1` for a directory pm decided on purpose not to enter, contradicting DESIGN-COMMANDS ('junction 跳过仍是 0'). SortGuardTests.caseSourceSkipsPmDir never checks the exit code.
confirmed.failure_scenario: User points `pm sort E:\Photography` at a backup-drive root (or any folder with a nested pm root). All photos already at destination → `✓ 没有需要归位的新照片`, then `⚠ 源里有 1 处未能枚举（见上「遍历时出错」）…退出码 1`; the command (and the GUI) reports failure although nothing was left unenumerated. || `pm sort D:\old-lib` (still has `.pm\root-id.json`): survey/plan ends with exit 1 instead of 0; scripts/GUI keying on exit 0 treat a clean run as a partial one.
confirmed.evidence: Scan.hs:172/186-188 `_ -> pure ([], [(relPath, "pm 状态目录（内含 root-id.json），源遍历不进入")], [])` (third component empty); SortSource.hs:102 `sfErrors = …`; SortSource.hs:204-205 `hardErrors = filter ((/= reparseSkipNote) . snd)`; SortSource.hs:207-214 foldHardErrors; Sort.hs:392/433/437/563/576 call sites; Sort.hs:293-296 bucket title. docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:492 'junction 跳过仍是 0'. test/SortGuardTests.hs:332 caseSourceSkipsPmDir asserts only the note in sfErrors.

verdict.reasoning:
CODE: src/Pm/Scan.hs:172 (WalkDotDirs branch of listTreeCov) returns `pure ([], [(relPath, "pm 状态目录（内含 root-id.json），源遍历不进入")], [])` — the skip is recorded as an error row and the third (uncovered) component is empty, whereas the genuinely-unknown case at Scan.hs:171 (ProbeUnknown) DOES put relPath in uncovered. listTreeWith (Scan.hs:95-96) drops the coverage list, so SortSource.listSource (line 74, 102) puts the row into sfErrors verbatim. SortSource.hs:204-205 `hardErrors = filter ((/= reparseSkipNote) . snd)` excludes only the junction note (Scan.hs:50-51 `reparseSkipNote = "symlink/reparse point skipped"`); foldHardErrors (SortSource.hs:209-214) lifts code 0 to 1 and prints `⚠ 源里有 %d 处未能枚举（见上「遍历时出错」）——不当作整卡都看过了，退出码 1` whenever `hard` is non-empty. Callers: Sort.hs:437 `foldHardErrors putStrLn (ssErrors sv) 0` in renderSortSurvey (survey form always feeds 0) and Sort.hs:563 `foldHardErrors sink (sfErrors sf) code` in runSortPlanTo. No caller filters the pm-state note beforehand; no type prevents it. Serve GET /api/sort/survey (Serve.hs:302-314) returns surveyJson without foldHardErrors, so the GUI survey page is unaffected; POST /api/sort/plan goes through runSortPlanTo (Serve.hs:324) and the GUI (app.js:633) keys on planId, showing the log (which then contains the bogus ⚠ line) rather than the code.

REPRO: on-disk `D:\old-lib\.pm\root-id.json` (any content) + `D:\old-lib\DCIM\a.ARW`. Run `pm sort D:\old-lib` (survey form). withSourceQ → listSource → listTreeWith WalkDotDirs: for name `.pm`, pathIsSymbolicLink=False, isDir=True, probeName(root-id.json)=NamePlain → falls to `_ ->` at Scan.hs:172 → errs = [(".pm", "pm 状态目录…不进入")]. sfErrors = [("D:\\old-lib\\.pm", …)]. renderSortSurvey prints `遍历错误 1 个`, reportAccounting prints bucket `遍历时出错 1 个（reparse point / 路径过长 / 读不到）: D:\old-lib\.pm — pm 状态目录（内含 root-id.json），源遍历不进入` (Sort.hs:293-296), then Sort.hs:437 foldHardErrors putStrLn errs 0: hard = errs (note ≠ reparseSkipNote) → prints `⚠ 源里有 1 处未能枚举…退出码 1` and returns 1. So the survey form exits 1 UNCONDITIONALLY for any source that is a pm root, even though every user file was enumerated. Plan form: same source with a.ARW already in staging → buildPlan returns 0 with `✓ 没有需要归位的新照片`, then line 563 lifts it to 1 with the same warning. Wrong outcome reached.

DESIGN: docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:492 defines the contract as `子树列不出（ACL 拒）→ 退出 1 …；junction 跳过仍是 0` — i.e. exit 1 is for subtrees pm could not enumerate, design-internal skips stay 0. Scan.hs:101-104 (listTreeCov doc) explicitly classifies the pm state dir together with real links and over-long paths as `确定性的跳过（真链接、超长路径、pm 状态目录）不在其中：那是「知道它不该进索引」，不是「查不出」` — the code's own coverage model says this is not an un-enumerated subtree, and the empty third component at line 172 (vs. non-empty at 171 for ProbeUnknown) implements exactly that. REVIEW-LOG-1B.md:490-493 (codex 27 #3) rules the .pm skip as `不进 .pm，但记一条不静默` — a note, not a failure. Nothing in DESIGN*.md, REVIEW-LOG*.md (F054 appears only in the mutation table, REVIEW-LOG-4.md:353) or README 465-553 says a pm-root source should exit 1. Tests: test/SortGuardTests.hs:72 checks hardErrors only against reparseSkipNote vs a listing failure; caseSortErrorsExit (lines 78-101) exercises junction and ACL-denied fixtures only; caseSourceSkipsPmDir (312-332) asserts only that the note is in sfErrors and never checks the exit code. So no test pins exit 1 for this case and the docs agree with the finder. Not refuted.
verdict.corrected_summary: When the sort source is (or contains) a pm root, listTreeCov records the deliberate non-entry of the directory holding root-id.json as an sfErrors row (Scan.hs:172) with an empty uncovered component, but SortSource.hardErrors (line 205) only exempts reparseSkipNote, so foldHardErrors lifts a clean exit 0 to 1 and prints '⚠ 源里有 1 处未能枚举…退出码 1'. The survey form (`pm sort <src>`, Sort.hs:437) therefore always exits 1 for a pm-root source, and the plan form (Sort.hs:563) turns '✓ 没有需要归位的新照片' / a fully-executed --go run into exit 1, plus the item is listed under the misleading bucket title 'reparse point / 路径过长 / 读不到'. This contradicts DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:492 (exit 1 only for subtrees that could not be enumerated; design-internal skips stay 0) and the listTreeCov doc comment (Scan.hs:101-104) that classifies the pm-state-dir skip as deterministic, not 'unenumerated'. The ProbeUnknown variant (Scan.hs:171, root-id.json existence unknown) is correctly a hard error and must stay one. GUI impact is limited to the spurious ⚠ line in the plan log (survey endpoint bypasses foldHardErrors; app.js keys on planId).
verdict.suggested_fix: In Pm/Scan.hs define the literal once, e.g. `pmStateDirSkipNote :: String; pmStateDirSkipNote = "pm 状态目录（内含 root-id.json），源遍历不进入"`, use it at Scan.hs:172 and export it; in Pm/SortSource.hs change `hardErrors = filter ((/= reparseSkipNote) . snd)` to `hardErrors = filter ((`notElem` [reparseSkipNote, pmStateDirSkipNote]) . snd)` (leave the ProbeUnknown '存在性查不出' row as hard). Optionally extend the bucket title at Sort.hs:295 to mention 'pm 状态目录'. Add to caseSortErrorsExit a fixture writing `src\.pm\root-id.json` and asserting both forms still return 0, and extend the unit assertion at SortGuardTests.hs:72. (A more principled alternative is to have listSource call listTreeCov and derive hard errors from the uncovered list, but that is a larger change.)

confirmed.title: stagingEventOf mis-parses the documented `To-Be-Sync'd\Raw\<year>\<event>` layout (reports the year as the event) and ignores files directly under Raw/Processed
confirmed.summary: Pm.Import accepts two Raw staging layouts. Status derives the staging-event list with a fixed component pattern `(top : sub : event : _ : _)`, so for the year layout `event` is the year directory: all events under one year collapse into a single 'event' named e.g. "2026". A file directly under `To-Be-Sync'd\Raw\` (3 components) is counted by stagingArchivedSummary but yields no event, so status can print no staging line and exit 0 while `pm import` reports 无法识别的暂存布局 and exits 1.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Staging holds To-Be-Sync'd\Raw\2026\26-06-Hallstatt\a.arw and To-Be-Sync'd\Raw\2026\26-07-Wien\b.arw. `pm status` prints `⚠ 暂存区 1 个事件未归档: ["2026"]` instead of 2 events; the GUI shows '暂存区 1 个事件未归档'. || GET /api/status returns stagingEvents ["2026"]; the redundant-archive branch likewise reports '1 个事件'.
confirmed.evidence: src/Pm/Status.hs:278-282 `stagingEventOf rel = case splitDirectories rel of (top : sub : event : _ : _) | top == stagingTop && sub `elem` ["Raw", "Processed"] -> Just event; _ -> Nothing`; src/Pm/Import.hs:66-88 route/routeRaw `(y : event : rest@(_ : _)) | isYearDir y`; docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:119-122; Status.hs:139, 220/223; gui/ui/app.js:118-120.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Status.hs:278-282 `stagingEventOf rel = case splitDirectories rel of (top : sub : event : _ : _) | top == stagingTop && sub `elem` ["Raw","Processed"] -> Just event; _ -> Nothing` uses a fixed positional pattern: the 3rd component is always taken as the event name and paths with fewer than 4 components yield Nothing. src/Pm/Import.hs:66-88 `route`/`routeRaw` explicitly accepts two Raw layouts: `(y : event : rest@(_ : _)) | isYearDir y` (year layer, event is the 4th path component) and `(event : rest@(_ : _))` (flat); docs/DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:119-122 documents both (`To-Be-Sync'd\Raw\[<年>\]<事件>`), and test/PlannerTests.hs:117,121,154,560 exercise the year layout for import. There is no guard elsewhere: Status.hs:139 feeds every catalog key through stagingEventOf, and `stagingArchivedSummary` (Import.hs:187-197) counts every `To-Be-Sync'd\*` entry outside 待修改 regardless of depth, so the file count and the event list are computed with different notions of 'staging'. No test references stagingEventOf/isStagingEvents (grep test/*.hs: only runStatus exit-code tests). REPRO 1: catalog keys `To-Be-Sync'd/Raw/2026/26-06-Hallstatt/a.arw` and `To-Be-Sync'd/Raw/2026/26-07-Wien/b.arw`, no archive copies. splitDirectories gives 5 components; pattern binds event="2026" for both; Set.fromList → ["2026"]; Status.hs:223 prints `⚠ 暂存区 1 个事件未归档: ["2026"]`; /api/status (Status.hs:112) returns stagingEvents ["2026"], gui/ui/app.js:120 and archive.js:31 display '1 个事件夹 · 2 文件 …2026'. Import.hs:80-84 would route both correctly as two distinct events. Exit code (Status.hs:170) is still 1 and the '→ pm import' hint is still right, so only the count/name is wrong. REPRO 2: catalog key `To-Be-Sync'd/Raw/a.arw` only (3 components). stagingEventOf → Nothing, stagingEvents = [], Status.hs:215 prints nothing about staging, code = 0 (if nothing else pending) while nStaging = 1 from stagingArchivedSummary is silently dropped; `pm import` (Import.hs:87 `_ -> Nothing` → irUnrecognized; Commands.hs:527-528, 542) prints '无法识别的暂存布局' and exits 1. Same for `To-Be-Sync'd/foo.jpg`. DESIGN: docs/DESIGN.md:238 says status must show 'staging 待归档' with a per-problem next-step; DESIGN.md:26 records the real library has a `To-Be-Sync'd\Raw\2026\` directory (empty at baseline), so the year layout is a real, supported shape (Import deliberately accepts it; pm sort itself writes only the flat layout, Sort.hs:635). No REVIEW-LOG entry, README 465-553 limitation, or comment near the site rules this intended; no test pins it. The finder's reading matches the code and the docs contradict the code, so not refuted. Severity: low — wrong count/label in a message/JSON field, exit code and next-step hint unaffected in scenario 1; scenario 2 is an edge shape (files loose under Raw/ or the staging top) where status is silent instead of pointing at import.
verdict.corrected_summary: Pm.Status.stagingEventOf derives the staging-event list from a fixed component position (3rd component after To-Be-Sync'd\<Raw|Processed>) and requires ≥4 components, while Pm.Import.route accepts both `Raw\<event>` and `Raw\<year>\<event>` layouts (documented in DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:119-122, tested in PlannerTests). For the year layout every event under one year collapses into a single pseudo-event named after the year ('1 个事件未归档: ["2026"]' in pm status, /api/status stagingEvents, and the GUI archive/home cards), and staging files with fewer than 4 components (e.g. To-Be-Sync'd\Raw\x.arw) are counted by stagingArchivedSummary but produce no event, so status prints no staging line and can exit 0 while pm import reports them as 无法识别 and exits 1. Exit code and the '→ pm import' hint are correct in the year-layout case, so the impact is a wrong count/name (cosmetic) plus a silent edge case.
verdict.suggested_fix: Make stagingEventOf mirror Import's layout rules: `(top : "Raw" : y : event : _ : _) | top == stagingTop, isYearDir y -> Just event` before the existing clause (export isYearDir from Pm.Import or inline `length y == 4 && all isDigit y`); optionally map any other `To-Be-Sync'd\*` entry outside 待修改 that yields no event to a sentinel such as "(无法识别)" so status still prints a staging line / exit 1 for shapes import will reject. No change to stagingArchivedSummary or the JSON contract needed.

confirmed.title: pm vault push no-item hint counts UNPUSHABLE .png as NEW to push (N4 same-shape regression)
confirmed.summary: In the no-plan branch of `runVaultPush` the hint uses `newActive r` (NEW − HELD) rather than `newAssignable r` (which additionally drops non-jpg). The N4 fix switched `renderHuman` to `newAssignable` for exactly this reason, but the push-side hint was left on `newActive`, so a .png-only NEW set prints '1 个 NEW 待分类：pm vault push --category …' — following that advice yields exit 2 'UNPUSHABLE'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Album contains only `c.png` not yet in vault. `pm vault push` → prints '→ 1 个 NEW 待分类：pm vault push --category <类目> <文件…>'. User runs `pm vault push --category landscape c.png` → '✗ c.png 是 UNPUSHABLE（写路径只收 jpg/jpeg）' exit 2. `pm vault status` for the same state correctly shows only the ✋ UNPUSHABLE line. || With mixed jpg/png the count is also wrong.
confirmed.evidence: src/Pm/Vault.hs:600-603 `unless (null (newActive r)) $ do putStrLn ("  → " <> show (length (newActive r)) <> " 个 NEW 待分类…")` vs Vault.hs:399/441 renderHuman uses `newAssignable r`; N4 comment :204-209/226-231; `newAssignable = filter pushableExt . newActive` (:232); checkAssignments (:640) rejects non-jpg. docs/REVIEW-LOG.md N4 row.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Vault.hs:598-603 — in the `null allItems` branch: `unless (null (newActive r)) $ do putStrLn ("  → " <> show (length (newActive r)) <> " 个 NEW 待分类：pm vault push --category <类目> <文件…>…")`. `newActive` (:226) = vdNew − held; `newAssignable` (:232) = `filter pushableExt . newActive`. `renderHuman` (:441) already uses `newAssignable` for its "→ pm vault push --category" line, and `checkAssignments` (:643) rejects `not (pushableExt f)` with "是 UNPUSHABLE（写路径只收 jpg/jpeg）". REPRO: album contains only `c.png`, vault categories empty. computeVault': listFlatPhotos includes .png (photoExtFold, VaultCore.hs:55) → srcNames=[c.png]; vaultDiff → vdNew=["c.png"]; unpushable=[("c.png","相册")]; held=[] → newActive=["c.png"], newAssignable=[]. `pm vault push` (mCat=Nothing, files=[]) → sel = Right [] → checkAssignments r [] = [] → allItems = vaultPushItems r [] = [] <> [] = [] → prints "  → 1 个 NEW 待分类：pm vault push --category <类目> <文件…>" then "（无可执行项，未生成计划）", exit 1. User obeys: `pm vault push --category landscape c.png` → checkSel: c.png ∈ vdNew, not held, `not (pushableExt "c.png")` → "  ✗ c.png 是 UNPUSHABLE（写路径只收 jpg/jpeg）", exit 2. Wrong outcome reached: the hint counts and advises pushing a file the very same command must reject. With a.jpg + c.png the hint says 2 待分类 while only 1 is pushable. DESIGN: docs/REVIEW-LOG.md:497 (门禁二轮 N4) rules: "新谓词 Vault.newAssignable … CLI「→ push」行与 GUI /api/vault/new 的 new 都只用它"; this push-side "→ … pm vault push --category" line is such a CLI → push line and was left on `newActive`. The comment at :228-230 says the same. Test caseUnstablePushExit (test/VaultTests.hs:643-653) only asserts the "无可执行项" substring and exit code, so nothing pins the count; caseUnpushableMatchesPushGate pins the predicates but not this call site. The docs agree with the finder.
verdict.corrected_summary: In the no-plan branch of `runVaultPush` (Vault.hs:600-602) the "→ N 个 NEW 待分类：pm vault push --category …" hint is gated and counted with `newActive` instead of `newAssignable`, so an album whose only NEW files are .png (or a jpg/png mix) is told to push N files with --category, and following that advice for a .png is rejected by `checkAssignments` (:643) with exit 2. This is the same N4 wording contradiction that was fixed in `renderHuman` (:441) but missed here; the exit code (`hasDiffR`) is unaffected and correct.
verdict.suggested_fix: At Vault.hs:600-602 replace both uses of `newActive r` with `newAssignable r` (guard and count); optionally add a sibling line pointing UNPUSHABLE NEW items to `pm convert`. Extend caseUnstablePushExit or add a case with a .png-only album asserting the hint line is absent.

confirmed.title: Direct `pm vault push --apply` never refreshes the main-side vault cache, so `pm status` keeps showing the pushed photos as NEW
confirmed.summary: `Pm.Apply.afterApply` re-runs `computeVault True cfg` after a vault-push plan is applied via `pm apply`, but the CLI path `runVaultPush` → `runPlan plan` returns straight after execution without recomputing. The `.pm/vault-cache/meta.json` written before the push stays, and `pm status` reports a lag that no longer exists.
confirmed.failure_scenario: 3 NEW jpgs. `pm vault push --category landscape a.jpg b.jpg c.jpg --apply -y` → all land, exit 0. Immediately `pm status` → '⚠ vault 上次比对 <now> · 差异 3（NEW 3 / …）→ pm vault status'. The same sequence via `pm apply <id>` shows '无差异'.
confirmed.evidence: src/Pm/Vault.hs:606-618 `Right plan -> do pr <- runPlan plan; … pure (planRunCode pr)` vs src/Pm/Apply.hs:196-200 `when (plKind plan == "vault-push") $ do … _ <- computeVault True cfg`; app/Main.hs:149-150; src/Pm/Status.hs:241-254.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Vault.hs:566-618 — `runVaultPush` begins with `er <- computeVault False cfg` (:568), which inside computeVault' writes `.pm/vault-cache/meta.json` with the PRE-push counts (`writeVaultCache root … meta` at :387-401, vmNew = length (vdNew d)). After `pr <- runPlan plan` (:611) it only prints git steps and returns `planRunCode pr` (:618); no recompute. `runPlan` is bound in app/Main.hs:149-150 to `savePlanAndMaybeRun' cfg go` → `savePlanAndMaybeRunTo` (Cli.hs:241-257) → `executePlanNowWith` (Cli.hs:124-164), which does execPlanRetry + `writeBackCatalog` of the plan root's own catalog only — nothing touches the main-side vault-cache. By contrast `Pm.Apply.afterApply` (Apply.hs:196-200) does `when (plKind plan == "vault-push") $ do … _ <- computeVault True cfg`, called from runApply (:170) and Serve.hs:340. REPRO: album a.jpg b.jpg c.jpg, vault empty categories. `pm vault push --category landscape a.jpg b.jpg c.jpg --apply -y`: computeVault writes meta {new:3, held:0, …}; checkAssignments ok; plan of 3 Pending Copies; savePlanAndMaybeRunTo: requireWritable, savePlan, confirm (apply+yes ⇒ True), executePlanNowWith ⇒ 3 ODone, exit 0, git steps printed. meta.json still says new=3. `pm status` → Status.hs:241-254: CacheOk v, vlag = 3−0+0+0+0 = 3 ≠ 0 → prints "  ⚠ vault    上次比对 <push time> · 差异 3（NEW 3 / MISS 0 / REN 0 / DRIFT 0 / 不稳定 0）→ pm vault status". Same plan via `pm apply <id>` → afterApply recomputes → new=0 → "无差异". Wrong outcome reached: a lag that no longer exists is reported, and the two execution paths of the same plan kind disagree. DESIGN: DESIGN-COMMANDS §10.2 (:362-368) requires the CLI direct push and the plan's `pm apply` to be "同源" for the收尾, and afterApply's comment ("刷新 vault 缓存（computeVault 顺带写缓存…）") shows the refresh is intended after a vault-push executes; REVIEW-LOG-4 簇 B states afterApply/runVaultPush were aligned on `landedItems`/`resultCategories` but says nothing about the cache. Nothing in README known limitations or REVIEW-LOG rules the stale cache intended. `pm status` does say "上次比对 <time>", which is literally true, so the impact is a misleading ⚠ line until the next `pm vault status`, not a wrong decision by the tool.
verdict.corrected_summary: `pm vault push … --apply` executes the plan through `savePlanAndMaybeRun'` and returns without re-running `computeVault`, so `.pm/vault-cache/meta.json` keeps the pre-push counts written at the start of the command; `pm status` then shows a ⚠ vault lag (NEW N) that was just pushed, whereas executing the identical plan via `pm apply <id>` / the GUI goes through `afterApply` which refreshes the cache. Cosmetic/misleading only; `pm vault status` corrects it.
verdict.suggested_fix: In runVaultPush (Vault.hs:611-618), after `pr <- runPlan plan`, when `pr` is `PrRun _ rs` with non-null `landedItems rs` (or unconditionally on PrRun) call `_ <- computeVault True cfg` to rewrite the cache, mirroring Apply.afterApply; or have runVaultPush call afterApply's vault-push branch. Add a test that reads readVaultCacheMeta after `runVaultPush (execNow cfg) … --apply` and asserts vmNew == 0.

confirmed.title: DRIFT items are turned into vault Copy ops without the jpg/jpeg write-path gate, so a .png can be pushed into a vault category
confirmed.summary: `vaultPushItems` builds `driftItems` from every `vdDrift` entry and only requires the name to be in `vrSrcMeta`; there is no `pushableExt` filter. A DRIFT on a `.png` produces an `OpCopy album/x.png → <cat>/x.png` (NEEDS-DECISION) which `pm resolve --keep src` executes, landing a .png through the push write path that the module header and DESIGN-COMMANDS §10.2 say 'push 写路径拒收'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Album has `p.png` (bytes A); vault `landscape/p.png` exists with bytes B. `pm vault push` (no args) → `allItems = driftItems` → plan saved (also via POST /api/vault/push-plan with empty assignments). `pm resolve <id> --item 0 --keep src` → quarantine old png + copy album png into vault.
confirmed.evidence: src/Pm/Vault.hs:655-665 driftItems; compare :643 `| not (pushableExt f) = Just (f <> " 是 UNPUSHABLE…")`; header :5-7; DESIGN-COMMANDS.md §10.2; casePushRefusals only covers NEW .png.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Vault.hs:655-665 `vaultPushItems r pairs' = newItems <> driftItems` where `driftItems = [(OpCopy (vrSrcDir r </> n) (c </> n) …, StNeedsDecision …) | (n, c, _, _) <- vdDrift (vrDiff r), Just e <- [Map.lookup n (vrSrcMeta r)]]` — no `pushableExt` filter. The only ext gate is `checkAssignments` (:643) which sees only the explicit NEW pairs, not DRIFT. VaultCore.vaultDiff (:72-94) classifies purely by sha over the photoExtFold set that includes .png (:55), so a .png can be DRIFT. Downstream: resolveKeep (Apply.hs:294-333) builds Quarantine+Copy with no extension check; Exec/GitGuard have none (grep pushableExt/.png in Exec.hs, GitGuard.hs: nothing). ServeVault.hs:104 explicitly admits an empty-assignment plan whenever vdDrift is non-empty. REPRO: album `p.png` bytes A, vault `landscape/p.png` bytes B. computeVault': srcShas{p.png→shaA}, vaultShas[(landscape,{p.png→shaB})] → inter contains p.png, shaA≠shaB → vdDrift=[("p.png","landscape",shaA,shaB)]; unpushable=[(p.png,相册),(p.png,landscape)]; vrSrcMeta has p.png. `pm vault push` → sel Right [] → checkAssignments []=[] → allItems=[(OpCopy album/p.png landscape/p.png shaA …, StNeedsDecision)] → mkVaultPushPlan → plan saved (exit 1 via PrSaved). `pm resolve <id> --item 0 --keep src` → dst exists → sha256File dst → appends Quarantine(landscape/p.png) + Copy, group; `pm apply <id>` → old png to vault .pm/trash, album png lands in landscape/. Wrong outcome reached: a .png travels the push write path. Meanwhile `pm vault status` for this state prints both "✋ UNPUSHABLE landscape/p.png（非 jpg：…push 写路径拒收 → pm convert…）" (:462-464) and "~ DRIFT landscape/p.png … → pm vault push 生成裁决计划" (:453-457) — the same self-contradiction class as N4. DESIGN: module header :5-7 "UNPUSHABLE … push 写路径拒收"; DESIGN-COMMANDS §10.1 (:333-335) "「只收 jpg/jpeg」的收紧只在 push/ingest 写路径生效"; §10.2 (:353-354) "写路径只收 jpg/jpeg（case-fold）"; Ingest.hs:260 "相册与 vault 只收成品 JPG". No REVIEW-LOG row or README limitation rules DRIFT .png intended; casePushRefusals (test/VaultTests.hs:319-338) and ServeWriteTests only cover NEW .png. Docs agree with the finder. Severity kept low: it requires a pre-existing .png already in a vault category (real vault has zero png, vault-topology-p3.md:34), requires an explicit user `--keep src` resolution, the old bytes are quarantined not lost, and the vault ends up with a png exactly where it already had one.
verdict.corrected_summary: `vaultPushItems` turns every DRIFT entry into a NEEDS-DECISION `OpCopy` without applying `pushableExt`, so when the vault already holds `<cat>/x.png` and the album's `x.png` differs, `pm vault push` (CLI, and POST /api/vault/push-plan with empty assignments) emits a plan that `pm resolve --keep src` + apply will execute, copying a .png through the push write path that the module header and DESIGN-COMMANDS §10.1/§10.2 say rejects non-jpg; `pm vault status` simultaneously labels that file UNPUSHABLE("写路径拒收") and DRIFT("→ pm vault push 生成裁决计划"). Edge path (needs a pre-existing png in vault), no data loss.
verdict.suggested_fix: Filter `driftItems` with `pushableExt n` (Vault.hs:660-665) and report the skipped non-jpg DRIFT as a "只报告" line (like RENAME/MISSING) pointing to `pm convert`; in ServeVault.hs:104 change the empty-assignment admission to check `any (pushableExt . fst4) (vdDrift …)` (or `not (null (vaultPushItems r []))`) so a png-only DRIFT does not yield an empty plan; add a VaultTests case with a vault-side .png DRIFT asserting no plan item is generated.

confirmed.title: caseRefusals unconditionally unsetEnv "PM_PYTHON" → clobbers a user-supplied PM_PYTHON before caseE2E/caseDerivedGuards, which need python
confirmed.summary: `bracket_ (setEnv "PM_PYTHON" (root </> "nope.exe")) (unsetEnv "PM_PYTHON")` restores the variable by unsetting it instead of restoring the previous value. The suite runs serially in one process and the group order is caseRefusals → caseE2E → …; after caseRefusals the process-wide PM_PYTHON is gone, so `findPython` falls back to PATH. Same pattern at line 254.
confirmed.failure_scenario: CI has no `python` on PATH and sets `PM_PYTHON=C:\Python312\python.exe`. `stack test`: caseRefusals passes, its cleanup unsets PM_PYTHON; caseE2E then `findExecutable "python"` = Nothing → assertFailure '找不到 python（PATH 上没有）'; caseDerivedGuards likewise. Reordering makes them pass.
confirmed.evidence: test/ConvertTests.hs:130-131; :254 `bracket_ (setEnv "PM_PYTHON" slow >> setEnv "PM_CONVERT_TIMEOUT" "1") (unsetEnv "PM_PYTHON" >> unsetEnv "PM_CONVERT_TIMEOUT")`; :63-65 `python = findPython >>= either (\m -> assertFailure m …)`; src/Pm/Convert.hs:88-96; test/Spec.hs:61; ConvertTests.hs:38-41.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: test/ConvertTests.hs:130 is exactly `bracket_ (setEnv "PM_PYTHON" (root </> "nope.exe")) (unsetEnv "PM_PYTHON") $ refuse ...` and :254 is `bracket_ (setEnv "PM_PYTHON" slow >> setEnv "PM_CONVERT_TIMEOUT" "1") (unsetEnv "PM_PYTHON" >> unsetEnv "PM_CONVERT_TIMEOUT")`. GHC's System.Environment.setEnv/unsetEnv on Windows call SetEnvironmentVariableW (unsetEnv passes NULL, removing the variable process-wide); lookupEnv reads GetEnvironmentVariableW, so the release action really deletes any pre-existing value rather than restoring it. src/Pm/Convert.hs:87-96 `findPython`: `lookupEnv "PM_PYTHON"` → Just p ⇒ doesFileExist check; Nothing ⇒ `findExecutable "python"` else Left "找不到 python（PATH 上没有）→ 设 PM_PYTHON ...". The test helper `python` (:64-65) is `findPython >>= either (\m -> assertFailure m >> pure "") pure`, and it is used by caseE2E (:136), writeRgbPng (:92, used by caseDerivedGuards :216) — all after caseRefusals. test/Spec.hs:60-61 runs the whole suite in one process with `localOption (NumThreads 1)`, and convertTests (:35-42) lists caseRefusals first, caseE2E second, caseDoctorDerived third, caseDerivedGuards fourth, so order is deterministic. The test module header (:6-7) explicitly advertises `PM_PYTHON → PATH` as the supported way to supply python for these tests, and nothing in Spec.hs or CI re-sets PM_PYTHON. The repo's own convention elsewhere is to restore the previous value (test/GuardTests.hs:636-641 `mold <- lookupEnv "PM_CONFIG"` ... `finally (maybe (pure ()) (setEnv "PM_CONFIG") mold)`), so this site is an inconsistency, not a chosen idiom. REPRO: Windows dev box with no `python` on PATH, `set PM_PYTHON=C:\Python312\python.exe`, `stack test`. caseRefusals: line 130 setEnv PM_PYTHON=<root>/nope.exe, `refuse` sees exit 2 with 'PM_PYTHON 指向的文件不存在' (Convert.hs:93) → passes; release action unsetEnv removes PM_PYTHON. caseE2E: line 136 `exe <- python` → findPython → lookupEnv = Nothing → findExecutable "python" = Nothing → Left "找不到 python（PATH 上没有）..." → assertFailure → test red. caseDerivedGuards: line 216 writeRgbPng → same failure. Running caseE2E alone (`-p`) or reordering makes it pass, which confirms the ordering dependency. (If the Windows Store `python.exe` app-execution alias is on PATH instead, findExecutable returns that stub and `py` fails with a non-zero exit — still a spurious failure.) CI (.github/workflows/build.yml:60-63) uses setup-python which puts python on PATH and never sets PM_PYTHON, so CI is not affected; the failure is confined to local runs that rely on PM_PYTHON. DESIGN: docs/DESIGN-P8.md:155-157, DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:550 and DESIGN.md:242 document PM_PYTHON as the first-priority discovery route; README 465-553 and REVIEW-LOG.md (:381, :436, :490) do not mention or rule on test env restoration. No doc declares 'python must be on PATH to run the suite', and the test header says the opposite. Not refuted, but it is test fragility only — it never hides a production bug and never affects CI — so severity is low.
verdict.corrected_summary: test/ConvertTests.hs:130 and :254 wrap PM_PYTHON overrides in `bracket_ (setEnv …) (unsetEnv …)`, which deletes rather than restores any PM_PYTHON the person running the suite had set. Because Spec.hs runs the suite serially in one process (NumThreads 1) and caseRefusals precedes caseE2E/caseDerivedGuards, a local run that supplies python only via PM_PYTHON (the route the module header itself advertises) sees caseE2E and caseDerivedGuards fail with '找不到 python（PATH 上没有）' after caseRefusals succeeds. CI is unaffected (python is on PATH there, PM_PYTHON unset); the defect is an order-dependent spurious failure in local runs, not a hidden production bug.
verdict.suggested_fix: At both sites capture the old value and restore it, mirroring test/GuardTests.hs:636-641: `old <- lookupEnv "PM_PYTHON"` then release with `maybe (unsetEnv "PM_PYTHON") (setEnv "PM_PYTHON") old` (and the same for PM_CONVERT_TIMEOUT at :254). Optionally factor a small `withEnv :: String -> String -> IO a -> IO a` helper in TestUtil and reuse it for the PM_CLAUDE_EXE/PM_SUGGEST_TIMEOUT brackets in ServeP8Tests.hs:287/336/354.

confirmed.title: innerHTML sentinel only checks the first two characters after '=' → `el.innerHTML = "" + expr` passes the '只允许赋空串' guard
confirmed.summary: `innerBad` flags an `innerHTML` occurrence unless the text after `=` starts with `""`. It does not require the statement to END there, so `box.innerHTML = "" + d.msg` is accepted. The guarantee that innerHTML is only ever assigned the empty string does not hold for this trivially reachable form. (Current gui/ui/*.js has only `innerHTML = "";` forms — sentinel gap.)
confirmed.failure_scenario: A later edit renders an API error with `box.innerHTML = "" + d.error;` in gui/ui/archive.js. `innerBad`: take 1 r == "=", take 2 … == "\"\"" → not flagged. caseGuiNoInlineStyle stays green while server-controlled text is injected as HTML.
confirmed.evidence: test/DocDriftTests.hs:220 `innerBad t = [take 30 s | s <- tails t, "innerHTML" `isPrefixOf` s, let r = dropWhile isSpace (drop 9 s), not (take 1 r == "=" && take 2 (dropWhile isSpace (drop 1 r)) == "\"\"")]`; :34 test title.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: test/DocDriftTests.hs:220 reads `innerBad t = [take 30 s | s <- tails t, "innerHTML" `isPrefixOf` s, let r = dropWhile isSpace (drop 9 s), not (take 1 r == "=" && take 2 (dropWhile isSpace (drop 1 r)) == "\"\"")]`. The predicate only inspects the first two characters after the `=`; nothing constrains what follows the `""`. The assertion at :226 (`assertEqual "gui/ui 脚本 innerHTML 只允许赋空串" [] (innerBad js)`) is the only check on innerHTML assignments; the other list at :225 (setAttribute(/insertAdjacentHTML/outerHTML/document.write/cssText) does not cover it either. REPRO: suppose gui/ui/archive.js gains `box.innerHTML = "" + d.error;`. For the tail s beginning at `innerHTML = "" + d.error;`: drop 9 → ` = "" + d.error;`; dropWhile isSpace → r = `= "" + d.error;`; take 1 r == "=" holds; drop 1 r = ` "" + d.error;`, dropWhile isSpace → `"" + d.error;`, take 2 == `""` holds → conjunction True → `not` False → occurrence not listed → innerBad js == [] → test green. Same for `innerHTML = "".concat(x)` and `innerHTML=""+x`. (`innerHTML += x` and `innerHTML = x` are correctly flagged.) Current tree: all 20 occurrences in gui/ui/app.js, archive.js, vault.js are exactly `innerHTML = "";` (grep confirms none deviate), so this is a sentinel gap, not a live production defect. DESIGN: docs/REVIEW-LOG.md:196-199 and :247 and docs/DESIGN-GUI.md:157-160 state the F090 premise as 'innerHTML 只赋空串' (innerHTML is only ever assigned the empty string) and the 48-round GO-note α (REVIEW-LOG.md:245-248) explicitly demanded that this sentinel's universal claim align with the tested surface, rewriting the literal table to lexical rules precisely because trivially different spellings (`style='…'`, `style = "…"`) slipped through. The docs therefore agree with the finder: the contract is 'only the empty string', and the lexical rule falls short of it for the `"" + …` spelling. No REVIEW-LOG entry rules this gap as accepted; REVIEW-LOG.md:413 only registers that GUI behaviour is not tested beyond static rules. Not a race/OS issue. Severity low: test-coverage only, requires a future edit in an unusual form, and no CSP directive is bypassed (XSS via innerHTML is not blocked by script-src 'self' for markup injection, so the sentinel is the only guard).
verdict.corrected_summary: caseGuiNoInlineStyle's `innerBad` (test/DocDriftTests.hs:220) accepts any innerHTML assignment whose right-hand side merely *starts* with `""`, so `el.innerHTML = "" + expr;` or `"".concat(expr)` would pass the '只允许赋空串' assertion while injecting server text as HTML. All current gui/ui/*.js uses are exactly `innerHTML = "";`, so this is a sentinel gap rather than a live defect, but it contradicts the documented F090 premise (REVIEW-LOG.md:196-199/:247, DESIGN-GUI.md:157-160) that innerHTML is only ever assigned the empty string.
verdict.suggested_fix: Tighten the sentinel to require the statement to end right after the empty string, e.g. change `take 2 (dropWhile isSpace (drop 1 r)) == "\"\""` to `take 3 (dropWhile isSpace (drop 1 r)) == "\"\";"` (all 20 existing uses are `= "";`, so the test stays green). Optionally add a mutation row (`innerHTML = "" + x`) to the REVIEW-LOG mutation table.

refuted.title: --verified-on compares a local calendar date against lastVerified, which Scan.hs writes in UTC, so entries hashed between 00:00 and 08:00 local (UTC+8) are silently excluded
refuted.summary: Scan.hs stores `enLastVerified = Just vnow` from getCurrentTime (UTC); Types.hs encodes it as `…Z`. verify_backup_entries.py selects entries with `.startswith(a.verified_on)` where the user supplies a local date. For a user in UTC+8, everything hashed before 08:00 local carries the previous UTC date and is skipped; the script then reports success over an incomplete set.
refuted.failure_scenario: `pm backup` finishes at 01:30 local on 2026-08-27; those entries get lastVerified `2026-08-26T17:30:xxZ`. User runs `--verified-on 2026-08-27` → zero targets selected, script ends with an all-OK summary. || `pm backup --apply` finishes at 21:30 EDT 2026-08-26 (= 01:30Z 08-27); `--verified-on 2026-08-26` → 0 targets, RESULT ok=0, exit 0. || pm backup finishes at 2026-08-27 01:30 CST → 0 targets, exit 0; the never-re-read batch is believed verified.
refuted.evidence: Scan.hs:324 `vnow <- getCurrentTime`, :333 `enLastVerified = Just vnow`; src/Pm/ExecTypes.hs:115 `enLastVerified = Just now`; Types.hs:149 `"lastVerified" .= enLastVerified e` (UTCTime → ISO-8601 Z); verify_backup_entries.py:4 docstring, :22-23/:61 `entries = [e for e in entries if (e.get("lastVerified") or "").startswith(a.verified_on)]`; DESIGN.md §6.4 (~399); README.md:199; backup_verify.py:161 exit 0 with empty targets.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Producer side is as the finder says — src/Pm/Scan.hs:324 `vnow <- getCurrentTime` / :333 `enLastVerified = Just vnow`, src/Pm/ExecTypes.hs:100-115 `updateCatalog now …` with `now` from `getCurrentTime` in Cli.hs:282, and Types.hs:149 `"lastVerified" .= enLastVerified e` — aeson's ToJSON UTCTime emits ISO-8601 with a trailing `Z` (UTC). Consumer side, scripts/verify_backup_entries.py:23 `entries = [e for e in entries if (e.get("lastVerified") or "").startswith(a.verified_on)]` is a raw string-prefix filter; it performs no time-zone conversion at all, so there is no *wrong* conversion. The finder's defect rests entirely on the premise that `--verified-on` promises a local calendar date. Nothing in the code or docs makes that promise: the script's own docstring (line 4) defines the flag as「只核 lastVerified 以该日期开头的条目」— 'entries whose lastVerified starts with that date', i.e. explicitly a prefix on the stored `lastVerified` string. DESIGN.md:392 says only「按备份 catalog 条目挑，如 --verified-on <日期>」and README.md:199 gives the example `--verified-on 2026-08-26` as 'by catalog entries (e.g. only those hashed at write time, never re-read)'. The rest of pm is consistent: plan ids (Plan.hs:130-132 `getCurrentTime` + `%Y%m%d-%H%M%S`) are also UTC strings, and `pm status` is the only place that converts to local (Status.hs:199-200), for display only. REPRO: I traced the finder's scenario (backup applied at 21:30 EDT 2026-08-26 → lastVerified `2026-08-27T01:30:..Z`; user runs `--verified-on 2026-08-26`): line 23 selects 0 entries, backup_verify.run prints `entries to verify: 0  bytes=0.00 GiB` (line 102) and `RESULT entries=0 ok=0 …` (line 150), finish exits 0 (line 161). So a wrong-date invocation does yield an empty run with exit 0 — but the count is printed twice, so it is not 'silent', and it only happens if the operator invents the date from wall-clock memory instead of reading it off the catalog. DESIGN: The real-world use that produced this script (docs/REVIEW-LOG.md:597, HISTORY.md:389) first built a histogram of the catalog's `lastVerified` values (08-25 3239 / 08-26 588 / 09-02 784) and then passed the bucket label to `--verified-on`; because both the histogram and the filter operate on the same stored UTC strings, the selection is self-consistent by construction (588/588 re-read). The flag is therefore a documented raw-prefix selector over catalog data, not a local-date query, and the code matches its contract. No test pins it (scripts are untested) but docs and code agree, and the CONTEXT rule 'doc says intended → refute' applies. Residual: at most a usability note (an operator who assumes local dates can under-select; an empty selection exits 0), severity low.
verdict.corrected_summary: Not a bug as claimed. `--verified-on` is, by its own docstring (line 4「lastVerified 以该日期开头」) and DESIGN.md:392/README.md:199, a literal string-prefix filter over the catalog's stored `lastVerified` (ISO-8601 UTC, `Z`), and the documented workflow (REVIEW-LOG.md:597) derives the date from a histogram of those same stored values, so producer and consumer agree. The script never promises local-date semantics and performs no time-zone conversion, so there is no UTC/local mistake in the code; an operator who supplies a wall-clock local date can under-select (possibly 0 entries), but the script prints `entries to verify: N` and `RESULT entries=N` so the shortfall is visible, not silent. At most a low-severity ergonomics gap.
verdict.suggested_fix: Optional hardening only: (a) state in the docstring/README that the value is matched against the stored UTC `lastVerified` prefix (or accept a local date by converting each `lastVerified` via `datetime.fromisoformat(v.replace('Z','+00:00')).astimezone().date()` before comparing — note aeson may emit more than 6 fractional digits, so trim them first); (b) in verify_backup_entries.py, warn or exit non-zero when `--verified-on` selects 0 entries and `--retry` is not set.

refuted.title: albumCandidates keys album entries by basename while classifyAlbum/albumPlanItems look up the exact `相册\<name>` path — the two views disagree when 相册 has subfolders
refuted.summary: `albumByFold` is built from every KindPhoto entry under `相册` (any depth) keyed by basename, whereas `classifyInto` looks up `foldPath (albumTop </> basename)` exactly. A same-sha copy at `相册\sub\x.jpg` makes `albumCandidates` treat `成片\E\x.jpg` as already in the album, while `pm album add E/x.jpg` will plan a copy to `相册\x.jpg`, creating a second album copy.
refuted.failure_scenario: Catalog has `成片\E\x.jpg` (sha S) and `相册\2024\x.jpg` (sha S). `pm album candidates` does not list x.jpg. `pm album add E/x.jpg` → classifyAlbum finds no `相册\x.jpg` → arCopy → plan lands `相册\x.jpg`; now the album holds two copies of S and `pm dedupe` reports them.
refuted.evidence: Album.hs:200 `albumByFold = Map.fromList [(foldPath (takeFileName (enPath e)), e) | e <- photos, top e == [albumTop]]`; Album.hs:206-207 lookup by basename; versus Album.hs:107-109 `catByFold` / `Map.lookup (foldPath d) catByFold` with `d = albumDst e = albumTop </> takeFileName (enPath e)` (line 69).

verdict.reasoning: CODE: the two views do differ as described — albumCandidates (Album.hs:198-207) builds albumByFold from every KindPhoto entry whose first component is 相册 at any depth, keyed by case-folded basename, while classifyInto (Album.hs:107-109) looks up the exact flat path `相册\<basename>` (albumDst, :69). REPRO (traced): catalog {成片\E\x.jpg sha S, 相册\2024\x.jpg sha S}: `pm album candidates` → m = Just (相册\2024\x.jpg), enSha equal → filtered out, x.jpg not listed; `pm album add E/x.jpg` → catByFold has no `相册\x.jpg` → judged Nothing → arCopy → plan lands 相册\x.jpg; album now holds S twice. So the divergence is reachable, but only when 相册 contains a subdirectory. DESIGN: the album is flat by contract — DESIGN.md:25 `收藏集 | 相册\ | … | **扁平**`, DESIGN-P8 §19 (:44 `相册\（平铺）`, :96 `相册是平铺`), Album.hs:4 `平铺收藏层（相册\<basename>）`, and pm never writes below 相册\<basename> (Ingest.hs:115, Album.hs:69, Convert.hs:265). Pm.Vault already treats subfolders under 相册 as an anomaly and warns explicitly: src/Pm/Vault.hs:331 `⚠ 相册下有子目录（平铺语义，不递归）`. A user-created subfolder is therefore an out-of-contract layout that pm flags rather than supports; the consequence in that state is a second same-sha copy that `pm dedupe`/`pm versions` report (no overwrite, no loss). Given the documented flat contract and the explicit warning, this is an edge-of-contract inconsistency, not a defect against the specification.
verdict.corrected_summary: albumCandidates matches album twins by basename at any depth under 相册 while classifyAlbum/album add look up the exact flat `相册\<basename>`; they disagree only if a user has created subfolders inside 相册, which the documented topology forbids (`扁平`) and `pm vault status` already warns about (Vault.hs:331). Worst case is a redundant same-sha copy at 相册\<name> that dedupe reports. Not a bug against the contract.
verdict.suggested_fix: Optional hardening: in albumCandidates restrict albumByFold to flat entries, e.g. `length (splitDirectories (enPath e)) == 2`, so both views use the same flat key; or none.

refuted.title: pm album unignore never accepts the record's stored path in the form pm itself prints/stores it
refuted.summary: The CLI help and the comment on ignoreRequest promise that a record's archived path (aiPath, stored as `成片\E1\a.jpg` and printed verbatim) is accepted. But resolveDel feeds every non-sha token through parseProcessedRel, which rejects any 成片 prefix. Additionally, when the stored path still exists in the index but with a different sha (re-export), resolveDel returns `不在忽略清单里` and never falls back to oldByPath.
refuted.failure_scenario: User runs `pm album candidates`, sees `已忽略… 成片\E1\a.jpg`, copies it: `pm album unignore 成片\E1\a.jpg` → exit 2 `不要带 成片\ 前缀…`. Or: a.jpg was re-exported so the record is stale; `pm album unignore E1/a.jpg` → Map.lookup by new sha fails → `E1/a.jpg 不在忽略清单里`, even though aiPath is exactly 成片\E1\a.jpg. Only the 64-hex sha works. || User ignores `成片\E1\a.jpg` (sha S1), re-exports at same path (S2). `pm album candidates` shows 「忽略记录已失效 …」. `pm album unignore E1/a.jpg` → exit 2 although `.pm/album-ignore.json` still contains that exact path.
refuted.evidence: Album.hs:368-378 resolveDel: `Right rel -> case Map.lookup (foldPath rel) byFold of Just e | Just x <- Map.lookup (enSha e) oldBySha -> Right (aiSha x) | otherwise -> Left (t <> " 不在忽略清单里"); Nothing -> maybe (Left …) (Right . aiSha) (Map.lookup (foldPath rel) oldByPath)` — oldByPath (line 366) only consulted in the `Nothing` arm; Album.hs:175 rejects 成片 prefix; Album.hs:392 `adds = [AlbumIgnore (enSha e) (enPath e) now | e <- okAdds]`; Album.hs:294-295 prints `enPath e`; app/Main.hs:298 help text; doc comment 352-354.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: resolveDel (Album.hs:368-378) accepts a 64-hex sha, otherwise runs parseProcessedRel, which rejects a `成片\` prefix (:175) with `不要带 成片\ 前缀，直接给 <事件夹>/<文件名>`; on Right rel it looks the current entry up by path and then its sha in oldBySha, and consults oldByPath only when the path is not in the index. REPRO of sub-claim 1: `pm album unignore 成片\E1\a.jpg` → perrs (:412-413) → exit 2 with that self-correcting message; `pm album unignore E1/a.jpg` then succeeds (or, if the object is gone, hits the oldByPath arm). Sub-claim 2: record {sha S1, path 成片\E1\a.jpg}, file re-exported with S2: `E1/a.jpg` → byFold hit with S2 → oldBySha S2 absent → `E1/a.jpg 不在忽略清单里`, no fallback — traced as the finder says. DESIGN: the promised token forms are `<事件夹>/<文件名>` (metavar `事件夹/文件名|sha...`, app/Main.hs:298) and DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:572 `unignore 收 64 位 sha、当前路径或记录存档路径（对象已删也能清）`; the code comment (Album.hs:353-354) says the same: `对象已不在索引时按存档路径也能清`. Both explicitly scope the archived-path fallback to objects absent from the index, which is exactly what the Nothing arm implements, and test caseIgnoreRequestPure (test/AlbumTests.hs:172-177) pins the archived-path form as `E9/old.jpg` (no 成片 prefix) — docs and test agree with the code. For the stale/re-export case the ignore semantics are by content sha (`重新导出=新字节会重新出现`, DESIGN-COMMANDS:572; Album.hs:304-306), so `不在忽略清单里` is accurate for the bytes now at that path, and `pm album candidates` (:296-297) already prints the working command `⚠ 忽略记录已失效 … → pm album unignore <sha>`; the GUI stale row likewise sends the sha (archive.js:117). No user is led to a wrong action: the 成片-prefix error tells them the exact form, and the stale-record hint gives the sha. Residual cosmetic nit: the 已忽略 list (:294-295) prints `enPath e` with the 成片\ prefix right under `pm album unignore <路径|sha> 恢复`, so a verbatim copy needs the prefix stripped.
verdict.corrected_summary: Not a contract violation: help text, DESIGN-COMMANDS:572, the code comment and the test all define the archived-path form as `<事件夹>/<文件名>` and limit the archived-path fallback to objects no longer in the index; a 成片\-prefixed token is rejected with an explicit fix-it message, and a stale (re-exported) record is already reported by `pm album candidates` with the sha-based unignore command. Only a cosmetic inconsistency remains: the 已忽略 listing prints the 成片\-prefixed path next to the `unignore <路径|sha>` hint.
verdict.suggested_fix: Optional polish: in runAlbumCandidates:295 print `joinPath (drop 1 (splitDirectories (enPath e)))` (the accepted form) or the sha, and/or let resolveDel strip a leading 成片\ component before parseProcessedRel; or none.

refuted.title: Interactive confirm executes the in-memory plan captured before the lock; a `pm resolve` written under the lock during the y/N prompt is silently overridden
refuted.summary: savePlanAndMaybeRunTo saves the plan, prints it, then blocks in `confirm go` with no lock held; on 'y' it passes the in-memory `plan` to executePlanNowWith and Exec.execPlan' never re-reads the plan file inside withRootLock. Apply.resolveOn deliberately reloads the plan inside the root lock and writes it back, so a resolve issued while the prompt is open succeeds, but its item-status change is not seen by the execution that follows.
refuted.failure_scenario: Terminal 1: `pm import --apply` -> plan saved, prompt '执行以上计划? [y/N]' waits. In terminal 2 the user runs `pm resolve <id> --item 7` (skip): resolveOn takes the free root lock, marks 7 StSkippedByUser, savePlan succeeds. Terminal 1: user answers y. executePlanNowWith runs the stale in-memory plan where item 7 is still StPending: execItem copies it. The on-disk plan says item 7 skipped, the journal says it was executed. Reverse direction (`--unskip`) leaves the approved item ONotExecuted.
refuted.evidence: Cli.hs:243-257 `savePlanAndMaybeRunTo … fp <- savePlan plan … ok <- confirm go; if ok then uncurry PrRun <$> executePlanNowWith cfg sink plan else pure PrSaved`. Cli.hs:74-85 confirm blocks on `getLine`. Exec.hs:114-118 no loadPlan inside the lock. Apply.hs:214-233 resolveOn: in-lock RMW of the plan file. DESIGN.md §6.7 '证据在锁内取'. Same shape for `pm apply <id>` (prepareApply -> loadPlanAnyRoot outside the lock).

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Cli.hs:241-257 savePlanAndMaybeRunTo saves the plan, prints it, blocks in `confirm go` (Cli.hs:74-85, `try getLine`) with no lock, then passes the same in-memory `plan` to executePlanNowWith; Exec.execPlan' (Exec.hs:114-190) never re-reads the plan file inside withRootLock — it re-verifies disk evidence only (root identity, I11, .pm trust, group barrier, per-item fingerprints/dst state). Apply.resolveOn (Apply.hs:226-242) does its own in-lock reload and write-back, so the finder's mechanics are accurate: a `pm resolve <id> --item 7` issued in a second terminal while the prompt is open succeeds, and the subsequent 'y' executes the pre-resolve item statuses. REPRO diverges at the judgment, not the trace: the plan the prompt shows is byte-for-byte the plan that runs, which is exactly what I3 (DESIGN §2: every write goes through a printed+confirmed Plan) requires; running the on-disk plan instead would execute items the user never saw at that prompt (e.g. `--keep both`/`--keep src` add supersede ops). The conflicting resolve is the same user's contradictory action against a prompt they themselves left open — not another actor and not a race window pm can be blamed for. Outcome is bounded: skip direction lands the no-replace Copy that was displayed and confirmed (I5 still enforced in the kernel); unskip direction leaves the item ONotExecuted and the resolved plan file remains applicable via `pm apply <id>`. Downstream state stays coherent: Plan.hs:351-356 planExecuted/runTag compute from StPending items ∩ journal Done, so an item marked StSkippedByUser on disk but Done in the journal does not yield a contradictory 'executed' display. DESIGN: §6.7 (DESIGN.md:438-447) enumerates the lock-internal evidence sites deliberately (barrier, trash empty, resolve, doctor --repair, catalog write-back, side caches) and REVIEW-LOG-2.md:120-140 (F2a) scopes the resolve fix to two resolves racing; no doc requires apply/confirm to re-read the plan file, and the plan's item statuses are the user's instruction, not on-disk evidence. Per the task rules this is at most a self-inflicted low-severity inconsistency with no documented contract violated, so refuted.
verdict.corrected_summary: Not a defect as claimed: the interactive confirm executes exactly the plan that was printed and confirmed (I3), the kernel re-verifies all on-disk evidence inside the lock, and the only way to get a divergence is the same user running `pm resolve` on the plan from another terminal while their own y/N prompt is open. Consequences are bounded (a displayed, no-replace Copy lands, or an item stays ONotExecuted and the resolved plan can still be applied) and planExecuted/runTag remain consistent. DESIGN §6.7's in-lock-evidence list intentionally covers resolve/doctor/trash/catalog, not plan re-reading at apply.
verdict.suggested_fix: none required; optional hardening: after `confirm` returns True, `loadPlan (plRootPath plan) (plId plan)` and refuse with a message if `plItems` differ from the in-memory plan (same idea for prepareApply → executePlanNowWith).

refuted.title: loadConfigState collapses an unreadable/ACL-denied config into '配置不存在 → 先运行 pm init'
refuted.summary: loadConfigState uses the boolean doesFileExist, which returns False for ACL-denied, locked-attribute or media errors as well as for absence. The absent branch tells the user the config does not exist and to run pm init. runInit itself was three-state-ified in round 36, but the read side used by every other command still guides the user to re-initialise.
refuted.failure_scenario: config.toml exists but a DACL deny makes GetFileAttributes fail with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. Every `pm <cmd>` prints "配置不存在: … —— 先运行 pm init --main <主库路径>" and exits 2. The user runs `pm init --main D:\Photography`; only then does runInit's probeName report "存在性查不出（ACL/介质错误？）".
refuted.evidence: Config.hs:202-215: `exists <- doesFileExist fp; if not exists then ... CfgAbsent … "配置不存在: " <> fp <> " —— 先运行 pm init …"`. Contrast Commands.hs:141-144 (runInit) `classifyGitProbe <$> probeName cfgFp`. Consumer Commands.hs:84-88 withCfg.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Config.hs:200-215 `exists <- doesFileExist fp; if not exists then … CfgAbsent "配置不存在: … —— 先运行 pm init --main <主库路径>"`. doesFileExist swallows ACL/media errors as False, so a DACL-denied config.toml yields the 'absent' message on every command routed through withCfg (Commands.hs:84-88), exit 2. REPRO: icacls deny(F) on %APPDATA%\pm\config.toml; `pm status` prints '配置不存在 … 先运行 pm init' exit 2. Following that advice: runInit (Commands.hs:141-144) probes with `classifyGitProbe <$> probeName cfgFp` → GetFileAttributesW fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED → ProbeUnknown → Left '配置文件 … 存在性查不出（ACL/介质错误？）' exit 2 before any write (the --force branch is behind that gate). So the trace never reaches a wrong outcome: nothing is written, nothing lost, the user gets the correct diagnosis one step later. DESIGN: REVIEW-LOG-3.md:105-150 (round 36 F1) explicitly fixed the ruling: 'boolean probes are only allowed where False→reject' (and Commands.hs:138-141 says runInit's probe was 'the only False→pass-through boolean probe in the repo'). loadConfigState's False→CfgAbsent→exit 2 is a reject, hence inside the documented class boundary. The CONTEXT counts a misleading message only when it would cause a wrong action; the suggested action is itself fail-closed. At most a cosmetic wording improvement.
verdict.corrected_summary: Not a defect under the project's stated rule: loadConfigState's doesFileExist collapses ACL/media errors into '配置不存在 → pm init', but that branch fails closed (exit 2, no write) and the recommended pm init is itself three-state gated (Commands.hs:141-144) and refuses with '存在性查不出'. Round 36 (REVIEW-LOG-3) explicitly permits boolean probes in False→reject positions. Only the wording is imprecise.
verdict.suggested_fix: Optional cosmetic: replace doesFileExist with probeName in loadConfigState and map ProbeUnknown to CfgUnreadable ("配置存在性查不出（ACL/介质错误？）") so the message does not point to pm init.

refuted.title: writeConfig silently replaces a symlinked config.toml with a regular file (deleteBoundAt deletes the link itself, not through it)
refuted.summary: writeConfig probes the target with doesFileExist (follows links) and then unlinks it with deleteBoundAt, whose open uses FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT and whose rawBoundTo check passes for the link's own path. For a config.toml that is a file symlink, the link is removed and the tmp is moved into its place as a plain file; the link target keeps the old content. No message tells the user.
refuted.failure_scenario: %APPDATA%\pm\config.toml is `mklink`'d to D:\dotfiles\pm\config.toml. `pm config set --vault X`: doesFileExist → True; deleteBoundAt opens the reparse point itself → link deleted; moveBoundNoReplace lands config.toml.tmp as a regular file. pm reports '✓ 已写入 …'. D:\dotfiles\pm\config.toml still holds the old settings; the next dotfiles sync restores stale settings.
refuted.evidence: Config.hs:288-301 `writeConfig … old <- doesFileExist fp; when old (deleteBoundAt fp); moveBoundNoReplace tmp fp`. Win.hs:717-731 deleteBoundAt: 'OPEN_REPARSE_POINT——终段是链接时拿到的是链接本体'. cbits/pm_win.c:50-56 pm_open_for_dispose uses FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS | FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT. Config.hs:278-287 comment never considers a linked config.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Config.hs:288-301 writeConfig: `old <- doesFileExist fp; when old (deleteBoundAt fp); moveBoundNoReplace tmp fp`. deleteBoundAt (Win.hs:717-731) opens via pm_open_for_dispose with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT (cbits/pm_win.c:50-56), so for a file symlink the handle is the link object; GetFinalPathNameByHandleW on that handle reports the link's own path → rawBoundTo passes → FileDispositionInfo removes the link; the tmp is then renamed into place as a regular file. REPRO: `mklink %APPDATA%\pm\config.toml D:\dotfiles\pm\config.toml`; `pm config set --vault X` → configTxn reads through the link (BS.readFile follows) → writeConfig deletes the link, lands a plain config.toml, prints ✓; D:\dotfiles\pm\config.toml unchanged. The behaviour is real. DESIGN: this is exactly the documented semantics of the primitive — Win.hs:717-719 '终段是 symlink 时删的是链接本体，目标不受影响' and openFreshBinary's comment '对 symlink 删的是链接本体' — and pm's write discipline (DESIGN §6 / §14, resolveUnder, openBoundTo) is to never write through a link; writing 'through' to the dotfiles target would be the forbidden alternative. Pre-P6-C the same site used removeFile, which on Windows also unlinks the symlink itself, so behaviour is unchanged since the config write existed. A symlinked config.toml is not a documented or tested configuration (DESIGN-GUI.md:191-206 describes config as a plain file in XDG/PM_CONFIG); no doc promises link preservation, and no data is lost (old settings remain readable in the target, new settings in the real file). This is standard replace-file semantics rather than a wrong result; at most a low-value hardening (refuse a surrogate) could be argued, so per the default-to-refute rule it is refuted.
verdict.corrected_summary: Real but intended behaviour: writeConfig's deleteBoundAt intentionally never follows the final component, so a symlinked config.toml is replaced by a regular file and the link target keeps the old text. This matches the documented unlink semantics, the project's never-write-through-links discipline, and the pre-P6-C removeFile behaviour; symlinked configs are not a supported configuration. Not a defect.
verdict.suggested_fix: None required. Optional hardening consistent with the fail-closed style: in writeConfig probe fp with probeName and refuse with a message when it is NameSurrogate instead of silently replacing the link.

refuted.title: Cross-process I10 contention raises PermissionDenied, not ResourceBusy, so every documented 'lock busy' downgrade is unreachable and the command crashes instead
refuted.summary: `withRootLock`/`withConfigLock` map only `isAlreadyInUseError` (ResourceBusy) to `Nothing`. `openStateLock` → `openBoundTo ReadWriteMode` → `openBinaryFile`. Under GHC's default (MIO) I/O manager on Windows, `__hscore_open` opens writable files with `_wsopen(…, _SH_DENYRW, …)`; a second *process* therefore fails at CreateFile with ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION → EACCES → `PermissionDenied`. `ResourceBusy` is produced only by the RTS per-process lockFile table (the same-process case that KernelTests exercises). So with two pm processes the `otherwise -> throwIO e` branch fires.
refuted.failure_scenario: GUI `pm serve` is open and the user runs `pm apply <plan>` in a terminal. (a) The CLI: instead of `另一个 pm 实例正持有该 root 的锁（I10），稍后重试` with exit 2, it aborts with `openBinaryFile: permission denied (Permission denied)` on `.pm\lock`, exit 1. (b) While apply holds the lock, the GUI's status refresh (`writeSideCache` → `withRootLock`) is documented to degrade to `CacheLockBusy`; it throws instead and the handler answers 500. (c) `pm doctor --repair` in parallel should downgrade to diagnose-only but crashes. (d) Cli.hs:285's `catalog 回写未完成` branch is never taken.
refuted.evidence: Config.hs:643-660 `withRootLock … Left (e :: IOException) | isAlreadyInUseError e -> pure Nothing | otherwise -> throwIO e`; comment at 636-638 asserts "第二个可写打开直接 resource busy". Config.hs:314-323 same shape. Win.hs:446-453 openStateLock; Win.hs:405-406 `openBinaryFile fp mode`. package.yaml:63-65 `-threaded -rtsopts -with-rtsopts=-N` (no `--io-manager=native`). Consumers: Exec.hs:176, Apply.hs:241, Doctor.hs:108, Cli.hs:285, Commands.hs:322, Config.hs:700-703. Tests: KernelTests.hs:721-727 nest withRootLock in one process; REVIEW-LOG-1B.md:174 "跨进程锁只用同进程线程代表"; HandleGuardTests.hs:188-190.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: withRootLock (src/Pm/Config.hs:645-661) and withConfigLock (:314-329) do `try (openStateLock fp)`, map `isAlreadyInUseError` (ResourceBusy) to Nothing, rethrow anything else, then `hTryLock h ExclusiveLock` and return Nothing when it yields False. openStateLock (src/Pm/Win.hs:446-455) -> openBoundTo ReadWriteMode (:405-407) -> `openBinaryFile fp ReadWriteMode`. The finder's whole mechanism rests on the claim that GHC's `__hscore_open` opens writable files with `_wsopen(..., _SH_DENYRW, ...)`, so a second PROCESS would get ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION -> EACCES -> PermissionDenied. That is the pre-9.x HsBase.h. The GHC 9.10.3 the project builds with (package.yaml/Stack; the same version is installed in this container at /root/.local/share/ghcup/ghc/9.10.3) ships ghc-internal-9.1003.0 include/HsBase.h lines 521-536: `if ((how & O_WRONLY) || (how & O_RDWR) || (how & O_APPEND)) result = __hs_swopen(file, how | _O_NOINHERIT, _SH_DENYNO, mode); else result = __hs_swopen(file, how | _O_NOINHERIT, _SH_DENYNO, mode);` — `_SH_DENYNO` (FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE) in BOTH branches. This is corroborated by the project's own same-GHC probe recorded in test/HandleGuardTests.hs:185-190 and docs/REVIEW-LOG.md:150-156 (46/47 rounds): under the legacy manager a leaked writable handle only lacks FILE_SHARE_DELETE (removeFile fails) — it does not deny read/write to other openers. ResourceBusy is indeed produced only by the RTS per-process lockFile table, but that is the same-process layer; the cross-process layer is the explicit `hTryLock` (LockFileEx with LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK|LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY over the whole range, returning False on ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION), and it is reachable because the second open succeeds. REPRO: GUI `pm serve` holds `<root>\.pm\lock`: CreateFileW(GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE, share READ|WRITE) + LockFileEx exclusive, handle kept for the duration of `act`. User runs `pm apply <plan>` in a terminal: Exec.hs -> withRootLock -> openStateLock -> openBinaryFile ReadWriteMode -> CreateFileW(GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE, share READ|WRITE): the existing handle shares READ+WRITE and the new one requests only READ+WRITE, so the sharing check passes; RTS lockFile finds no entry in this fresh process; handleIsAt/handleIsSingleLink pass; `hTryLock h ExclusiveLock` -> LockFileEx fails with ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION -> False -> `pure Nothing` -> Exec.hs:176 `Left "另一个 pm 实例正持有该 root 的锁（I10），稍后重试"`, exit 2. Same for writeSideCache (Config.hs:696-709 -> CacheLockBusy), Doctor.hs:103-108 (I10 Bad, diagnose-only), Apply.hs:241, Commands.hs:322, Cli.hs:285, VaultCmd.hs:75 (code 4 -> ServeVault.hs:195 409). The trace diverges from the finder at the very first step (the open does not fail), so none of the claimed crashes/500s occur. DESIGN: docs/DESIGN.md:102 and :435-449 describe exactly this outcome (hTryLock kernel lock; lock busy = CacheLockBusy / diagnose-only / exit 2), and the code delivers it cross-process. The only inaccuracy is the comment at Config.hs:636-639 which calls the RTS same-process 'second writable open -> resource busy' layer a cross-process kernel lock; that is a comment nit, not a behavioural defect. REVIEW-LOG-1B.md:174 registers 'cross-process lock only represented by same-process threads' as a testing residual, which is honest but does not indicate a real failure. Not a bug.
verdict.corrected_summary: Not a defect. Under GHC 9.10.3 (the version the project pins and that is installed here), `__hscore_open` in ghc-internal's HsBase.h opens every mode with `_SH_DENYNO` (FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE), not `_SH_DENYRW`, so a second pm process CAN open `.pm\lock` in ReadWriteMode; contention is then detected by the explicit `hTryLock` (LockFileEx, FAIL_IMMEDIATELY) which returns False and makes withRootLock/withConfigLock return Nothing — exactly the documented 'lock busy' downgrade (exit 2 / CacheLockBusy / doctor diagnose-only / API 409). The `isAlreadyInUseError` branch only covers the same-process RTS lockFile case, which is also handled. The only inaccuracy is the comment at Config.hs:636-639, which attributes the same-process 'second writable open -> resource busy' RTS behaviour to a cross-process kernel lock.
verdict.suggested_fix: None required. Optionally reword the comment at src/Pm/Config.hs:636-639 to say the ResourceBusy branch covers the same-process RTS handle-lock case while cross-process contention is caught by hTryLock (LockFileEx), and optionally add a real two-process test (spawn a second pm.exe that holds the lock) to close the REVIEW-LOG-1B residual.

refuted.title: scanRootRetry's 'clean' predicate counts deterministic walk skips (reparse point, path too long) as transient errors, causing up to dwAttempts pointless full rescans of the backup drive with a misleading 瞬断 message
refuted.summary: Scan.hs mixes deterministic skip rows into the same `srErrors` list as transient failures. scanRootRetry decides `clean res = null (srErrors res) && srCarried res == 0`; when the drive is present it prints `⚠ 扫描 读写出错…按瞬断处理，5 s 后重试`, sleeps, and rescans with the same result, up to dwAttempts times.
refuted.failure_scenario: Backup root path is longer than the main root; one deep RAW path that is 236 chars on D: is ≥240 on E:, so listTreeCov reports `path too long` on every backup scan (or a reparse point sits under the backup root). Each `pm backup` loops: scan → "按瞬断处理，5 s 后重试" ×5 → scan, several extra minutes on an HDD, and still reports `1 个备份盘条目读取出错`.
refuted.evidence: Scan.hs:132, :149, :356 `srErrors = walkErrs <> statErrs <> hashErrs`; Removable.hs:212-218 `clean res = null (srErrors res) && srCarried res == 0`; Removable.hs:138-141 Hiccup branch. BackupCmd.hs:226.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: the mechanics are as described. Scan.hs listTreeCov puts the two deterministic skip rows into the walk error list (`pure ([], [(relPath, "path too long (>=240 chars)")], [])` and `pure ([], [(relPath, reparseSkipNote)], [])`), scanRoot folds them into `srErrors = walkErrs <> statErrs <> hashErrs`, and Removable.hs:212-218 has `clean res = null (srErrors res) && srCarried res == 0`; with the drive present (`driveOk` True) the Right branch calls `recover ... Hiccup` which prints `⚠ 扫描 读写出错（N 处读错、0 条落在未枚举子树）；盘仍在，按瞬断处理，5 s 后重试`, sleeps `min 5 cooldown` = 5 s and rescans with `Just (srCatalog res)` as the old snapshot, at most `dwAttempts` = 5 times (driveWaitSecs). The rescan does not re-hash (statHitStable reuse), so each extra pass is a walk + stat pass; on the real 4611-file drive the whole scan path measured 9 s (REVIEW-LOG.md:601), i.e. roughly 5×(5 s + ~9 s) ≈ 70 s extra, not "several minutes". The final verdict is still honest: backupVerdict reports `N 个备份盘条目读取出错` and exit code 1. REPRO: a junction under the backup root → every pass yields one reparseSkipNote row → 5 × (message + 5 s + rescan) → honest incomplete verdict. That is the behaviour the finder describes, so the trace reaches it. DESIGN: this exact policy is pinned and documented as intended. test/RemovableTests.hs caseScanRetry ② puts a *persistent, deterministic* read error (withDenyAll ACL denial, drive present) in front of scanRootRetry and asserts `length (filter ("盘仍在" `isInfixOf`) ls) @?= 3` and `length (srErrors r2) @?= 1` — i.e. bounded retries with the 瞬断 message followed by an honest error report is the designed outcome for a non-transient error. REVIEW-LOG.md:599 spells it out ("ACL 拒读一文件（盘在）→ 有界 3 次「盘仍在」后如实 1 处读错") and its residual register accepts the cost ("Hiccup 对主库 root 同样生效但只多花 ≤ 25 s"); REVIEW-LOG.md:597 states the rule the module mirrors from backup_verify.py: "任何读错先当瞬断重试 --attempts 次再记读错"; DESIGN.md:379-381 / DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:306-307 say "一遍有读错/未枚举就等盘、拿这一遍的 catalog 当旧快照重扫"; and the comment at Removable.hs:195-198 says the function only reduces *false* incompleteness and the caller still judges by srErrors. A reparse-point or path-too-long row is just another persistent error under this pinned policy. The only cost is a bounded ~70 s and a message whose wording ("按瞬断处理") is the documented, tested wording; the user is not led to a wrong action because the final report lists the real error.
