Realism is also weak: pm never creates junctions on a backup mirror, and a path that is too long only on the backup side cannot have been written there by pm (the same 240 guard is applied on landing).
verdict.corrected_summary: scanRootRetry does retry (up to 5 × 5 s + a reuse-only rescan) when the backup scan's only errors are deterministic skip rows such as `symlink/reparse point skipped` or `path too long`, printing the 瞬断 message each time before honestly reporting the error. This is the pinned design (RemovableTests caseScanRetry ② asserts exactly this for a persistent ACL error; REVIEW-LOG 597/599, DESIGN §6.4): any read error is first treated as a hiccup for a bounded number of attempts, then reported as-is. Not a defect; at most a minor optimisation opportunity.
verdict.suggested_fix: none required. Optional polish: exclude the two literal design-skip rows (reparseSkipNote and the path-too-long note) from the `clean` predicate in scanRootRetry so they do not trigger retries — but that changes a behaviour the tests and docs currently pin, so it would need a doc/test update.

refuted.title: execPlanRetry ignores readJournal's error list: an unreadable journal is settled as empty and landed renames are re-run and reported CONFLICT
refuted.summary: Between sessions execPlanRetry settles interrupted groups via `lastDone . fst <$> withDriveRetry dw root "读 journal" (readJournal root)`. readJournal never throws — it folds every failure into the warnings component — so the wrapper is dead and the warnings are discarded; `done` becomes empty. Groups whose completion is only knowable from the journal are re-executed; for landed Rename items the kernel returns OConflict "重命名源不存在".
refuted.failure_scenario: Backup drive hiccups during a plan with a rename group: rename lands, Done appended, then the next copy throws. recover → heal → readJournal: an AV holds journal.ndjson without FILE_SHARE_READ for a moment → `([], ["…无法可信读取…"])` → done = empty → settle → whole group re-run → execRename' → OConflict "重命名源不存在" for a rename that is on disk exactly as planned; the warning is never shown.
refuted.evidence: src/Pm/Removable.hs:257; :287-295 byJournal; :260. src/Pm/Journal.hs:110-126 `Left m -> pure ([], [m])`. src/Pm/Config.hs readPmState (:407-421). src/Pm/Exec.hs:591-597.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: the dead-wrapper observation is correct. Journal.hs readJournal returns `([], [m])` for a trust-gate failure (:115) and readJournal' returns `([], [m])` for a readPmState Left (:125); Config.hs readPmState wraps the open/read in `try` (:439) and converts every IOException except ENOENT into `Left "… 无法可信读取 …"` (:442-446), so `withDriveRetry dw root "读 journal" (readJournal root)` at Removable.hs:257 can never see an exception, and `fst` discards the warning. But the failure scenario does not reach the claimed outcome. (a) Rename items are never grouped with a Copy: the only plan-level OpRename is built in Names.hs:299 with `piGroup = Nothing`; Album.hs:167 and Apply.hs:315 group only Copy/Quarantine items; Exec.hs:312 restoreOp is an internal rollback, not a plan item. Exec.hs:241 calls `eeProgress env it out` right after each item, so in the finder's scenario ('rename lands, Done appended, then the next copy throws') the rename is its own group with a `Just (it', ODone …)` entry in `seen`; settleGroup takes the `byProgress` branch (Removable.hs:283) and never consults `done`. It is not re-run. (b) The journal is only decisive for a Done-lost rename (R2: exception between moveBoundNoReplace and `jAppend j Barrier (JDone …)` at Exec.hs:632-637). Trace: session 1 throws there → recover waits for the drive + 30 s cooldown → heal = runDoctorWith (under its own withDriveRetry, Doctor.hs:91) reads the journal, appends the R2 Done, requireDrive passes → readJournal. For readJournal to yield `([], [m])` now, the same file that doctor just read and appended milliseconds earlier must become unreadable: either the drive drops again in that gap, or an external process holds it with a deny-read share (GHC's ReadMode open uses _SH_DENYNO; Defender opens files share-all, and the code base's known sharing-violation problem is on DELETE, Win.hs:631, not read). If the drive dropped, `done` is empty and the group is left in `todo'`, but the very next `execPlan` opens `.pm/lock` / the journal on the absent drive and throws → `judgeIO` → `driveOk` False → Dropped → recover waits → heal → readJournal now succeeds → `byJournal` finds the repair's JDone as the last event → `ODone Nothing Nothing Nothing`, the correct result, at the cost of one attempt. The OConflict "重命名源不存在" (Exec.hs:596) is reached only if the drive drops after doctor's append and is back before the next execPlan's first open, i.e. a drop-and-remount inside a millisecond window, whereas the recorded minimum remount time is 2 s. DESIGN: REVIEW-LOG.md:599 documents the intent that `withDriveRetry` wraps the journal read, so there is a genuine mismatch between intent and effect (the wrapper is inert and the warning is swallowed), but no realistic input produces a wrong outcome; the task rules say to refute anything needing a millisecond-scale race and to default to refuted when uncertain.
verdict.corrected_summary: In execPlanRetry the `withDriveRetry … (readJournal root)` wrapper is inert because readJournal folds every read failure into its warnings list (Journal.hs:115/125, Config.hs:439-446) and `fst` drops that list, so a failed journal read is silently settled as 'no Done entries'. However no realistic wrong outcome follows: renames are always singleton groups settled from eeProgress when their Done was appended; the journal-only case (Done lost, repaired by doctor) requires the journal to become unreadable in the milliseconds after doctor just read and appended it, and if that is caused by a second drive drop the next execPlan fails on the absent drive and the following heal/readJournal round settles the item correctly. Reaching OConflict "重命名源不存在" needs a drop-and-remount inside a millisecond window. Cosmetic/robustness gap, not a demonstrable defect.
verdict.suggested_fix: Make the wrapper meaningful and stop swallowing the warning: inside the withDriveRetry action call readJournal, and when it returns no entries together with a warning (the `([], [m])` shape from the trust gate / readPmState Left), `throwIO` an IOException carrying m so judgeIO can classify it; otherwise print any warnings through dwSay before using the entries. Do not throw on torn-tail warnings (those are expected after power loss and arrive with entries).

refuted.title: lastVerified is stamped after hashing finishes, so the racy-mtime guard can trust a torn hash on coarse-timestamp volumes
refuted.summary: statHitStable reuses a (size, mtime)-equal entry when `lastVerified − mtime > 2 s`, on the premise that the hash was taken after the file's timestamp tick had closed. hashOne records `enLastVerified = Just vnow` where vnow is read AFTER sha256File returns. If hashing takes longer than the slack, a same-size write inside the same tick yields a torn sha with lastVerified > mtime + 2 s, reused permanently.
refuted.failure_scenario: Root on FAT32/exFAT. Another process rewrites file F in place (same size) starting at tick M; pm stats (size, M); pm hashes F for 6 s while remaining writes land within the same tick; post-stat equal → entry stored with sha(torn) and lastVerified = M+6 s. Next scan: statHitStable = True → torn sha reused forever.
refuted.evidence: src/Pm/Scan.hs:319-334: `sha <- sha256File abs'; post <- statSnap abs'; if post /= preSnap then Left rel else do vnow <- getCurrentTime; … enLastVerified = Just vnow`. src/Pm/Hash.hs:193-198 racySlackNs = 2 s (180-183). `statNow` (Scan.hs:264) exists but is not stored.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: Scan.hs:317-334 confirms the mechanics: preSnap comes from the stat pass (Scan.hs:265-267, possibly minutes before hashing), `sha <- sha256File abs'`, `post <- statSnap abs'`, `if post /= preSnap then Left rel` (volatile), else `vnow <- getCurrentTime` AFTER hashing and `enLastVerified = Just vnow`. Hash.hs:193-198 statHitStable trusts when `utcToNs v - mtimeNs > racySlackNs` (2 s). So a torn sha survives only if: the volume has coarse timestamps (FAT/exFAT 2 s; on NTFS a write after the pre-stat changes the 100 ns mtime and post /= pre catches it), the writer's last write lands in the SAME 2 s tick as the mtime pm pre-stat'ed, that write hits a region pm has already read during this hash, and the file is never written again (any later write moves mtime and forces a re-hash). Because pm reads sequentially, a sequential writer that finishes within the tick cannot be overtaken unless pm started reading it in that same ≤2 s window; the hole needs a non-sequential in-place writer (e.g. write body then patch header) with its two writes ≥ pm's read lead apart yet inside one 2 s tick, during which pm's hash of that very file is in flight. REPRO trace of the finder's scenario diverges: with the writer active for 6 s the post-stat mtime advances to a later tick (M+4/M+6) → `post /= preSnap` → Left rel → volatile, not indexed (DESIGN §6.7:437 '双 stat，不一致 → 标 volatile 本轮不入索引'). The only surviving variant is the sub-2-second benign race described above. DESIGN: §14 risk table row 'Lightroom / 用户并发改文件' names the triple defence (Plan 前提复核 + 双 stat + 落位 no-replace) and REVIEW-LOG-1B.md:366-371 records the ruling that a stale/torn catalog sha 'fails loudly at apply' (Exec re-hashes existing dst and compares write-hash vs re-read hash against opSha) so the worst case is a silent non-move/misgrouping, never a wrong write; the main library is NTFS (REVIEW-LOG.md 1.1.2 '主库是内置 NVMe'), coarse-tick volumes are backup drives and cards that are not concurrently edited. This is a sub-second benign race on a coarse-timestamp volume with bounded consequences, which the verifier rules fall on the 'refute' side of. The observation that recording the pre-hash time would be strictly safer is valid as hardening, not a defect.
verdict.corrected_summary: Not a defect within the design's threat model: lastVerified is stamped after hashing, so the racy guard can only trust a torn sha when a coarse-timestamp (FAT/exFAT) volume, a non-sequential in-place writer whose last write lands inside the same 2 s tick as the pre-stat mtime, and pm's read of that region all coincide, with no later write to the file. On NTFS the post-stat catches any write after the pre-stat; a stale sha is anyway re-verified at apply (REVIEW-LOG-1B:369). Sub-second benign race with bounded (non-write) consequences.
verdict.suggested_fix: Optional hardening: take `t0 <- getCurrentTime` before `sha256File` in hashOne (or use `statNow`) and store that as enLastVerified, so the stability check compares the hash START to mtime; cost is at most one extra re-hash of files modified within 2 s of the scan.

refuted.title: POST /api/backup-init reports every failure as 400 '登记失败', including config-lock-busy and the partial-success case where the backup root marker was already created
refuted.summary: `backupInitRun` returns `Left` both for validation problems and for post-create failures: after `createRootInfo` succeeds, `register` can fail with '另一个 pm 正在改配置…' and the marker stays on the drive. The endpoint maps all of these to 400, whereas `POST /api/config` answers 409 for the same lock-busy condition.
refuted.failure_scenario: User clicks 登记这块盘 while a terminal `pm config set` holds config.toml.lock. createRootInfo writes `.pm/root-id.json` on the drive → register → withConfigLock Nothing → Left → 400 '登记失败' + details. The GUI shows '登记失败：…'; a simple retry would succeed (BiReused path).
refuted.evidence: src/Pm/Serve.hs:358-366 `Left m -> jsonR status400 [] (object ["error" .= "登记失败", "details" .= [m]])`. src/Pm/BackupCmd.hs:125-130, :163 `fromMaybe (Left "另一个 pm 正在改配置（配置锁被占），备份盘没登记进配置") m`. Contrast Serve.hs:281 409.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/BackupCmd.hs:107-131 backupInitRun returns `Left` for preflight, role/corrupt/untrusted marker, createRootInfo failure and for `register` failures; register (BackupCmd.hs:145-175) returns `Left "另一个 pm 正在改配置（配置锁被占），备份盘没登记进配置"` when withConfigLock yields Nothing. Serve.hs:358-361 maps every Left to `400 {"error":"登记失败","details":[m]}`. The CLI does exactly the same collapse (`runBackupInit` BackupCmd.hs:178-181: every Left → print + exit 2). REPRO: GUI 登记 while a terminal holds config.toml.lock → createRootInfo writes `.pm/root-id.json` → register → Nothing → Left lock message → 400 → gui/ui/app.js:492 shows「登记失败：登记失败\n另一个 pm 正在改配置（配置锁被占），备份盘没登记进配置」. The user sees the real cause and retries; the retry takes the RootPresent/RoleBackup branch (BackupCmd.hs:113-116) and registers via BiReused. The GUI never branches on the numeric status (app.js:492 only prints j.error/j.details), so 400 vs 409 changes nothing observable except the number. DESIGN: the partial state is explicitly documented as intended and idempotent in the code comment BackupCmd.hs:140-143 ('建标识在前、登记在后：登记这一步失败时盘上已有备份 root 标识，重跑走 BiReused 分支沿用它，因此这条路径是幂等的') and the 24th-round note that the write failure must be reported (it is). DESIGN-GUI.md and DESIGN-COMMANDS.md do not specify a 409 for backup-init; the 409 at Serve.hs:281 is a separate endpoint's contract. The message is accurate and leads the user to the right action, so this is a status-code taxonomy nit, not a misleading-error or partial-success bug.
verdict.corrected_summary: Not a bug: `POST /api/backup-init` answers 400 for every `backupInitRun` Left, including config-lock-busy, but the body carries the exact reason (「另一个 pm 正在改配置（配置锁被占）…」), the GUI renders `details` verbatim and never branches on the status code, and the marker-created-but-not-registered state is documented in BackupCmd.hs as intentionally idempotent (retry → BiReused). Only the numeric status differs from /api/config's 409.
verdict.suggested_fix: none (optionally map the lock-busy Left to 409 by giving `backupInitRun` a distinguishable constructor, purely cosmetic)

refuted.title: Manifest torn tail after power loss (§6.3 step 1) becomes a permanent TRASH-MANIFEST Bad (doctor exit 1) with no repair path, contradicting DESIGN §6.4 '撕裂尾不是损坏' and unlike the journal's Warn
refuted.summary: The journal and the trash manifest share the same append port (`withPmStateAppend'` seals a half-written last line with `\n`), but only the journal writes a `torn-gap` marker and only `readJournal'` classifies a sealed torn line as a Warn. `readManifest'` reports any unparsable line as a "manifest line N" warning and `runDoctor'` turns every such warning into `Finding "TRASH-MANIFEST" Bad`; `pm trash list` prints `✗ manifest 损坏行`. Because the manifest is append-only and --repair never touches it, the Bad row persists forever after a single benign power loss.
refuted.failure_scenario: `pm apply` executes a quarantine item; power is lost during `appendManifest`. On restart the manifest's last line is half a JSON object. Next quarantine calls `withPmStateAppend'` which appends `\n` and the new record. `readManifest'` now yields one permanent `Left "manifest line N: Error in $: ..."`. Every subsequent `pm doctor` emits `✗ [TRASH-MANIFEST] …` Bad → exit 1 forever; `pm trash list` prints `✗ manifest 损坏行` each time. The same physical event on the journal yields `⚠ [TORN] … expected after power loss`. `--repair` has no closure for it, so the library's doctor status can never return to 0 without manual editing of `.pm/trash/manifest.ndjson`. || Nothing moved (Intent not yet written), so this is exactly the 'expected after power loss' state; the user is told the manifest is corrupt and has no pm-provided way to clear it.
refuted.evidence: Trash.hs:150-158 `ls = filter (not . BS.null) (BSC.lines raw); step i l = case eitherDecodeStrict l of … Left e -> Left ("manifest line " <> show i <> ": " <> e)` — no torn/last-line distinction. Doctor.hs:175-183 `[Finding "TRASH-MANIFEST" Bad w "" | w <- tvWarnings tv]`; Doctor.hs:248-249/260-261 `code = if worst >= Warn then 1 else 0`. Contrast Journal.hs:135-141/268-274 torn tail → Warn (Doctor.hs:121-122 `take 4 w == "torn"`). Config.hs:465-481 `withPmStateAppend'` seals with `BS.singleton 10` only; Journal.hs:91-94/224-227 marker only for the journal; Trash.appendManifest (Trash.hs:117-119) writes no marker. Doctor.hs:640-650 repair closures. Commands.hs:294/339 `putStrLn ("✗ manifest 损坏行: " <> w)`. DESIGN.md:400 / §6.4 '撕裂尾（掉电写了半行）不是损坏… 隔离区 manifest 走同一追加口（同样先封尾，不写标记）'. test/SweepTests.hs:176-181 pins only the bad-line count.

verdict.reasoning:
CODE: The mechanics the finder describes are accurate. `withPmStateAppend'` (src/Pm/Config.hs:465-475) seals a non-newline tail with `BS.hPut h (BS.singleton 10)` and passes `torn` to the callback; only `withJournal` (src/Pm/Journal.hs:88-95) uses that flag to write a `JTornGap` marker, while `appendManifest` (src/Pm/Trash.hs:117-119) calls the flag-less `withPmStateAppend` and writes no marker. `readManifest'` (Trash.hs:150-158) maps every unparsable line to `Left ("manifest line " <> show i <> ": " <> e)` with no last-line/sealed distinction, `runDoctor'` maps `tvWarnings` to `Finding "TRASH-MANIFEST" Bad` (src/Pm/Doctor.hs:182), the exit code is `if worst >= Warn then 1 else 0` (Doctor.hs:249), and `applyRepairs` (Doctor.hs:673-698) only appends Done for C2/R2/Q-DONE-LOST, generates C5 plans, and unlinks pm-owned tmp/derived files; nothing rewrites the append-only manifest. `pm trash list`/`empty` print `✗ manifest 损坏行: …` (src/Pm/Commands.hs:294, 339) but still list/empty normally (list returns 0; empty proceeds on the parseable records only). `manifestWarns` feeds only `findings0` (Doctor.hs:232-233); it does not gate I7 or any repair.

REPRO (traced, reaches the finder's outcome): §6.3 step 1 — `Exec.hs:685` `appendManifest` hPut+FlushFileBuffers; power lost mid-write leaves `.pm/trash/manifest.ndjson` ending in `{"victim":"half`. Next quarantine → `withPmStateAppend'` sees the non-`\n` tail, writes `\n`, then the new record. `readManifest'`: `BSC.lines` → line N = `{"victim":"half` → `eitherDecodeStrict` Left → warning `manifest line N: …`. `trashView` → `tvWarnings = [w]` → Doctor `Finding "TRASH-MANIFEST" Bad` → `worst = Bad` → exit 1 on every subsequent `pm doctor`; `--repair` has no closure that touches the manifest. Same event on the journal → `torn tail at line N (sealed by a later append…)` Warn (Journal.hs:137-141, Doctor.hs:121-122). So the asymmetry is real.

DESIGN / TESTS: This asymmetry is explicitly documented and pinned. docs/DESIGN.md:400-401 (the very §6.4 paragraph the finder cites) says: `隔离区 manifest 走同一追加口（同样先封尾，不写标记）` — the manifest deliberately gets NO torn-gap marker, and the preceding sentence ties the Warn classification to the marker (`journal 另落一条 {…,"e":"torn-gap"} … 读侧据此报 Warn`). DESIGN.md:96 (I4) repeats it: seal-first for both files, `journal 另落一条 torn-gap 标记`. test/SweepTests.hs:167-181 (`caseTornTailThenAppend`) pins exactly this behaviour with the comment `manifest：半截记录之后追加，新记录完整可读、残行单独计一条损坏行` and asserts `length bad @?= 1` — i.e. the torn remnant is intended to be counted as a 损坏行. docs/REVIEW-LOG-4.md:320-321 records the F028 ruling with scope `新记录不黏进残行；残行仍报 torn（Warn）而非 CORRUPT；manifest 同口同修` (the manifest half of the fix is the no-glue seal only), and REVIEW-LOG-4.md:290 lists `journal 撕裂尾 Warn 残余（既有注释登记）` under 接受不修. Per the rules (documented + test-pinned with docs agreeing with the test) this is refuted. The residual is a rare, fail-closed cosmetic: the window is a single ~200-byte hPut+flush before any Intent is written (nothing moved), a bad manifest line never causes an unlink (fail-closed by design, Trash.hs:147-149), trash list/empty still work, and the only cost is a persistent doctor Bad row / exit 1 that the docs do not promise to clear.
verdict.corrected_summary: Not a bug under the documented contract. A power loss mid-`appendManifest` (§6.3 step 1) does leave a permanently unparsable manifest line that `readManifest'` reports as `manifest line N: …`, `pm doctor` shows as `TRASH-MANIFEST` Bad (exit 1) and `pm trash list/empty` print as `✗ manifest 损坏行`, with no `--repair` path — but DESIGN.md §6.4 (lines 400-401) and I4 (line 96) explicitly state the manifest goes through the same seal-first append port **without** writing a torn-gap marker, test/SweepTests.hs:167-181 pins that the remnant counts as one 损坏行, and REVIEW-LOG-4 F028 (lines 320-321, 290) rules the fix scope as no-glue only. Direction is fail-closed (a bad line can never cause an unlink; trash list/empty still operate on the parseable records; I7/repairs are not gated). Residual is a rare persistent diagnostic row, not wrong behaviour.
verdict.suggested_fix: None required. If the persistent Bad row is deemed undesirable: (a) minimal — in `readManifest'` treat an unparsable *final* line as a `torn`-prefixed warning and in `runDoctor'` map `take 4 w == "torn"` manifest warnings to Warn (mirrors `readJournal'`'s `null rest` branch), which covers the un-sealed state only; (b) full parity — make `appendManifest` use `withPmStateAppend'` and, when `torn`, write a manifest marker record (e.g. `{"e":"torn-gap","at":…}`), and have `readManifest'` classify `unparsable line + following marker` as a torn Warn; update DESIGN.md:400-401 (`不写标记`) and SweepTests.hs:181 (`length bad @?= 1`) accordingly.

refuted.title: `pm vault status --json` prints its ERROR text to stdout, not stderr as the legacy contract specifies
refuted.summary: The legacy spec says the exit-2 conditions write `ERROR: source/vault missing: …` to stderr, keeping stdout pure for `--json` consumers; `runVaultStatus` uses `putStrLn` for every `Left (msg, code)`, so in `--json` mode a non-JSON line lands on stdout.
refuted.failure_scenario: Vault path points to an unplugged directory. `pm vault status --json | python -c 'import json,sys; json.load(sys.stdin)'` → stdout contains `ERROR: vault missing: D:\vault\摄影作品` → JSONDecodeError.
refuted.evidence: src/Pm/Vault.hs:414-418 `Left (msg, code) -> putStrLn msg >> pure code`; strings built at :266-267; docs/specs/sync-photos-legacy-spec.md:63 and §3.1. Same pattern in runVaultPush :569.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Vault.hs:414-417 `runVaultStatus asJson cfg = do er <- computeVault asJson cfg; case er of Left (msg, code) -> putStrLn msg >> pure code`, and the exit-2 strings are built at :266-267. So yes, in `--json` mode an `ERROR: vault missing: …` line lands on stdout. However this is the project-wide CLI convention, not a deviation: the only stderr writer in src/ is Scan.hs:362 (progress), and the sibling `pm vault notes --json` does exactly the same `Left (msg, code) -> putStrLn msg >> pure code` at src/Pm/VaultCmd.hs:332; Commands.hs:91/292/334 likewise. The `quiet` flag on computeVault ("--json 输出面要纯净", :270) exists to keep stdout clean when JSON IS emitted (exit 0/1); on exit 2 no JSON is emitted on any stream. REPRO: vault dir unplugged → `pm vault status --json` → stdout `ERROR: vault missing: D:\vault\摄影作品`, exit 2, no JSON. A consumer that pipes stdout into json.load without checking the exit code fails with JSONDecodeError — but it would fail identically (empty stdout) if the line went to stderr, so the stream choice changes no outcome; a consumer that checks exit 2 first is unaffected either way. DESIGN: docs/specs/sync-photos-legacy-spec.md:63 does record that the legacy script wrote these to stderr, but §6 "保留 vs 修复" of the same spec lists what pm preserves as contract (六态语义, DUPLICATE 不进退出码, JSON 键名/键序/值形状, status 只读, 拓扑) and the error-message stream is not in that list; DESIGN-COMMANDS §10.1 (:329-331) says only "退出码 0/1/2 同". No test pins either stream. With no documented stream contract, no consumer in the repo (GUI uses the HTTP API), and no reachable wrong outcome, this is at most a cosmetic convention difference.
verdict.corrected_summary: `pm vault status --json` prints exit-2 error text on stdout like every other pm CLI message (project-wide convention; VaultCmd.hs:332 `--json` path is identical). The legacy spec notes the old script used stderr, but the stream is not part of the preserved contract (spec §6, DESIGN-COMMANDS §10.1 only preserves exit codes), no JSON is emitted on exit 2 anyway, and a consumer must branch on the exit code regardless. Not a defect.
verdict.suggested_fix: none (optional polish: `hPutStrLn stderr msg` when `asJson` at Vault.hs:417, mirrored at VaultCmd.hs:332 for consistency)

refuted.title: readPmRecords reports a benign in-flight overwrite (delete→rename window) as crash residue and hard-fails
refuted.summary: `writeJsonReplacing` does: create tmp → delete old file → rename tmp→file. A concurrent lock-free reader (`computeVault` → `readHolds`, used by `pm vault status`, `GET /api/vault/status|new|notes`, runVaultNotes, validateIngest, afterApply) that observes the main file missing and then sees the tmp present returns `Left "… 缺失，但残留 …tmp（覆盖写中途崩溃）——拒绝…"`. refuted.evidence: src/Pm/VaultHold.hs:118-137 `Right Nothing -> do t <- readPmState root tmpName; case t of … Right Nothing -> re-read … Right (Just _) -> pure . Left $ (… " 缺失，但残留 " <> tmpName <> "（覆盖写中途崩溃）…")`. src/Pm/Config.hs:733-741 writeJsonReplacing `old <- doesFileExist fp; when old (deleteBoundAt fp); moveBoundNoReplace tmp fp`.
